docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 solves a normal system for the spline coefficients. On a 96-channel input with seeded Gaussian samples, the fitted residuals differed from an independent B-spline least-squares calculation by RMS 0.0557 with 47 pieces and 0.5401 with 93 pieces. Casa-rs solves the design matrix with an SVD. Its fitted residuals agreed with the independent calculation within RMS (2.2\times10^{-8}) on both inputs.

docs.title: Single-dish automatic line masks can access invalid channels in CASA
docs.text: CASA's line finder can call its median helper with zero searchable bins. Its wing extension can also decrement an unsigned index at channel zero. Casa-rs stops an averaging level when it has fewer than two eligible bins and stops the wing at the start of the spectrum.

docs.title: Single-dish line fitting can exceed its time bin on descending rows
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 iterates fit_line by data description and the uncombined scan, state, and field keys. SDMSManager::setIterationApproach omits TIME from this sort. The averaging iterator compares later time stamps with its first buffer's time. With physical rows at 6, 4, 2, and 0 seconds and timebin='1s', timespan='scan', CASA combines the four spectra per hand into one. The same input in chronological order produces four spectra per hand. casa-rs sorts the integrations by time inside each grouping key so the requested interval holds for either row order. The paired oracle verifies both CASA results and the native chronological grouping.

docs.title: Single-dish polarization averaging can abort for one selected hand
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, PolAverageTVI::configurePolAverage obtains its two hand indices from the full POLARIZATION table setup. With an XX/YY MS and sdfit(pol='YY', polaverage='geometric', nfit=[1]), CASA uses the original pair to slice an array with just one selected hand and aborts with ArrayBase::operator()(b,e,i) - incorrectly specified. casa-rs resolves the two hands after correlation selection. When there is no complete pair it uses the selected spectrum unchanged, as the iterator's own skip message describes. The value agrees with fitting the same selected hand without averaging.

docs.title: Single-dish line fitting aborts for negative component counts
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 uses std::stoi on the comma-separated list counts and stores them in an unsigned vector. In list mode, nfit=[-1] reaches a negative array shape and aborts outside the task exception handler. casa-rs reports the invalid component count before allocating a fit and keeps the auto-mode interpretation, where the line finder determines component counts.

docs.title: A failed line fit can delete the previous report
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 removes an existing sdfit report at the beginning of an overwrite. If a later selection or fit fails, the older report is lost. casa-rs stages the text report and replaces the existing file after successful processing.

docs.title: Atmospheric correction can remove an unrelated output directory
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 uses recursive directory removal for an existing sdatmcor destination when overwrite=True. A nonempty directory containing unrelated files is deleted before output is written. casa-rs replaces a readable MeasurementSet or an empty placeholder after preparing the new product. It preserves a nonempty directory that contains no MeasurementSet.

docs.title: An empty atmospheric correction window selection raises a record-type error
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 resolves the windows to process separately from the windows to output. With spw='19', outputspw='23' on the upstream total-power fixture, the work list is empty. NumPy infers a floating-point array for the empty list, and the atmcor record conversion rejects processspw before it can write the requested data. casa-rs passes a typed empty list and writes window 23 with its spectra unchanged.

docs.title: Atmospheric correction can index a cropped window from channel zero
docs.text: On X320b_sel2.ms, sdatmcor(spw='19', outputspw='19:370~407^2', scan='7') writes the requested channels. CASA 6.7.6.14 subtracts corrections for original channels 0 through 18 from their data. The paired oracle recovers that exact offset from the uncropped CASA product. casa-rs uses the correction at each selected original channel. Its cropped spectra equal the same channel slice of its full-window correction, including reordered and overlapping ranges.

docs.title: Atmospheric correction can publish unflagged nonfinite spectra
docs.text: With the recorded total-power fixture and CASA 6.7.6.14, a gain table with zero amplitude for window 19 produces an infinite reciprocal-square factor. A scalar factor of 1e40 also exceeds the Float32 range of the corrected spectra. Both inputs write unflagged nonfinite samples. casa-rs rejects either result before publishing the output, preserving an existing product on overwrite.

docs.title: ASAP import writes observation times in days to a seconds column
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 copies the scan table's MJD day range into OBSERVATION.TIME_RANGE, whose unit is seconds. The same import converts the MAIN integration times to seconds. On the upstream ALMA ASAP test fixture, the observation range starts at 56839.91554 and the first integration is 4910968702.656 seconds from MJD zero. casa-rs converts both tables to MJD seconds and preserves the original observation bounds.

docs.title: The single-dish filler can write inconsistent receptor metadata
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 writes two receptor names to FEED.POLARIZATION_TYPE with NUM_RECEPTORS=0. It fills POLARIZATION.CORR_PRODUCT with zero pairs even for YY, LL and cross-hands. The imported spectra themselves are in the order indicated by CORR_TYPE. casa-rs writes the receptor count and maps directly measured linear and circular products to the corresponding ordered pairs. Derived Stokes products retain their placeholders.

docs.title: NOSTAR import writes FEED rows only for the first beam
docs.text: On the upstream Orion KL NOSTAR file, CASA 6.7.6.14 writes MAIN spectra for antenna IDs 0 through 3, but FEED rows only for antenna ID 0. The other three beams reference feeds with no corresponding metadata. casa-rs writes one FEED row for each beam and spectral window referenced by MAIN.

docs.title: NOSTAR import discards the imaginary part of cross-hand spectra
docs.text: In a four-plane NOSTAR integration, the third and fourth planes encode the real and imaginary components of the cross-hands. CASA 6.7.6.14 always writes FLOAT_DATA. A test with the instrument planes [XX=1, YY=2, XY=3, YX=4] produces [1, 3, 3, 2]. casa-rs writes complex DATA with both components in the conjugate products [1, 3+4i, 3-4i, 2].

docs.title: Single-dish averaging can label two time-averaged hands as Stokes I
docs.text: After fit_line(timebin='8s', timespan='scan', polaverage='geometric') CASA 6.7.6.14 uses its time-averaging iterator for subsequent operations on the same attachment. Smoothing, baseline subtraction and atmospheric correction produce both XX and YY samples, but link the output data description to a one-correlation Stokes I setup. casa-rs preserves the XX/YY setup that describes the actual samples.

docs.title: Applying a single-dish baseline can abort after polarization averaging
docs.text: On an XX/YY attachment, CASA 6.7.6.14 can save a one-correlation baseline table after fit_line(polaverage='stokes') or fit_line(polaverage='geometric'). Applying that table on the same attachment terminates the process with a casacore matrix row error. casa-rs applies the model to the projected correlation. The paired oracle reads both saved tables through casacore and applies both in casa-rs.

docs.title: Single-dish polarization averaging can clear a rejected integration's row flag
docs.text: On an XX/YY spectrum with FLAG_ROW=true and clear per-channel FLAG cells, fit_line(polaverage='geometric') followed by atmcor in CASA 6.7.6.14 produces a row with clear flags. casa-rs retains the rejection in the output row and channels. The baseline fitter also excludes that integration from its fit.

docs.title: GSPLINE append overwrites the previous field's fit
docs.text:
In CASA 6.7.6.14, gaincal(gaintype='GSPLINE', field='FLUX') stores the FLUX fit under every FIELD_ID, including unselected fields. Solving field='PHASE', append=True into that table then replaces the fit under each existing FIELD_ID. With disjoint field time ranges, applying the updated table to the original field loses its corrections.

casa-rs publishes rows for selected fields and updates only those fields on append. Added fits can have different knot counts. The stored arrays share a shape so CASA can read them, and each row keeps its actual count. The paired oracle compares the original rows to a saved copy of the initial solve and the new rows to CASA. It then applies the combined table through both implementations.

The direct calibrater.setsolvegainspline and solve workflow uses the same selected-field publication policy. Its paired oracle checks the new field's coefficients against CASA and verifies that append preserves the prior field.

docs.title: GSPLINE fit logs give the RMS for the wrong baseline
docs.text: The gaincal(gaintype='GSPLINE') diagnostic log indexes residuals as if only cross-correlations occupied the array. The solver's storage includes autocorrelation slots. A noisy fit therefore displays a zero RMS for the first baseline, then assigns its residual to a different baseline. casa-rs reports the weighted fit RMS for the stated baseline. The paired oracle recomputes it from the visibility data and saved coefficients.

docs.title: GSPLINE can abort when every channel has a rejected correlation
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 uses common channel flags for the time-spline solve. An XX/YY input with all YY channels flagged therefore has no usable shared samples. CASA can terminate while attempting this fit. Casa-rs returns the insufficient-sampling result without publishing a calibration table.

docs.title: GSPLINE can publish nonfinite phases for a disconnected antenna
docs.text: When all baselines to one antenna are flagged, CASA 6.7.6.14 attempts to fit that antenna along with the connected array. The singular fit can publish nonfinite coefficients, including for antennas that have data. Casa-rs fits the connected array and omits antennas without accepted data. Both legacy readers then flag visibilities with a missing antenna gain. This rule also applies to generic calibrater.setsolve(type='GSPLINE'), which publishes the fitted antennas across every attached field.

docs.title: fringefit can abort with one selected channel per spectral window
docs.text: With combine='spw', CASA 6.7.6.14 can abort if every selected window contributes only one channel. In a test with two windows 48 MHz apart and spw='0:0,1:0', the concatenated FFT tried to address channel zero on an array with a zero-length frequency axis. CASA raised ArrayError and terminated before publishing the table. Casa-rs derives the grid spacing from the separation of the selected frequencies and checks the FFT memory requirement before allocating the grid. Its two-band regression exercises both search modes.

docs.title: accor rejects TaQL selections because the wrapper uses the ANTENNA table name
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 adds ANTENNA==ANTENNA2 when the caller supplies a nonempty msselect. A valid predicate such as ANTENNA1<3 fails because ANTENNA is a subtable. The default task path already uses ANTENNA1==ANTENNA2. Casa-rs intersects the caller's predicate with ANTENNA1==ANTENNA2 in both cases. Its test compares the result to CASA selecting those same antennas through antenna.

docs.title: pccor can fail after creating an empty calibration table
docs.text:
Selecting no spectral windows in CASA 6.7.6.14, for example with spw='!0' on a one-window MeasurementSet, reaches the table constructor before the first attempt to index an empty set of solutions. The task raises IndexError. Casa-rs checks the selected windows before publication and returns the same exception.

CASA can also raise UnboundLocalError when the first selected reference antenna has pulse data only outside the reference interval. Casa-rs reports the missing reference data with a RuntimeError. The paired PCCOR oracle covers both cases and checks destination preservation.

docs.title: appendantab attaches new subtable links to the child tables
docs.text:
CASA 6.7.6.14 creates SYSCAL and GAIN_CURVE under the copied MeasurementSet and writes each keyword on the corresponding child table. The embedded gain-curve consumer reads the GAIN_CURVE link on MAIN. Casa-rs attaches both links on MAIN. The paired oracle compares the subtable contents and gives the CASA reference copy the same MAIN links before checking its independent gencal consumer.

With overwrite=True on a copy that has no gain rows, CASA also indexes the first receptor of an empty sensitivity array and raises IndexError. Casa-rs imports the gain records and publishes the completed copy. Its test compares the output with the default CASA import.

CASA uses the position of an ANTAB gain record as a channel index when overwriting a gain row. This raises IndexError when the second antenna has a gain record for a one-channel window. Casa-rs tests the window's frequency coverage against the gain record's range. The oracle checks both antennas' replaced sensitivities.

CASA assembles Tsys temperatures in spectral-window number order, then writes row identifiers in data-description order. The temperatures can follow the wrong SPW when those orders differ. Casa-rs assembles each row using its stated spectral-window identifier. It also ignores an unknown station's GAIN record while preserving the following GAIN header. CASA can consume that header while skipping to the next slash.

docs.title: Baseline Mueller calibration assumes ordered antennas
docs.text:
CASA 6.7.6.14 computes its M Mueller and Mf Mueller baseline index assuming the first antenna ID is at most the second. For five antennas, (0,3) uses slot 3, while (3,0) uses slot 9, the slot for (2,2). This can select or update the wrong baseline response. Exchanging antennas also conjugates the parallel-hand visibilities. Casa-rs stores the response for the ordered pair and conjugates it when solving or applying a reversed row. The paired BLCAL oracle checks the reversed-input solve and apply against the known sky model.

When cross-hands carry weight and both parallel hands have zero weight, CASA can attempt the interval and publish unflagged NaNs from a zero-weight division. Casa-rs retains the interval and flags the unavailable parallel-hand responses, with the same zero coefficients as other absent solutions. The oracle compares the attempt and checks the output flags.

docs.title: Calibrater reports antenna IDs from the last visibility buffer
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 collects field, observation and scan IDs throughout the calibrater.returndict() visibility iteration. It fetches the antennas after iteration, from the last buffer. With antennas 0 and 1 in the first selected scan and 2 and 3 in the second, the record lists both scans and only antennas 2 and 3. Casa-rs reports the four antennas in the selected rows. The paired calibrater oracle checks both records on the disjoint baselines.

docs.title: Calibrater can reuse inverse Jones terms when corrupting a model
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 applies a constant antenna gain of 1.2 correctly in a fresh calibrater.corrupt(), multiplying the physical model by 1.44. After correct('trial') on the same tool and selection, it divides the model by 1.44 on each corrupt() call. VisCal::corrupt2 requests forward application even in this sequence. Casa-rs evaluates the forward Jones terms on every model corruption. The paired tool oracle checks both sequences against the constant-gain product law. Both engines retain the previous single-term activity counts across the corruption.

docs.title: Calibrater's legacy iterator can crash during a gain solve
docs.text: With CASA 6.7.6.14, setvi(True, True) followed by a selected G Jones solution can terminate Python with a segmentation fault in solve(). The direct solve oracle reproduces the crash with the legacy gain case. The same legacy fixture returns normally when minblperant=99 blocks the fit. Casa-rs completes the fit using its shared solver and checks the resulting table and activity against the successful CASA modern-iterator solve. Legacy return records retain their original layout without solvestats.

docs.title: Direct FRINGE can terminate Python with an empty mask and default windows
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, use the direct FRINGE fixture, set a valid reference antenna, and call setsolve(type='FRINGE') with the default empty paramactive, delaywindow, and ratewindow lists. On unflagged selected data, solve() can terminate Python. The same empty mask with explicit search bounds raises Error in Calibrater::solve.. Casa-rs reports that error for a nonempty gather that requires global refinement with no active parameters. An empty gather still completes and reports zero attempts. #2012

docs.title: Direct specifycal aborts for literal wildcard selectors
docs.text: With CASA 6.7.6.14, call calibrater.specifycal(caltable='gain.cal', caltype='amp', parameter=[1.5], antenna='*') on the direct fixture. CASA passes antenna index -1 into a parameter-array slice and aborts. A literal spw='*' likewise reaches an invalid spectral-window index. Casa-rs broadcasts over the requested wildcard axes and verifies the resulting table against CASA's empty-selector form, which expresses the same prescription. #2015

docs.title: mstransform silently skips requested continuum fitting
docs.text:
CASA 6.7.6.14 mstransform sends the public fitspw argument to its continuum visibility iterator under the key fitspw. UVContSubTVI::parseFitSpec reads fitspec, so the iterator receives no fit windows and copies each visibility unchanged. Reproduce with douvcontsub=True and fitspw="0:1~4" on a dataset with a varying spectrum. The same task with douvcontsub=False writes the same visibility values.

casa-rs fits the requested polynomial on the unflagged line-free channels and writes residuals, or the estimate when want_cont=True. The paired oracle in tools/casa-compat/ms_transform_continuum_oracle.py reproduces the public wrapper bug and independently compares the native result with CASA's compiled fitter after correcting only the configuration key. The native task also discards its staged product when fit selection fails, which allows the caller to correct the selection and retry at the same path.

The compiled denoising fitter has a second defect in GslMultifitLinearBase::calcFitModelCore. It replaces the model vector for each coefficient instead of adding the polynomial terms. That helper evaluates the stored float output and the residuals used to reweight both the real and imaginary data during later iterations. For example, a linear float spectrum with nonzero offset retains the full offset after CASA subtraction. casa-rs evaluates the whole polynomial in both places. The oracle compares those cases with a separate NumPy weighted fit.

When the compiled fitter follows time averaging, its line-channel mask is written through a reference to the averaging iterator's cached visibility flags. It can replace valid flags and change scalar weights and sigmas. The native fit reads the flags and applies the mask only to the fit samples. The oracle takes the averaged flags and noise from CASA's public task, where the misnamed configuration key leaves the mask inactive.

The compiled path can also try to change the shape of an allocated WEIGHT_SPECTRUM cell when the original task selects only part of a spectral window. For the selection case, the oracle applies CASA's channel selection first and fits using the equivalent local channel indices. The native task computes the intersection on the selected grid in one transform.

docs.title: Direct fluxscale can terminate Python with an empty window map
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, use the direct fluxscale fixture, attach the MS, and transfer from FLUX to PHASE with refspwmap=[]. The reference process can terminate with SIGSEGV. Casa-rs treats an empty map as no remapping and compares its returned record, caltable and HISTORY against CASA's default refspwmap=[-1]. #2017

docs.title: Direct opacity solves can terminate Python
docs.text:
CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts calibrater.setsolve for TOpac and TfOpac. With usable data, the first fit in either visibility iterator terminates the process with SIGSEGV and leaves no calibration table. An otherwise equivalent VI2 T solve completes. If every selected sample is flagged, both opacity families return success and preserve the configured solver. They record zero attempted and successful intervals and publish no table.

Casa-rs preserves the setup, state and no-result behavior. When the selected data would reach a fit, it raises a recoverable solve error and clears the equation. The oracle runs the reference fits in child processes. Direct opacity solve oracle

docs.title: An additive polynomial window can keep a degenerate frequency basis
docs.text: With a one-channel selection in each of two combined spectral windows, flagging one window throughout the first scan makes CASA 6.7.6.14 record the remaining channel's frequency as both domain endpoints. A later scan can have usable samples at both frequencies, but the saved basis still has coincident endpoints. Casa-rs derives the domain from both selected frequencies and retains a solvable linear fit in the later scan. Additive Mueller polynomial oracle

docs.title: Generic BPOLY setup can terminate Python
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 can terminate with SIGSEGV during calibrater.setsolve(type='BPOLY') on an attached MeasurementSet in either visibility iterator. Casa-rs raises a recoverable setup error. The dedicated setsolvebandpoly entry point supplies the polynomial controls and supports the legacy fit. Generic polynomial oracle

docs.title: Generic GSPLINE phase wrapping can vary between CASA processes
docs.text: With the same data and generic calibrater.setsolve(type='GSPLINE') arguments, CASA 6.7.6.14 produced different phase coefficients in separate processes. One process was terminated during phase fitting under the local memory limit. The dedicated setsolvegainspline call uses explicit wrapping controls. Casa-rs uses 7,200-second spacing, two phase points, and a zero wrap threshold for the generic path. These controls reproduced the pinned phase coefficients in the dedicated reference and in three isolated generic preaveraged fits. Generic polynomial oracle

docs.title: Competing VI1 callibrary slices can mix antenna gains in one buffer
docs.text:
In CASA 6.7.6.14, calibrater.corrupt() with the old iterator looks up a callibrary buffer with wildcard scan and intent. Competing scan-specific entries for one table can therefore resolve to the earlier selected scan for both scans of a field. On a fixture with two scan-specific mappings and an additional explicitly scoped field, CASA combined unity and calibrated antenna gains within the same scan. This produced distinct baseline factors of 1, 1.2, and 1.44 from a single intended antenna gain of 1.2. Casa-rs selects one slice consistently for both antennas in each legacy buffer. Scan-filtered input, other fields, correction, and modern corruption retain their applicable mappings. Paired calibration-library oracle

The selected slice uses its registered calibration scan even when the current visibility belongs to a different scan. Mixed scan and intent wildcards can also give the CASA ordered index a cyclic comparison. The one-antenna probe with three distinct gains found an insertion-order-dependent result. The native lookup uses one ordered context throughout a buffer. The oracle records the two registration orders where the pinned CASA result differs.

docs.title: Some direct calibration factories gather data without a usable fitting stage
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts generic calibrater.setsolve for J, Jf, A Noise, F Jones, B TSYS, gain curve, and legacy power curve. With all input flagged, the tool reports the expected intervals and does not produce a table. When four-correlation usable data reaches the fitting stage, the pinned legacy J/Jf and both B TSYS iterators terminate. The tested modern J/Jf, A Noise, F Jones and curve configurations return a solve error. Modern power curve returns a setup error. Casa-rs retains the available gather stage and uses a recoverable error for the unavailable fit. These limits concern solving. Existing table application and specification are separate operations. Paired factory oracle

docs.title: Direct KAntPos can abort when a solution combines multiple buffers
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 uses its antenna delay fitter for direct calibrater.setsolve(type='KAntPos'). Both iterators write the two fitted terms in a three-term KAntPos Jones table. The unused third term is zero, valid for the reference antenna and flagged for the others. Two overlapping windows with combine='spw' or two fields with combine='field' terminated in both iterators when the multi-buffer fitter assigned two terms to a three-term array. Casa-rs reports a recoverable error when this fit is reached. Windows separated into single-buffer scan or integration intervals produce tables. Paired antenna-position oracle

docs.title: A Noise baseline indexing assumes ordered antenna columns
docs.text: With eight antennas, both CASA 6.7.6.14 calibrater iterators applied the A Noise coefficients of (0, 7) to a deliberately reversed (1, 0) visibility. Casa-rs uses the coefficients of (0, 1), conjugates them, and exchanges the cross hands to preserve the visibility's orientation. The ordinary ordered-baseline inputs agree with CASA. Paired A Noise oracle

docs.title: Direct EVLASWP can gather data and fail at fitting
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts direct calibrater.setsolve(type='EVLASWP') when the MeasurementSet links readable SYSPOWER and CALDEVICE tables. Both iterators record expected intervals and write no table for fully flagged input. Both terminate on the isolated usable visibility fit. Casa-rs retains the gather stage and returns a recoverable solve error for usable data. Paired switched-power and KMBD oracle

docs.title: Joint KMBD fitting can abort with single-correlation buffers
docs.text: When calibrater combines spectral windows for a KMBD fit, both CASA 6.7.6.14 iterators refuse a mix of single- and dual-hand buffers. Two single-hand buffers instead terminate when the one-hand answer is assigned to the two-hand table array. Casa-rs reports a recoverable solve error in each case. Paired KMBD oracle

docs.title: A calibrater gain matrix can keep its correction direction during corruption
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, a VI2 session that calls correct and then corrupt with the same single-slot gain table can apply the inverse gain to both visibility columns. Casa-rs applies the inverse gain to CORRECTED_DATA and the forward gain to MODEL_DATA. The same planted session with VI1 terminates during its direct amplitude G fit in an isolated CASA process. The native VI1 session completes the fit and both visibility operations. Paired session oracle

docs.title: calanalysis.get can terminate on a restricted feed
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, open one of the two-feed, multi-window tables in the selected-series oracle and call get(feed='1'). On both complex and real tables, the reference process terminates with SIGSEGV after opening the table successfully. Casa-rs filters the selected feed by its table index and verifies that the returned records equal the same feed's series from the unrestricted query.

docs.title: calanalysis.fit can terminate on an empty or singleton fit input
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, use the fit oracle to fit a fully flagged channel with type='ROBUST'. Both AVERAGE and LINEAR terminate when the robust estimator asks for a median of an empty array. With one timestamp and axis='F', a successful AVERAGE fit can also terminate while calculating the variance of one residual. Casa-rs returns the input series with an invalid fit when every sample is flagged and reports zero residual variance for a successful singleton fit.

docs.title: calanalysis.get can invent phase wraps on descending frequencies
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, the group-delay oracle supplies eight descending channels with constant complex gains. Default group-delay unwrapping searches a signed interval away from zero and inserts wraps into a zero-delay solution. Casa-rs searches a symmetric interval using positive spacing between distinct frequencies. It removes the common carrier from the power calculation and refines peaks at the bandwidth scale, preserving the original channel order. The oracle checks ascending and descending zero-delay and planted-delay series, including 1 kHz channels at 100 GHz.

docs.title: calanalysis.fit can overestimate a nearly exact fit's reduced chi-square
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, the fit oracle supplies an almost exact linear series over eight channels near 100 GHz with uncertainty 0.001. CASA reports a reduced chi-square of about 0.0365. Its returned residuals and uncertainties imply about 2.33e-8. The normal-equation calculation subtracts much larger quadratic terms. Casa-rs sums the squared, weighted residuals directly, after the existing flags and uncertainty exclusion, and uses that metric for reduced chi-square and unweighted covariance.

docs.title: Layer absorption queries can terminate Python on an invalid layer
docs.text: With CASA 6.7.6.14, initialize a profile and spectral window, then call getAbsTotalDry(getNumLayers(), 0). The C++ wrapper checks the window and channel but lets the layer's std::out_of_range escape, terminating Python. casa-rs raises RuntimeError for an invalid layer and preserves the tool state. The paired atmosphere oracle isolates the CASA call and checks all nine native layer getters, including a valid query after each error.

docs.title: Intent wildcards can lose literal punctuation
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, give a STATE row the intent OBSERVE+TARGET#ON_SOURCE and use that row in MAIN. msmetadata.fieldsforintent("OBSERVE+*") then returns no fields, although the exact intent and "OBSERVE*" match. The shared wildcard helper uses a replacement that refers to a nonexistent regex capture, dropping characters such as +. casa-rs treats * as the wildcard and matches all other characters literally in field, scan, and spectral-window intent selectors (#1029).

docs.title: MSCAL predicates can crash or hang in applycal
docs.text: On the synthetic MeasurementSet in the applycal oracle, CASA 6.7.6.14 terminates with SIGSEGV when msselect calls mscal.scan("2") or mscal.time(">2019/12/31/21:53:15"). An mscal.uvdist("<40m") predicate returns rows in a direct table query but times out with the MeasurementSet open for applycal. casa-rs evaluates these expressions through the shared scan, time and UV-distance grammars. The oracle uses equivalent ordinary CASA TaQL predicates to compare the calibrated and untouched rows and their flags.

docs.title: A metadata tool borrowed from ms can crash or follow a different attachment
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, a child returned by ms.metadata() can terminate the process when its name() is called. The borrowed constructor initializes the metadata reader without initializing the table pointer used by name(). For example, open the upstream ngc5921_ut.ms, obtain a child with cachesize=0, and call name() on it. The child can also start reading the rows of an unrelated MS after the parent closes and reopens, as seen when reopening a seven-row reference view. casa-rs gives the child the logical name of its original attachment. The same child continues to see selections and reset from that attachment and keeps its last selection after the parent detaches. It also drops cached scan metadata when its selection changes. In CASA, calling scannumbers() before selecting scans 3–5 in ngc5921_ut.ms can keep returning all seven scans even though nrows() reports the selected row count. If the original directory is removed or replaced, casa-rs reports an unavailable attachment on queries that need its data (#1030).

docs.title: Out-of-range TaQL array indices can abort MS selection
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, open an MS with ordinary visibility arrays and pass abs(DATA[999,1]) > 0 as msselect's TaQL predicate. msseltoindex and msselect(onlyparse=True) accept the predicate without reading cells. Applying it can terminate the process with an uncaught array-slicing exception. casa-rs validates the expression without reading visibility cells and reports a failed selection when evaluation reaches an invalid index. The previously selected rows remain accessible (#1030).

docs.title: A Multi-MS metadata count can omit newly published member rows
docs.text: Open a genuine CASA Multi-MS and obtain its metadata with cachesize=0. Append a complete row to the last member and close its writer. CASA 6.7.6.14's child count can stay at the original total and a summary can abort. The casa-rs child counts the published member rows and reports the same total in its summary (#1030).

docs.title: Concatenated FIELD tables can hide their ephemerides
docs.text: Create a Multi-MS with two members carrying FIELD ephemerides and list FIELD among the tables to concatenate. CASA 6.7.6.14 can search a transient, nonexistent table directory for both members' ephemerides. ms.getfielddirmeas() then returns an empty direction and ms.metadata().phasecenter() raises an error. casa-rs finds each ephemeris beside its physical FIELD table. Each combined direction matches CASA's direction for the corresponding member opened on its own (#1030).

docs.title: An unobserved antenna name can return every antenna station
docs.text: With CASA 6.7.6.14, attach a MeasurementSet whose ANTENNA table includes A4 but whose observation 0 uses only A1 through A3. msmetadata.antennastations("A4", obsid=0) and antennastations(["A4"], obsid=0) return every station. The name-selection branch passes its empty intersection to an accessor where an omitted ID list means every station. The numeric selection of the same antenna returns an empty list. casa-rs returns an empty list for both forms because no selected antenna participated in the observation (#1029).

docs.title: Unsupported antenna scalars can silently select unrelated antennas
docs.text: With CASA 6.7.6.14, pass numpy.uint32(1) or numpy.bool_(True) as the selector for msmetadata.antennaids, antennastations, or antennaposition. CASA discards the scalar. It returns all antenna IDs, all stations, or the position of antenna zero, respectively, just as for an omitted selector. casa-rs uses the unsigned antenna ID in the two methods that accept IDs and raises RuntimeError for unsupported selector types. An unsupported value cannot silently widen the selection or return the position of a different antenna (#1029).

docs.title: A cached cross-correlation row count can underflow
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, call msmetadata.summary() and then nrows(autoc=False, flagged=True) on an attached MeasurementSet containing cross-correlations. CASA's cached row-statistics path subtracts the total row count from the autocorrelation count in an unsigned type. For example, a 30-row MeasurementSet with 18 cross-correlations can return a float equal to 2⁶⁴. casa-rs counts the actual MAIN rows whose antenna IDs differ, independently of which metadata method was called first (#1029).

docs.title: MeasurementSet row counts and effective exposure can ignore FLAG_ROW
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, set FLAG_ROW=True on a MAIN cross-correlation row while leaving that row's FLAG array clear. msmetadata.nrows(flagged=False) counts the row and effexposuretime() includes its exposure. Setting the entire FLAG cell instead excludes both. casa-rs treats the row flag as marking all samples in the row bad, as the MeasurementSet defines it. This leaves total row counts and the effective-exposure bandwidth denominator unchanged (#1029).

docs.title: Summarizing an empty MeasurementSet can abort CASA
docs.text: Open a valid zero-row MeasurementSet, for example a disk reference view made with CASA's table.selectrows and an empty integer array. In CASA 6.7.6.14, msmetadata.summary() computes minimum and maximum times on an empty array and aborts the Python process. casa-rs raises RuntimeError because the summary has no beginning or ending timestamp. The tool remains attached and reports zero rows (#1029).

docs.title: Descending channels can produce negative unflagged counts and effective exposure
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 weights usable samples by signed CHAN_WIDTH in msmetadata.nrows(flagged=False) and effexposuretime(). With four 1 MHz channels stored in descending order, negative channel widths, positive TOTAL_BANDWIDTH, and one channel flagged in each correlation, CASA reports −13.5 unflagged cross-correlation rows and −22.5 s on an 18-cross-row fixture. The ascending ordering gives +13.5 rows and +22.5 s. casa-rs uses channel-width magnitudes, so either ordering gives the same positive count and duration (#1029).

docs.title: MS selection can reopen subtables through a retargeted symlink
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, open an MS through a directory symlink. Retarget the symlink to a reference view without a local ANTENNA subdirectory, then call msselect with a baseline present in the original MAIN. CASA tries to open ANTENNA/table.f0 through the new target and returns False. casa-rs keeps the public link name and resolves reads and writes against the MS captured at open, so changing the link cannot redirect an attached operation (#1030).

docs.title: An invalid FIELD direction column can return the north celestial pole
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, call ms.getfielddirmeas("phase") on a valid MS. CASA logs an illegal column name and still returns a J2000 direction with declination π/2. casa-rs logs the bad column and returns the empty boolean array also used for other failed direction queries (#1030).

docs.title: Empty MS selections can fail the spectral-window summary
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, select zero rows from a valid MS with nonempty DATA_DESCRIPTION and SPECTRAL_WINDOW, then call getspectralwindowinfo(). The scalar range returns an empty record and the summary indexes a missing field, raising an internal assertion error. casa-rs returns an empty dictionary because no data descriptions are used (#1030).

docs.title: An MS opened read-only can start writing through another handle
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, open an MS with ms.open(path, nomodify=True) and call hanningsmooth("data"). It initially returns False and asks for nomodify=False. Open and close the same path for update with a second ms or table tool. The first handle now reports iswritable() == True and hanningsmooth("data") writes to MAIN, even after the writer closed. casa-rs retains the requested access mode per handle. A read-only handle continues to report False and refuses writes (#1030).

docs.title: PlotMS can lose its backend on the real axis of FLOAT_DATA
docs.text:
In CASA 6.7.6.14 with casaplotms 2.9.1, select real versus channel on a float-only MeasurementSet using ydatacolumn="float". The headless backend can close its RPC stream during export, producing no file. The cache fills the floating amplitude array. The real axis indexer reads a separate array that the cache leaves empty. The explicit axis validation permits real-valued plots. Pinned cache Pinned indexer

casa-rs reads the real values directly. The regression checks the same selected samples against CASA's successful signed amplitude export, which has the same coordinates for float cells (#1032).

docs.title: Clearcal releases a caller's explicit table lock
docs.text:
In CASA 6.7.6.14, open a writable MeasurementSet with table.open(vis, nomodify=False, lockoptions={'option': 'user'}) and take an explicit write lock with table.lock(write=True). Calling clearcal(vis, addmodel=True) writes the scratch columns. The attached table then reports haslock(write=True) == False even though its owner never released the lock.

CASA also releases automatic locks on unrelated tables open in the same process. casa-rs yields automatic locks on the input MeasurementSet before its clearcal provider starts and keeps the caller's table attached. An explicit or active lock still held by the caller produces a RuntimeError before the task writes. The caller retains ownership of that lock (#1520).

docs.title: PlotMS time averaging can dilute complex visibilities when FLOAT_DATA is present
docs.text:
In CASA 6.7.6.14 with casaplotms 2.9.1, plot two Real ordinates from CORRECTED_DATA and MODEL_DATA against channel on a MeasurementSet that also stores DATA and FLOAT_DATA. With unit visibilities and unit weights, averaging pairs of integrations produces 0.666667 for both ordinates. Adding a two-channel average gives the same values.

The mixed-column transform enables time averaging for the float column. Its accumulator adds observed float weights to the weight spectrum used to normalize the corrected and model columns. casa-rs accumulates weights for the requested complex columns and preserves the constant value 1. The paired fixture checks the selected bins and metadata in both modes (#1032). Pinned transform setup Pinned time averager

docs.title: PlotMS can stall while exporting phase-shifted coordinates to text
docs.text:
In CASA 6.7.6.14 with casaplotms 2.9.1, plot U in metres against observed phase for selected XX channels on a complex MeasurementSet. Enable transform=True and set phasecenter="J2000 00h00m02.00s -29d59m40.00s". The headless task writes the PNG and returns. A text export of the same phase shift can stop after the selection header and fail to return.

casa-rs exports the selected coordinates and flags to text. The paired test compares them with pinned PlotMS on a separate MS written by the CASA phaseshift task. Both CASA paths use the same phase-shifting visibility iterator. The test also compares PNG export using the original MS and active transform in both public PlotMS tasks (#1032). Pinned PlotMS iterator setup Pinned phase-shifting iterator

docs.title: PlotMS SPW averaging can repeat the first window's channel selection
docs.text:
In CASA 6.7.6.14 with casaplotms 2.9.1, select spw="0:0,1:2" with avgspw=True on an MS with two four-channel windows. The second window contributes channel 0 to the average. With SPW averaging disabled, the same selection correctly exports channel 2 from that window.

casa-rs pairs channels by their position within each selected window. The public-task regression checks the original selection against unaveraged CASA data, then moves the selected sample to the common index in a separate CASA input. The aligned CASA average matches the native coordinates. When the selected channel counts differ, CASA can repeat the first count as well. casa-rs reports that the selected shapes cannot be averaged together before writing the export (#1032). Pinned PlotMS reducer

docs.title: PlotMS can terminate on disjoint channel ranges in two averaged windows
docs.text:
With CASA 6.7.6.14 and casaplotms 2.9.1, set spw="0:0~2;5~7,1:0~2;5~7", avgspw=True and avgchannel="2" on an MS with two eight-channel windows. The transform reports a mismatch between the number of widths and the number of windows, then the PlotMS backend terminates. Selecting the disjoint ranges in a single window exports the two physical bins over channels 0–1 and 5–6.

casa-rs runs the same channel transform for both windows and averages their output samples by bin position. The regression checks the shared physical grid against the single-window CASA request and verifies the two-window output against the weighted complex average (#1032).

docs.title: Empty MS visibility strides can abort or change the attachment
docs.text:
On a nonempty MS, getdata(increment=4294967297) can admit a stride using its low 32 bits and select zero rows using the full stride. CASA 6.7.6.14 returns empty visibility and time arrays. flag_sum can report an arbitrary second extent, and requesting u aborts with ArrayConformanceError. An axis_info request raises on the missing row zero and leaves the attachment with zero selected rows.

casa-rs preserves the empty stride result and returns typed empty UVW components and flag counts of shape (0, 0). The axis metadata query raises while retaining the prior active row view (#1030).

With average=True, CASA also indexes the missing channel and row dimensions of the rank-one empty visibility array. The pinned control reported DATA shape (0, 1). casa-rs returns deterministic averaged shapes (0, 0) for data and (0, 0, 1) for flags, with typed empty weights.

On the 30-row control, getdata(['data', 'DATA'], increment=3, average=True) raises because the first reduction consumed its temporary field. CASA then leaves the 10-row stride selected. casa-rs reports the duplicate averaging error and retains the original active rows.

docs.title: MS visibility averaging uses the wrong row and correlation weights
docs.text:
In CASA 6.7.6.14, ms.getdata(['data', 'flag', 'weight'], average=True) advances a flattened WEIGHT pointer once per row and applies that value to every correlation and channel. WEIGHT instead has a separate cell for each correlation and row. For six rows with first-channel correlation 0 values [1, 9, 17, 25, 33, 41], weights [1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11], and the second value flagged, CASA returns 29.631578. The unflagged weighted mean is 30.575758. The stock NGC 5921 test_getdata_args also records CASA's flattened-weight result.

casa-rs applies each unflagged visibility's own row and correlation weight before projecting its amplitude, phase, real, or imaginary part. The original test stays verbatim, and an independent weighted regression checks the corrected scientific result (#1030). Pinned casacore averaging loop

docs.title: Averaging the same MS sigma field twice can exhaust memory
docs.text:
For an ordinary MS with a nonempty SIGMA matrix, CASA 6.7.6.14 ms.getdata(['avg_sigma', 'sigma'], average=True) reduces SIGMA twice. The second call supplies a vector to a routine that indexes dimensions of a matrix or cube. On the 30-row control the process consumed one CPU and grew past 5 GiB of resident memory before it was stopped.

casa-rs computes the root sum of squares over the row axis once and retains the raw array returned for the literal avg_sigma item (#1030).

docs.title: MS baseline-axis gap metadata can terminate the process
docs.text:
In CASA 6.7.6.14, ms.getdata(['axis_info'], ifraxis=True, ifraxisgap=1) on a view with several first-antenna groups uses the gap sentinel -1 as an ANTENNA row index. The pinned CASA process aborted in a casacore array slice. casa-rs preserves the -1 baseline number and puts empty names and a zero length at each gap. The other axis coordinates remain available (#1030).

The same invalid access occurs in a row-blocked iterator when axis_info is requested with gaps. The baseline numbers and numeric visibility record remain readable on pinned CASA when axis_info is omitted.

docs.title: MS baseline-axis singleton integrations can return invalid coordinates or hang
docs.text:
CASA 6.7.6.14 removes the time dimension of visibility arrays when exactly one integration is available. Its baseline flag_sum still reads that missing extent. The pinned process did not return from the two-row control within 30 seconds and was terminated. The UT coordinate also reads a second integration in this case. For a 5-second integration its result was the absolute MJD seconds instead of seconds from midnight.

casa-rs retains the singleton visibility shape, counts the flags at each baseline's one integration, and uses that integration to determine midnight for UT (#1030).

docs.title: Duplicate MS baseline-axis fields can append spurious integrations
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 appends a baseline/time block each time an item occurs in ms.getdata(items, ifraxis=True). A two-integration view queried for ['time', 'data', 'TIME'] reports four times for two data slices. casa-rs uses one integration axis for each case-insensitive field name and leaves the attachment selection intact (#1030).

docs.title: The legacy MS baseline number can identify two different antenna pairs
docs.text:
CASA 6.7.6.14 uses 1000 * ANTENNA1 + ANTENNA2 as both the displayed baseline number and the key for placing data on the ifraxis grid. On a valid MS with 1,002 antennas, baselines (0, 1001) and (1, 1) at the same time yield one slot numbered 1001. CASA discards the earlier pair's visibility and derives the label for both from (1, 1).

casa-rs places and labels data by the actual antenna pair. Both slots and their separate labels remain available even when their legacy public baseline numbers coincide (#1030).

docs.title: MS baseline-axis averaging can weight the wrong cells and collapse baselines
docs.text:
With ifraxis=True, average=True, CASA 6.7.6.14 advances its flattened WEIGHT pointer once per baseline and integration. The stored WEIGHT has a separate value for each correlation, baseline and integration. Zero-filled sparse slots also reach the averaging loop with their flag clear. On the sparse eight-row control, one measured sample of 89 is halved to 44.5, other measured samples disappear, and seven output flags disagree with the independent weighted calculation.

With only one integration, the visibility cube has no final time axis. CASA interprets its baseline dimension as ordinary rows and collapses four distinct baselines into one result with no baseline dimension.

casa-rs reduces occupied slots within each antenna pair using each unflagged sample's correlation weight. It retains the baseline axis for a single integration and marks a sample with no unflagged observations flagged. Unchanged upstream tests still record the pinned CASA results (#1030). Pinned casacore averaging loop

docs.title: MS averaged sidereal time can fail when multiple fields are selected
docs.text: CASA 6.7.6.14 derives the common FIELD_ID as -1 when a time-averaged selection spans fields. With ifraxis=True, average=True, a request for axis_info and last then tries to open FIELD row 18446744073709551615. Local apparent sidereal time depends on the epoch and observatory position. casa-rs computes it in the first antenna's measure frame at the mean epoch, including when no single field describes the selection (#1030).

docs.title: MS channel selection can accept an index one past the window
docs.text: On a four-channel MS, CASA 6.7.6.14 accepts selectchannel(3, 0, 1, 2), which requests channels 0, 2 and 4. A later getdata aborts while using the invalid channel. casa-rs checks every selected bin against the active spectral windows, returns false at selection time and retains the previous channel selection (#1030).

docs.title: MS channel selection repeats channels when data descriptions share a window
docs.text: With two active data descriptions for the same spectral window and four input channels, CASA 6.7.6.14 returns four DATA and FLAG channels for either selectchannel(2, 0, 1, 2) or selectchannel(2, 0, 2, 2). It adds each range to the iterator once per description. Both frequency and resolution metadata still describe two selected channels. casa-rs applies each range once per spectral window so DATA, FLAG and the reported frequencies have the requested channel count. It preserves the selected rows and their order (#1030).

docs.title: MS channel averaging mistakes data description IDs for visibilities
docs.text: After selectchannel(2, 0, 2, 2), CASA 6.7.6.14 raises an incorrect-data-type error for getdata('data_desc_id'). Its flagged-visibility cleanup treats the integer field as complex data because its name contains data. casa-rs preserves the integer row IDs while averaging the visibility channels (#1030).

docs.title: MS time averages use mismatched flags and weights after Stokes conversion
docs.text: For an MS recording RR and LL, select I and call getdata with average=True. CASA 6.7.6.14 passes the one-correlation visibility cube to its averaging loop with the original two-correlation flags and weights. The loop walks the flags by the converted data shape and does not select a weight for each output correlation. With unequal recorded weights and flags, one controlled MS differed from the propagated-variance calculation by 0.059 normalized RMS on ordinary reads and 0.250 when averaging by baseline. casa-rs projects visibility flags and inverse variances to the selected Stokes products for the reduction. Public raw weight and sigma fields retain their recorded correlation axes, as in CASA (#1030).

docs.title: MS channel averaging can abort when Stokes conversion changes the axis size
docs.text: On an MS with four channels and recorded RR and LL, call selectchannel(2, 0, 2, 2), selectpolarization(['I']) and then getdata(['data', 'flag', 'axis_info']). CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts with an uncaught ArrayConformanceError. Its flagged-data cleanup reshapes the one-correlation converted data using the two-correlation recorded flag cube. casa-rs uses the converted flag axis to zero the masked Stokes values and returns the recorded FLAG shape and the requested Stokes data shape (#1030).

docs.title: MS polarization reads can reuse the wrong recorded correlation order
docs.text: Interleave two data descriptions for the same spectral window. The first records [RR, LL]. The second records [LL, RR] with matching receptor products. In CASA 6.7.6.14, both selectpolarization(['RR']) and conversion to ['I', 'V'] can use the first description's order for a row in the second description. For a second-description row with real samples [9, 10], CASA read RR as 9 and Stokes V as −0.5. casa-rs uses each row's recorded correlation order, giving RR 10 and V +0.5 (#1030).

docs.title: MS iteration can reuse stale row blocking after a cursor is replaced
docs.text: On an MS with ten rows per integration, call iterinit(maxrows=7) and position the cursor. A subsequent iterinit() should restore ordinary chunk traversal. CASA 6.7.6.14 leaves the previous maxrows flag set and reads only the first integration of the new outer chunk. Ending the blocked iterator and then requesting a normal read with selected channels or correlations can also raise “Attempt to advance subchunk past end of chunk.” casa-rs keeps row blocking with the cursor that requested it. Reinitialization and ordinary reads use the requested layout (#1030).

docs.title: MS iterator argument errors can replace an active cursor
docs.text: After starting a blocked cursor with iterinit(maxrows=7) and iterorigin(), pass an invalid interval such as None or the string "15", or pass maxrows=None. CASA 6.7.6.14 reports a Python SystemError but replaces the active cursor before reporting it. The next getdata('time') raises “VisBuffer not positioned to a subchunk.” casa-rs retains the positioned cursor when Python argument conversion fails and returns the same exception class (#1030).

docs.title: MS row-blocked baseline reads can lose an integration or average across baselines
docs.text: With ten baselines per integration, call iterinit(maxrows=12), iterorigin(), and getdata(['data', 'time'], ifraxis=True). The first block contains ten rows from the first integration and two from the second. CASA 6.7.6.14 replaces the first two baseline samples with the later values and reports only the first time. casa-rs returns both times on the integration axis and retains all twelve samples. With maxrows=3 and average=True, CASA reduces the baseline axis and returns one value per correlation and channel. casa-rs averages across time for each baseline and retains the baseline axis, including flags for absent samples (#1030).

docs.title: MS iterator frequency metadata can refer to a different data description
docs.text: On an MS with four channels in the first data description and three in the second, start ordinary iteration over all rows before requesting any visibility record. The first read initializes the ordinary attachment view to the first description, while the iterator still traverses both. CASA 6.7.6.14 reads three-channel data in the second chunk but reports the first description's four-channel frequencies. casa-rs reports the frequencies of the iterator's data description while keeping the ordinary attachment selection separate (#1030).

docs.title: A live Stokes conversion can use the wrong stored hand of an MS iterator
docs.text: For a MeasurementSet recording RR and LL, select LL before starting and positioning an iterator, then select I before reading the chunk. CASA 6.7.6.14 keeps the one-correlation flag and weight shapes but can read a contiguous prefix of the original two-correlation data into the one-hand shape. This mixes recorded correlations, channels, and rows. With RR selected, the same test also changes the sample amplitudes. casa-rs applies the live conversion to the captured data and its physical correlation label, giving half the recorded parallel-hand visibility for I when only that hand is present. The reduction uses the corresponding flags and variances (#1030).

docs.title: MS visibility ranges can include a zero from an entirely flagged first block
docs.text: For a reference view with a fully flagged first block and a later unflagged sample with real values 9 through 16, CASA 6.7.6.14 reports a real range of [0, 16] with blocksize=1. The same rows read with blocksize=10 report [9, 16]. CASA treats the earlier empty block's zero-initialized extrema as valid measurements. casa-rs initializes the range from the first included sample, independent of the block size. An entirely flagged selection still yields CASA's zero extrema (#1030).

docs.title: An entirely flagged FLOAT_DATA range can abort CASA
docs.text: Call ms.range('float_data') when every sample is flagged. CASA 6.7.6.14 aborts with an uncaught ArrayError from MaskedArray::minMax, which requires an unmasked sample. casa-rs uses the same zero extrema as an entirely flagged complex visibility range and keeps the tool attached. Calling again with useflags=False returns the recorded extrema (#1030).

docs.title: MS writes can overrun a positioned max-row block
docs.text: Position an MS cursor with iterinit(['TIME'], 0.0, 10, False), advance to the second block, and pass its ten-row getdata('data') array back to putdata. CASA 6.7.6.14 restarts the inner traversal and attempts to slice rows 10–19 from the ten-row array. The resulting ArrayError aborts the Python process. casa-rs uses the rows of the positioned block and writes no other rows (#1030).

docs.title: An invalid MS write can leave CASA using the previous selection
docs.text: On a writable MS, pass a Float32 array for FLAG_ROW to putdata. CASA 6.7.6.14 rejects its type after creating an internal iterator. Selecting only row zero and writing one Boolean row plus a weight vector on the same attachment can then abort. Closing and reopening before the second selection succeeds. casa-rs validates the record before starting a mutation. The error leaves the attachment usable for a new selection and write (#1030).

docs.title: MS writes can reorder values read from saved views
docs.text:
Read getdata('data') from a saved reference whose rows are out of order, or from a multi-MS whose members cover the same integration times. With no explicit iterator, CASA 6.7.6.14 can sort the rows for putdata even though it returned the input in view order. Modified samples then go to different physical rows or members. casa-rs writes each row to its saved physical location in view order. Where a reference repeats one physical row, its final supplied value wins (#1030).

For a single integration, getdata(ifraxis=True) drops the singleton time dimension. On the saved row order [2, 0, 3], CASA 6.7.6.14 returned the three baselines in order [0, 2, 3] and swapped physical rows 0 and 2 when the array was written back unchanged. casa-rs resolves an ambiguous trailing axis using the most recent read of writable visibility data. A subsequent ordinary row-axis read restores row ordering for such arrays (#1030).

docs.title: An MS write after baseline downsampling can overwrite omitted rows with zeros
docs.text: On a writable MeasurementSet, read getdata('data', ifraxis=True, increment=2) and pass its baseline-axis array to putdata. CASA 6.7.6.14 restores the full row selection after the read but retains the sampled baseline axis. It writes zeros to rows on baselines absent from that axis. In the control, CASA zeros the visibilities in 15 of 30 rows. casa-rs rejects the sampled baseline-axis record before mutation. A fresh read with increment=1 supplies a complete writable grid (#1030).

docs.title: MS record selection can misread non-native NumPy byte order
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14 on a little-endian host, ms.select({'antenna1': v}) selects antenna 0 from the big-endian Int64 array v = numpy.array([1], dtype='>i8'). On NGC 5921 that gives 1,619 rows instead of the 1,559 for antenna 1. An exact times selection using a big-endian Float64 array for a known integration selects zero of its 351 rows. casa-rs reads the numeric values according to the array dtype's byte order and selects the specified antenna and integration (#1030).

docs.title: A two-dimensional MS record selection can terminate CASA
docs.text: In CASA 6.7.6.14, ms.select({'rows': numpy.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])}) can abort with a casacore ArrayNDimError when it tries to construct a vector. casa-rs raises a Python RuntimeError when a numeric selection field has more than one non-singleton axis. It retains earlier successful fields in the same ordered record. A vector with a singleton axis, such as shape (1, 4), is accepted (#1030).

docs.title: Agent Reference
docs.text:
Truth class: normative Last reality check: 2026-11-02 Verification: just docs-check

Situational guidance for agents: read only the section relevant to the task.

docs.title: CASA And C++ Oracles
docs.text:
• Local CASA task runs use the CASA 6.7.6 release's Python, /Applications/CASA.app/Contents/MacOS/python3, which has casatasks and casatools. Scripts take CASA_RS_CASA_PYTHON to use another one. On the Mac mini the release (6.7.6.14) is /Volumes/Extra Storage (not encrypted)/DeveloperTools/CASA.app, so set CASA_RS_CASA_PYTHON to its Contents/MacOS/python3 there.
  • The CASA task inventory (resources/casa-compat/casa-6.7.6.14/) is pinned to CASA 6.7.6.14. scripts/test-casa-inventory.sh compares it with the installed CASA and fails when CASA is missing or another version; --write re-records it and regenerates docs/reference/casa-compatibility.md.

docs.title: plotms PNG Export
docs.text:
For headless CASA plotms oracle PNGs, set:

DISPLAY=${DISPLAY:-:99}
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=${QT_QPA_PLATFORM:-offscreen}
MPLBACKEND=${MPLBACKEND:-Agg}

Then call casaplotms.plotms with showgui=False, plotfile=..., expformat="png", and overwrite=True.

The local macOS CASA build does not use Xvfb, but plotms still requires DISPLAY. Do not run this CASA/Qt path in a shell sandbox that blocks sysctl CPU-feature queries: Qt may mis-detect arm64 NEON and print Incompatible processor. Use the normal user environment or an explicitly unsandboxed command runner.

docs.title: Shared Data Roots
docs.text:
TESTING.md is the canonical resolver policy. Current workstation locations are:

  • Shared CASA C++ test data: CASA_RS_TESTDATA_ROOT, ../casatestdata, or ~/SoftwareProjects/casatestdata; long-gate preflight may select /Volumes/home/casatestdata when it contains the required paths.
  • Tutorial parity data: CASA_RS_TUTORIAL_DATA_ROOT/tutorial-parity/... or ~/SoftwareProjects/casa-tutorial-data/tutorial-parity/.... No copy is kept; /Volumes/home/casa-rs/tutorial-data/ holds the download scripts and checksums to fetch the data from NRAO.
  • Measures runtime data: an explicit root supplied to MeasuresRuntime::open, or a complete CASA_RS_MEASURESPATH / ~/.casa/data candidate selected by the application before opening the runtime. Discovery never installs data.
  • Small bundled real-MS CI fixtures: crates/casa-ms/tests/fixtures/.

Slow, release, parity, and tutorial gates run shared-data preflight and report the selected root. Do not use /private/tmp as a canonical dataset location or add personal workstation archives as implicit default-gate fallbacks.

docs.title: Storage Locations
docs.text:
Follow the storage rules in AGENTS.md. Current locations:

  • Internal disk (small; keep at least about 40 GB free): source, builds, and small durable evidence for quick tests under /Users/brianglendenning/SoftwareProjects/casa-rs-evidence/<work-item>/.
  • NAS storage over Tailscale, mounted at /Volumes/home: large or long-lived artifacts under /Volumes/home/casa-rs/. Shared CASA test data is at /Volumes/home/casatestdata. The laptop mounts it at login and remounts it when it drops (a user LaunchAgent; the login is in the Keychain).
  • External disk GLENDENNING at /Volumes/GLENDENNING/: a 1 TB NVMe SSD (about 3 GB/s), fast working space for large datasets and runs, never the only copy of anything that matters. Copy a run's inputs onto it from the NAS first; never read a large MeasurementSet over the network in place.
  • Archives of earlier GLENDENNING disks on the NAS, each with a README.md that maps its paths: /Volumes/home/casa-rs-glendenning-preserve/GLENDENNING/ and /Volumes/home/casa-rs/glendenning-stick-20261016/.

Keep an MS or large output only when it will be reused and would take hours to regenerate: a fixed timing input, or a long CASA run used as a correctness reference, kept with the exact MS it ran on. Record its generator, parameters and timings in a manifest beside the archive (for example T55's casa-rs-evidence/t55/GOLDEN-DATASETS.md in the preserve archive).

docs.title: Workstation Toolchain
docs.text:
• Keep Xcode and the Command Line Tools on the same major version. If cc links fail with tapi error ... unknown architecture (for example while building fitsio-sys), xcrun is resolving a newer Command Line Tools SDK than Xcode's linker understands: update Xcode, or set SDKROOT=$(xcode-select -p)/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk.
  • After an Xcode update, run sudo xcodebuild -license accept and sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch; until then git and cc fail.
  • FFTW: casa-fft finds FFTW through pkg-config, so a plain build links Homebrew's FFTW, which has no NEON kernels. Releases build the SIMD FFTW with scripts/build-fftw.sh. Performance work and timing evidence use the same build: on this workstation it is PKG_CONFIG_PATH=/Users/brianglendenning/SoftwareProjects/fftw-3.3.11-simd/lib/pkgconfig. Check which FFTW a binary linked (the target/release/build/casa-fft-*/output link path, or nm BIN | grep -c n1fv_ for NEON codelets) before comparing timings, and link both sides of an A/B against the same FFTW.

docs.title: Cloud Sessions
docs.text:
Claude Code cloud sessions run in a Linux container prepared by .claude/hooks/session-start.sh. Variables in the cloud environment's settings extend it; a session reads them when it starts.

  • TS_AUTHKEY joins the session to the owner's tailnet in the background (.claude/hooks/tailscale-up.sh; log in /var/log/tailscale-up.log). Use an ephemeral key. The container has no UDP, so peers are reached through Tailscale's relays: fine for SSH and small files, slow for bulk data.
  • CASA_RS_MAC_SSH_KEY lets the session work on the Mac mini (bg-mac-mini) as the owner: the macOS-only crates and Metal tests, the CASA oracle, or a second build beside the local one. scripts/mac-run.sh COMMAND mirrors the working tree to the mini and runs COMMAND there (--help for details).
  • The value is a private key without a passphrase whose public half is in the owner's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the mini, base64-encoded onto one line (base64 -i KEY | tr -d '\n' on macOS). CASA_RS_MAC_USER overrides the login name (default brianglendenning).
  • Copies live in ~/ext/SoftwareProjects/casa-rs-cloud/src/<branch>/ on the mini (the top of the ~/ext volume is owned by root), each building in its own targets/<branch>/ beside src/, since copies sharing one target would link each other's crates; CASA_RS_MAC_ROOT overrides the location. Remove a branch's copy and target with scripts/mac-run.sh --clean once its work is merged or pushed.
  • Commands run in a login shell, which reads ~/.zprofile and ~/.zshenv but not ~/.zshrc; settings the tests need, such as CASA_RS_MEASURESPATH, belong in the former. ~/.zshenv must print nothing, or rsync fails with "is your shell clean?". Stopping the script does not stop the command at once; it ends when it next writes output.
  • The script uses Homebrew's rsync on the mini when it is installed and the system openrsync otherwise; if openrsync refuses a transfer, brew install rsync there.
  • Run work that reads large data on the mini, next to the NAS and GLENDENNING, and bring back only results.
  • The NAS is not mounted in cloud sessions: the container's kernel has no SMB support and the NAS needs its own login. Reach its data from the mini, which does not mount it by default: the owner mounts it there (Finder or screen sharing) when a run needs it, and SSH logins see it under /Volumes while it stays mounted. Non-public datasets stay off the cloud container (AGENTS.md).

  • Local installs: just install-local (or just install-local-suite)

docs.text:
TESTING.md ("Imaging tiers and evidence") says what an evidence run must record. Locations on this workstation:

  • Timed rows and large inputs (pilot, 512-plane cube, deep32, full cube, Wave3, #625): ~/SoftwareProjects/casa-rs-if10-data.noindex/ on this laptop, ~/ext/SoftwareProjects/casa-rs-data/ on the Mac mini, and the NAS manifests under /Volumes/home/casa-rs/if10/.
  • Wave3: the MS that CASA's Wave3 reference was imaged on is casa-rs/glendenning-stick-20261016/wave3-regenerated-ms-20261013.tar, not the differing original in the NAS mirror.

An evidence run that needs one (forced paging, a fixed budget) builds an evidence-only patch of ImagingRequest::resource_policy and HostResources::detect from the committed head, labels the binary with the patch, and reverts the checkout afterwards; IF-11's patch is recorded on #660.

docs.title: Calibration Tasks User Guide
docs.text: This guide shows how to run the casa-rs calibration tasks from the calibrate command line and from Python.

docs.title: The calibration surfaces
docs.text:
All calibration work runs through one provider executable, calibrate. The application catalog exposes it as these task surfaces:

  • calibrate: the general surface; --mode selects apply, export_corrected_data, fluxscale, gencal, solve_bandpass, solve_gain, stats, or summary
  • gaincal, bandpass, applycal, fluxscale, gencal, clearcal, delmod, uvsub: CASA's tasks, with CASA 6.7.6's parameters and defaults

Every surface is a one-shot task. Run it as calibrate <surface> (calibrate bandpass --ms ...; calibrate alone is the general surface), which resolves a parameter profile (Defaults, Last, Last Successful, or a TOML file), applies overrides, saves Last state in the workspace, and runs the task. See Task Parameter Profiles for sources and managed Last files, and the generated parameter reference for every parameter and its CLI flag.

Use a writable copy of the dataset when you intend to apply calibration, because applycal (and calibrate --mode apply) writes CORRECTED_DATA in place, as CASA's does. As in CASA, a calflag run first saves the flags to the next applycal_N flag version (flagbackup, default on), so flagmanager can restore them; --no-flagbackup skips it, and calonly and trial change no flags and save none.

docs.title: ngc5921.ms walkthrough
docs.text:
Expected field roles:

  • field 0: flux/bandpass calibrator
  • field 1: phase calibrator
  • field 2: target

Recommended reference antenna: VA15.

workdir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/casars-cal.XXXXXX)
cp -R /path/to/casatestdata/measurementset/vla/ngc5921.ms "$workdir/ngc5921.ms"
cd "$workdir"
  1. Solve a phase-only gain on field 0:

bash calibrate gaincal --vis ngc5921.ms --caltable ngc5921.G0 \ --refant VA15 --gaintype G --calmode p --solint inf \ --field 0 --spw 0 --smodel 1,0,0,0

  1. Solve the bandpass on field 0, applying the gain table on the fly:

bash calibrate bandpass --vis ngc5921.ms --caltable ngc5921.B0 \ --refant VA15 --gaintable ngc5921.G0 --field 0 --smodel 1,0,0,0

  1. Apply both tables to field 0:

bash calibrate applycal --vis ngc5921.ms \ --gaintable ngc5921.G0,ngc5921.B0 --field 0

  1. Inspect the solutions and the corrected data with calibrate --mode stats or --mode summary, and plotms.

The CASA-named surfaces take CASA's chain: the --gaintable list, with the positional --gainfield, --interp and --spwmap lists, so the i-th table takes the i-th entry of each and a table past the end of a list takes CASA's default (every field, linear, no window map); --calwt gives one flag for every table or one per table. A flag's value is split at commas, so an entry that holds a comma, such as CASA's interp='nearest,linear', is given as a Python list: --interp "['linear', 'nearest,linear']", and so is a window map per table: --spwmap '[[0, 0], []]'. --docallib --callib FILE applies a CASA calibration library instead. --applymode trial reports the apply plan without changing the MeasurementSet. calibrate --mode apply keeps casa-rs's own --gaintables with ;-separated per-table lists.

With an empty smodel, gaincal and channelized bandpass (bandtype='B') look for the selected field's virtual model, then its MODEL_DATA column, and fall back to a 1 Jy point source. Supply a point source for BPOLY when the selected data has a stored model. A CASA parameter casa-rs does not implement yet is taken only at its default, and a CASA value such as gaintype='GSPLINE' is refused until implemented. These errors name #979. docs/reference/casa-compatibility.md lists them.

Channelized bandpass can average selected channels before solving. Use solint='inf,4ch' for four channels per solution or solint='25s,3MHz' to set a 25-second time interval and a 3 MHz frequency interval.

Use calibrate gaincal --template to see every parameter with its default, and --save-params FILE to keep a run's resolved profile for reuse with --params FILE.

Use gaintype='K' to solve antenna delays or gaintype='KCROSS' to solve the shared cross-hand delay. Supply a reference antenna and select at least two frequency channels. KCROSS needs four correlations. The output stores delays in nanoseconds as FPARAM and can be supplied to applycal or to a subsequent solve as a prior calibration table.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
The same surfaces are generated functions under casars.tasks with CASA's signatures (casars.tasks.gaincal(...), casars.tasks.applycal(...), and so on), returning what CASA's tasks return, and casars.tasks.run("gaincal", ...) accepts the same parameters and returns the run's TaskCompletion. Each call starts the calibrate executable in the current directory (or in tasks.run's workspace), passes its log to sys.stderr, and saves no Last. CASA's parameters are the consent; there are no separate confirmations.

from casars import tasks

solved = tasks.gaincal(vis="ngc5921.ms", caltable="ngc5921.G0", refant="VA15",
                       gaintype="G", calmode="p", solint="inf", field="0", spw="0",
                       smodel=[1, 0, 0, 0])
solved["selectvis"]["antennas"]   # the antennas the solve selected

Profiles saved before these surfaces took CASA's names load as the runs they meant: out_table becomes caltable, gain_type='g' becomes gaintype='G', the ;-separated per-table lists become CASA's positional lists, and so on. Where CASA's default differs (applycal's calwt, gaincal's calmode and smodel, bandpass's combine and smodel), a profile that left the value out adopts CASA's default with a warning.

Scientific products follow each CASA task's lifecycle: gaincal and bandpass replace an existing calibration table unless append=True; fluxscale refuses an existing flux table unless append=True; gencal adds specified real corrections to its existing table; gain-curve generation replaces its absolute coefficients. Append requires a compatible calibration type, MeasurementSet identity and spectral metadata. A solve with no successful solutions returns its statistics without writing or replacing a table. New products are staged before publication so a failed run preserves the prior product.

On these CASA-named tasks, overwrite=True controls only the output report. On the native calibrate workflow, it also permits replacing its scientific output (including corrected-data exports); without it an existing output is refused. Report collisions are checked before the scientific operation runs.

Reports cannot overlap scientific inputs or outputs, including prior calibration tables and gain-curve sources. Append retains additional local keyword subtables.

Scientific publication reserves the destination across processes. An interrupted writer leaves its reservation and staging or backup directories beside the product; a later writer refuses them. Inspect those directories and recover the prior product before removing the reservation and retrying. Append refuses symbolic-link subtables rather than risking their loss during replacement.

docs.title: Reset and remove visibility models
docs.text:
tasks.clearcal(vis, field='', spw='', intent='', addmodel=False) resets CORRECTED_DATA from DATA and initializes an existing MODEL_DATA to an unpolarized unit model on the same selected rows and channels. Any missing scratch columns it creates are initialized across the whole MeasurementSet. Set addmodel=True to create MODEL_DATA when it is absent.

tasks.delmod(vis, otf=True, field='', scr=False) removes the virtual model recipes for the selected fields. An empty field selects all fields. Set scr=True to drop the whole MODEL_DATA column. Set otf=False to retain the virtual recipes. Both tasks update the MeasurementSet in place and return None.

tasks.uvsub(vis, reverse=False) writes the residual to CORRECTED_DATA. When the corrected column is absent, it starts from the observed data. It reads a field's virtual model, its scratch model, or the default unit model in that order. Set reverse=True to add the model. The casars.tools.ms tool exposes the same operation through uvsub(reverse=False) on a MeasurementSet opened with nomodify=False.

docs.title: Current limitations
docs.text: • there is not yet a dedicated setjy task

docs.title: Concatenating simulated MeasurementSets
docs.text:
casars.tasks.concat and the concat binary combine simulated interferometric MeasurementSets through the existing observation creation plan. The task has CASA 6.7.6's nine parameters, in its order and with its defaults, and returns None in Python.

from casars.tasks import concat
concat(vis=["simulation.12m.ms", "simulation.7m.ms"],
       concatvis="combined.ms", visweightscale=[1.0, 0.34])

The simulation subset sorts inputs by their earliest integration, keeps each weight factor with its input, merges the standard catalogues, offsets scans, and writes every stored MAIN row, including flagged rows with NaN weights. It preserves pointing names, targets and tracking flags, static feed validity, unused antennas' feeds, source-model records, separate row/element flags, stored sigma and uncertainty spectra. Weights multiply by their factor; sigma divides by its square root. Stored spectra may vary by channel. Matching static feeds combine validity as CASA does.
