Amended: 2026-10-03, on owner direction: private same-run spill keeps no checksums, and ownership-only association extends to imaging inputs, replay and reprojection targets (this replaced the spill exemption of 2026-09-18). 2026-10-09, on owner direction: nothing of casa-rs's is stored in the MeasurementSet (ADR-0008). 2026-11-02, on owner approval: the 2026-10-03 decision, recorded separately until then, is merged here.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Imaging once hashed product content and reread complete arrays to authorize publication, kept SHA-256 or CRC framing on private same-run spill, and minted content identities for models, plans and normal state. None of it had an independent trust boundary: the generator and its writer, and a spill file's writer and reader, are the same trusted process. A fresh digest with no independently trusted expected value detects no corruption; it only gives corrupted bytes a different identity. The mechanism cost initial hashes, repeated verification, private backing arrays, copies and staged records on the timed path.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Identity is ownership.

  1. No content attestation. Production code computes no SHA-256, CRC or other digest over scientific arrays (visibilities, models, weights, reprojection targets, replay contributions), compiled problems, plans, run summaries or spill to mint, verify or authorize an identity, and makes no verification-only pass over full arrays. There is no optional mode, renamed substitute, memoized seal or compatibility checksum. Already available metadata is compared directly, not serialized and hashed.
  2. Ownership. Trusted data within one process is associated by ownership, compiled selection and shape, row and channel order, actual completion counts and live lifecycle checks. A live owner token is not a content fingerprint and is not a portable identity for another run. Values and support are validated where they enter or change; continuing, preparing a delta or completing does not rehash or reread an unchanged model.
  3. Nothing in the MeasurementSet. Holding the open MeasurementSet is the ownership. casa-rs stores no keywords, generations, identities or marker files in it (ADR-0008).
  4. Run-local spill. Private same-run spill is part of the bounded buffer system, not a trust boundary. It keeps versioned framing, exact lengths and offsets, frame order and counts, shape and inventory, source association, file identity, truncation and EOF checks and ordinary I/O error propagation, and no payload or header checksums.
  5. Products. Generation writes bounded owned windows directly into the CASA-compatible writer's private staging images. It keeps the member inventory and shape, ordered complete window coverage, metadata, WCS, masks and beams, fallible writes and flushes, resource admission and the atomic replacement of each image. If publication fails the run fails and its output set is incomplete; rerunning is required. There is no resumable member ledger, partial-publication recovery or rollback, the set is not an atomic transaction, and a failed set is never reported as a success.
  6. Bounded telemetry. Progress stays in memory and is O(1) per phase; nothing serializes, hashes or walks whole plans, models or history. A run leaves one final success or failure summary.

Unchanged: CASA-compatible formats and the integrity their formats define; checksums that external formats or imported artifacts carry; scientific algorithms, flags, masks, WCS, beams and numerical acceptance; bounded memory. Diagnostic fingerprints are allowed in explicitly invoked tests and benchmarks and never add work to production execution.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - no hashing, rereads, backing copies or verification phases on the timed path - one notion of identity across products, models, plans and spill

Negative: - an equal-length corruption of private spill is not detected by a checksum; scientific value checks still apply where data is consumed - a failed publication leaves an incomplete output set to regenerate

Neutral / tradeoffs: - no bitwise floating-point output requirement may justify extra production buffers, passes or arithmetic beyond scientific acceptance

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Keep product attestation as an optional mode. Rejected: it keeps the mechanism and its cost under another name.
  2. Keep CRCs on private spill. Rejected: the writer and reader are one trusted process, and framing checks catch truncation and misordering.
  3. Make the output set an atomic transaction with member recovery. Rejected on owner direction: rerunning the task is the recovery.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: product publication tests of write-only bounded ownership, complete ordered coverage, unchanged science and metadata and real I/O failures (TESTING.md); count, order, source and lifecycle checks on owned data - lint/import/dependency rules: scripts/check-imaging-dependencies.py refuses content hashing in the imaging and simulation crates (no-content-hashing-in-imaging-crates); imaging code rule 4 in ARCHITECTURE.md - CI checks: just arch-check - review trigger: reintroducing production attestation, a verification-only full-array pass or a telemetry exception needs a new ADR and the owner's approval, with a concrete failure model and measured CPU, memory, I/O and end-to-end cost; a ban on the word "seal" is not a sufficient check - none / guidance only:

docs.title: Drift detection
docs.text: Suspect drift if: - a hash, CRC or digest is computed over scientific data, a plan or spill in production code, under any name - a phase rereads a complete product or model only to authorize it - progress reporting serializes or scans whole plans, models or history - casa-rs writes anything into a MeasurementSet that CASA would not - a failed publication is reported as a success or partly recovered

docs.title: ADR-0016: Imaging foundation
docs.text:
Status: accepted Date: 2026-10-07 Truth class: normative Supersedes: the unified imaging resource authority ADR of 2026-08-18 (deleted 2026-11-02; git history keeps it); the "Migration" section and the attestation wording of ADR-0009; the joint continuum-plus-line decision of ADR-0011 Superseded by:

Amended: 2026-10-25, on owner direction: every imaging crate may depend on the definitional crates (decision 10). 2026-10-28, on owner approval: the model may also depend on casa-observation (decision 10; imaging port decision 1,

Amended: 2026-10-28, on owner direction of 2026-10-27 (#938): single-dish image-plane gridding is its own operator family (decision 13).

Amended: 2026-11-02, on owner approval: the foundation plan this ADR cited was deleted; its references now point to ARCHITECTURE.md, TESTING.md or git history, and the ticket and review-gate process (decision 12) is reduced to what still holds.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Programme #486 delivered cube, MFS, Clark, multi-worker and Metal imaging as several parallel routes: four CPU gridding drivers, two Metal drivers, closed enums selecting gridders, a 20k-line replay cache standing in for re-reading the MeasurementSet, and a runtime whose receipts, execution DAG, resource topology and identity hashing were almost entirely write-only. W-projection, AW-projection and mosaic could not reach the fast cube path or Metal. The programme's own process machinery (a migration matrix, a 3,578-line checker hashing Rust function bodies, per-ticket contract revisions) would resist any consolidation. The owner reviewed this state on 2026-10-07 and approved the imaging foundation plan, which git keeps at 0b470017:docs/imaging-architecture/imaging-foundation-plan-20261007.md.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
CASA-RS imaging is one measurement operator, one major-cycle pass, one deconvolution driver and one execution model. This ADR records the binding decisions. The plan's review rules (its section 10) are the imaging code rules in ARCHITECTURE.md, and its test tiers (section 7) are TESTING.md "Imaging tiers and evidence"; the rest of the plan is the design as landed, kept in git at the location above as a record, not a binding document.

  1. One operator. casa-imaging-operator owns Placement/SampleBlock records, a ConvolutionFunctionSet trait with exactly four implementations (standard spheroidal, W-planes, AW catalog, mosaic PB), a GridBackend trait with exactly two implementations (CPU, Metal), GridAccumulator, MeasurementOperator and WeightingGeneration. Standard, W, AW, mosaic, MT-MFS, cube and MFS imaging are parameterisations of these types. Paired forward/adjoint choices (kernel set, conjugation, Mueller routing, phase gradient, phase-centre phasor, channel and polarisation maps, Taylor factors) live in the operator's kernel contract: the Placement, SampleBlock and GridBackend rustdoc (the plan's section 5.3 records the design as landed).
  2. One pass. Every major cycle re-traverses the selected MeasurementSet through MajorCyclePass and grids residual samples. No replay cache of visibility-independent factors is retained; a bounded tap-plan cache may be added later only as a measured execution strategy over the same operator.
  3. One driver. casa-imaging-deconvolution owns the minor-cycle driver, the controller (thresholds, cycleniter, convergence and divergence rules) and a Solver trait with Hogbom, Clark, multiscale and Taylor implementations.
  4. Runtime core. Resource handling is HostResources, a ResourcePolicy, one admit() per phase returning an RAII reservation, a sequential phase list with a cancel token, the Metal execution state and the bounded worker team. There are no execution receipts, execution DAG, lease epochs, logical/physical slot ledgers, cost-model profiles, adaptation transitions or plan identities. The only runtime record is an O(1)-per-phase run summary. The earlier unified resource authority is superseded in full.
  5. No identity hashing. Compiled problems, plans, products and selections are compared directly or by ownership. No identity is persisted; an AW convolution-function cache is reused by its cell layout (decision 7). ADR-0014 (identity is ownership) remains in force and covers plans and run summaries. Nothing of casa-rs's is persisted in a MeasurementSet: no keywords, generations, identities or marker files. Imaging opens a MeasurementSet as CASA writes it (owner direction 2026-10-09, which amends ADR-0008).
  6. Grid precision. Metal accumulates in f32; CPU defaults to f64 and offers f32 as a user-selectable request field. Acceptance is the 1e-3 normalised tolerance of the owner's 2026-09-24 direction, not bitwise agreement.
  7. AW cache. CASA CF images are read directly (headers at open, cells on demand into a bounded in-memory LRU). Native EVLA generation writes CASA-format CF images. There is no private content-addressed store, manifest, payload hash or eviction ledger.
  8. Request layer. One ImagingRequest struct defaulted and validated from the provider-contracts catalog; one CompiledProblem; one availability gate. Capabilities that are rejected are not in the catalog.
  9. Diagnostics. Library crates read no environment variables and emit no eprintln!; diagnostic switches are request fields; emission is tracing.
  10. Crates. casa-imaging-model, casa-imaging-operator, casa-imaging-deconvolution, casa-imaging-products, casa-imaging-runtime, casa-imaging-metal (macOS), and casa-imaging-application. casa-imaging-reconstruction is deleted when empty. Dependency direction is enforced by scripts/check-imaging-dependencies.py over cargo metadata. Every crate the policy covers, the model included, may depend on the definitional crates: crates that define values, units, quanta, measures and coordinate systems and the pure functions on them, do no file, network, process or environment I/O, start no threads, use no device, and depend on no workspace crate but one another. They are casa-values, casa-types and casa-coordinates; beyond them the model depends only on casa-observation, the observation boundary, whose catalogue, batches and pointing samples its batch geometry reads (amended 2026-10-28 on owner approval; imaging port decision 1 of 2026-10-27, #932). The policy names the definitional crates and lists each crate's other workspace dependencies exactly. Adding a crate to the definitional set widens what every layer may use, so it is the owner's decision, recorded on its pull request; the checks above then apply to it. (Amended 2026-10-25 on owner direction: with no workspace dependencies at all, the model could not share the workspace's correlation, measure and coordinate vocabulary and kept private copies of it, such as CorrelationType, DirectionFrame, FrequencyFrame and Epoch.)
  11. Joint continuum-plus-line reconstruction is removed from the code. ADR-0011's sequential continuum subtraction remains; its joint-basis decision is superseded and may be re-proposed as a separate ADR with its own scientific contract.
  12. Process. The migration matrix, contract revisions, evidence registries and programme-specific closure rules are retired and are not restored. Every imaging change is held to the imaging code rules in ARCHITECTURE.md; reviews follow AGENTS.md "Review".
  13. Single-dish gridding. Single-dish (total-power) imaging, CASA's SDGrid, places each spectrum at its pointing's pixel and spreads it with a radial kernel: no FFT, no uv coordinates and no gridding correction. It is its own operator family, outside decision 1's measurement operator and its four kernel sets. casa-imaging-singledish joins decision 10's crates in the execution layer. It owns the single-dish kernels, the image-plane gridder and the degridder that the simulator's total-power prediction uses, its adjoint. It admits its grids through the runtime and grids on its worker team. (Amended 2026-10-28, on owner direction of 2026-10-27, #938.)

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
Positive: - One place for each scientific choice; W, AW and mosaic reach every backend and the cube streaming path. - About 130k lines of parallel routes and write-only bookkeeping removed; target under 70k non-test imaging lines. - Tests become laws and tolerances rather than fixture expectations.

Negative: - Later major cycles re-read the MeasurementSet; the performance pass must show this is within the measured checkpoints or add a bounded cache. - Execution receipts are gone; the run summary is the one run record.

Neutral / tradeoffs: - Metal f32 accumulation differs from CPU f64 within tolerance; this is a precision choice, not a correctness gap.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
1. Keep the replay cache as the default residual path. Rejected: it is not scientifically required, its scratch footprint exceeds the input, and it duplicates the operator in a second record-based implementation.
  2. Keep the earlier resource authority and trim it. Rejected: its admission decisions reduce to one arithmetic formula, and every other structure was write-only.
  3. Keep the architecture checker and update its ratchets per commit. Rejected: it enforced programme process, not architecture.
  4. (Amendment of 2026-10-25.) Keep the model free of workspace dependencies and convert between vocabularies at the application, or admit each definitional dependency into each crate's exact set. Rejected: the first keeps two types for one meaning; the second makes every use of a unit or measure a policy edit while guarding nothing, since a definitional crate brings in no persistence, I/O or device. casa-numerics and casa-fft are algorithms rather than definitions and stay listed where used.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text: This decision is enforced by: - tests: T0 operator laws and T1 end-to-end capability tests (TESTING.md "Imaging tiers and evidence") - lint/import/dependency rules: scripts/check-imaging-dependencies.py (crate edges, definitional crates closed and free of I/O, device APIs only in casa-imaging-metal, no std::env or eprintln! in library crates, no content hashing in imaging crates) - CI checks: just arch-check - review trigger: the imaging code rules in ARCHITECTURE.md for every imaging change; adding a definitional crate (decision 10) is the owner's decision

docs.title: ADR-0017: Rust computation and CASA-shaped Python interfaces
docs.text:
Status: accepted Date: 2026-11-12 Truth class: normative Supersedes: ADR-0018 and ADR-0019; their original text is in Git history.

The product is the casars Python package and the cataloged headless task executables. Use existing Python tools for notebooks, interactive inspection, and plot rendering. Rust produces typed plot data. casa-rs ships no separate GUI, terminal UI, session provider, or launcher.

  • Rust owns computation, persistence, and parallelism, including the orchestration CASA implements in Python. Keep Rust APIs idiomatic.
  • casars.tasks presents CASA's names, signatures, and return shapes. Python converts arguments and results, maps errors, and starts each task's executable directly. The shared task runtime owns defaults, normalization, and validation (ADR-0006). Ordinary Python task calls do not load or write managed Last state.
  • casars.tools exposes CASA-named PyO3 classes through casars._core, the sole native extension. Declare signatures and effective defaults in Rust and compare with the installed CASA binding. Share conversions. CASA-independent resource controls are keyword-only constructor arguments, with no environment lookup. Tool state is Send; release the GIL during disk access, array copies, and long calls. Legacy casars.data.Image and Table are tracked separately in #839.
  • Do not ship casatasks or casatools alias packages; they would shadow CASA. CASA itself is used only for tests and evidence.

The Python package and task CLI tests cover the boundary and compare the observable behavior with CASA. See Provider Contracts for invocation and discovery details.

docs.title: ADR-0020: Build for one investigator
docs.text:
Status: accepted Date: 2026-11-12 Truth class: normative

casa-rs is in development with no downstream users. Optimize the time it takes one investigator to get a scientifically sound result and to understand or change the code that produced it.

  • Compute efficiently. Keep one native Rust path organized around the mathematics. Measure the affected computation, memory, and I/O before adding complexity for speed. Use focused regression tests and CASA comparisons to defend the result.
  • Keep scientific data interoperable. Preserve the ability to exchange CASA/casacore data in both directions, and preserve MSv4 conformance and exchange where supported. These are external data requirements. CASA is a test oracle; casa-rs performs its own computation. Record justified numerical divergences from CASA.
  • Keep local interfaces current. Change casa-rs-owned APIs, settings, and developer artifacts directly when a simpler design serves current work. A saved parameter file can carry one current version marker and give a clear error when stale. Do not maintain migrations, legacy aliases, append-only version histories, or support layers for hypothetical future users. Revisit only when a real user or workflow needs them.
  • Keep the work record small. An issue states the outcome and remaining work; its PR and executable tests carry the evidence. Reuse a single handoff for long work. Use ADRs for durable architectural decisions, consolidated when they overlap. Scale review to the scientific, data, and implementation risk. Keep decisions the owner already made in the record without opening a second approval or tracking process.

This replaces ADR-0006's requirement to preserve old casa-rs profile contracts and their history. It does not change CASA/MSv4 formats or scientific acceptance.

docs.title: ADR-NNNN: Decision title
docs.text:
Status: proposed Date: YYYY-MM-DD Truth class: normative

Describe the concrete problem, the decision, and any tradeoff the next maintainer needs to know. Link an existing test or architecture reference when it helps. Name any superseded decision.

docs.title: MeasurementSet boundary: rules
docs.text:
Truth class: normative Last reality check: 2026-11-02

casa-rs reads and writes MeasurementSet v2 and XRADIO MSv4 through one boundary. casa-observation holds the shared contract: the catalogue, the access request and its estimate, the traversal that delivers VisibilityBatches, scientific groups and their completion, the buffer pool, and update sessions. casa_ms::observation_io holds the adapters behind it: opening, the MSv2 and MSv4 stores, the converter and the MSv2 creation plan. Their rustdoc is the contract: what each type holds, what each store delivers, and what it refuses. This file keeps only what the code does not state: the rules that bind changes to the boundary, the owner decisions behind it, and what each capability not yet offered must meet. Moving the remaining consumers onto the boundary is tracked in #1055.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Rule Required behavior C1: source independence No physical row IDs, Zarr keys, storage managers or MS-version branches in numerical processing loops. Only opening, creation, capabilities and diagnostics see the store. C2: faithful values Coordinates and references are native casa-rs Measures types and views, accepted directly by its conversion APIs. Canonical units; explicit frames and precision; native flag and weight semantics; full data-group association; ordered baselines. No silent scientific transform: what the profile cannot represent is refused. C3: layout independence Sample topology, memory layout, scientific grouping and storage chunking stay separate. C4: bounded ownership Every live payload, index, decode buffer, cache, packed copy and queue is admitted; borrowed views cannot outlive or refill their storage. Independent work retires separately; shared storage stays live until its last use. C5: invertible updates A sample-preserving reorder or selection keeps a checked inverse map to the store; a reduction does not, and its result goes to an explicit output. Shared variables have an explicit mutation scope. C6: honest guarantees Unsupported profiles, layouts and native features, and non-atomic writes, are explicit typed refusals. C7: bulk execution Bind numeric kind, layout and invariant context outside scalar loops; use native array views and family-specific kernels. No per-value object allocation, virtual dispatch, coordinate reconstruction or repeated setup or provider lookup.

Moving a consumer onto the boundary deletes its old route in the same change: no compatibility layer and no second production route kept for comparison (a baseline build serves that). A consumer has not moved while a wrapper still leaks physical rows or DATA_DESC_ID into its algorithm.

docs.title: Owner decisions in force
docs.text:
• Formats (2026-10-23): MSv2 and MSv4 (XRADIO schema 4.0.1 on local Zarr v3). MSv3 is deferred until a concrete dataset or producer needs it; it then comes as a named profile with its own independent producer and reader checks, never inferred from a product name. Object stores, MSv4 image persistence and Zarr v2 are separate later work.
  • Shape (2026-10-24): the interface takes MSv4's native shape, and the MSv2 adapter assembles MSv2 into it at opening.
  • Arrays (2026-10-24): numerical arrays and views are ndarray's, under thin domain types that carry axis meaning, Measures metadata, and flag and weight meaning.
  • Measures (2026-10-24): the boundary uses casa-types Measures and quanta types directly, with no observation-specific measure vocabulary, and the Measures APIs may be reworked for bulk use (below).

docs.title: Capabilities not yet offered
docs.text:
Each is refused today with a typed error, or offered only in part. It is offered when its obligation is met.

Capability Obligation Units and conversions requested at binding A requested unit holds for the view's bound scope; conversions fused with the fill; identity conversions copy nothing; weights transform as w / \|a\|² under an amplitude scale a. Precision other than Complex<f32>, bool, f32, f64 Native precision, lossless widening or approved narrowing per role, charged and fused with decode; the writer checks representability. Real-valued data (FLOAT_DATA, MSv4 SPECTRUM) Its own typed variant under its own profile, never reinterpreted as visibilities. More than one data group per traversal Each group keeps its UVW and field and source context, and explicit alias relationships to the others. Unknown occupancy Representable in the batch; conversion to rows resolves it by a declared policy or reports the ambiguity, never inventing an MSv2 row; writing into holes needs an explicit fill policy. Native flags: bitmask dtypes, reason bits, FLAG_CATEGORY, row flags as their own view Dtype and reason bits preserved on writes; generic flagging bound to the store's actual unspecified bit; clearing an effective flag never clears unknown reasons, FLAG_ROW or FLAG_CATEGORY. Per-cell weight fallback An undefined sigma or weight cell falls back per cell, recorded per cell, instead of failing the read. Updates beyond the write-back sessions Bit flags and flag categories; structural writes (a new MSv4 data group, or rebinding a group to its own copy of a shared variable); a composition rule or refusal for conflicting queued patches; per-batch MSv2 planning; a process killed during MSv4 chunk replacement, ENOSPC and stray temporary files, checked by reopening selected and unselected sentinels. Creation beyond the MSv4 writer and the MSv2 creation plan An MSv4 from several observations; failure injection at publication; the writer's held chunk admitted with the producer's batches; omitting padding without a counting pass. Calibration binding in production gainfield and nearest-field selection through bound fields; bandpass and other per-channel tables; tables solved over combined windows; FEED and receptor association; field binding tolerant of ephemeris fields. Ephemerides XRADIO's optional ephemeris variables carried through the boundary and the converter (#998). Baseline-dependent polarization (polarization_mixed) A checked per-baseline basis mapping in the catalogue. TIME_CENTROID_EXTRA_PRECISION The residual carried through the epoch view, slicing, packing and writing; adding it to a large f64 is no substitute. Four-dimensional EFFECTIVE_INTEGRATION_TIME Per-channel exposure in the batch's timing. Resource admission of the whole read and write path Everything a traversal or writer holds is admitted through the runtime's HostResources with cancellable backpressure, including zarrs codec scratch (found or conservatively bounded before work, failing with the minimum it needs) and store caches bounded in bytes. Decode on the admitted executor Executing threads and live codec buffers counted on the real decode path; no fall-through to a global pool; in-partition parallel decode (#1016). Bulk Measures conversion Below.

Updates are addressed in the store's native domain. A patch's affected extent and its conflicts are resolved after expanding data-group aliases and broadcast aliases: setting one channel's effective weight where MSv2 holds one WEIGHT for every channel needs an explicit whole-scalar scope, a channel-resolved destination created under bounded memory, or refusal. Calibration owns any reduction of channel weights into a row WEIGHT and submits both patches; storage never invents that inverse. There is no default last-writer-wins.

The MSv4 write guarantees (per-object atomic replacement, staging and publication, no cross-process lock protocol) and any change to ADR-0008's locking and partial-failure rules need a reviewed new ADR before they are advertised as persistent guarantees.

docs.title: Bulk Measures conversion
docs.text:
Every supported Measures and quanta family offers bulk operation, present and future: directions, epochs and time scales, positions, baselines and UVW, frequencies, radial velocities and Doppler conventions, magnetic and other vector measures, and unit conversions. LSRK↔TOPO is one example, not the acceptance. The shape is prepare, then apply: - bind the route, units and policy once per conversion request; - prepare context-dependent terms (matrices, factors, interpolation state) at their valid scope, in bounded groups where the context varies; - apply to numeric slices into reusable buffers, keeping the per-value nonlinear or iterative work each family needs, with no per-value object, allocation, lock or route search.

A prepared transform is tied to every input that affects it, so a context change invalidates it; equal reference enums with different contexts are not an identity. CASA-compatible ordered interpolation keeps its sequence across batches and workers. Acceptance for each family: consumers use it directly; scalar, bulk and CASA agree to that family's tolerances; and timings, with binding and preparation reported apart from apply, are compared against both the scalar path and any already-prepared production path.

docs.title: Python Support
docs.text:
casa-rs-python installs as casars and separates four public concerns:

  • casars.data provides in-process access to persistent CASA-style images and tables.
  • casars.tasks provides higher-level task wrappers, each of which starts its task's own executable.
  • casars.tools provides CASA's tools as classes under CASA's names, with CASA's methods, parameter order and defaults, so a CASA script changes only its imports (ADR-0017): simulator (CASA's sm), measures (me), quanta (qa), componentlist (cl), image (ia), coordsys (cs), table (tb), msmetadata (msmd) and ms. Each has every method of CASA 6.7.6.14's binding; a method casa-rs does not implement yet raises NotImplementedError naming the issue that records it. A tool's constructor takes only casa-rs's controls, keyword-only: simulator(*, memory_budget=None, backend='auto', workers=None) caps the memory close holds (bytes), names the device to predict on ('auto', 'cpu' or 'metal') and the threads to keep busy; None takes the machine's balanced share, and the MeasurementSet written is the same whatever the controls. casars.simutil provides the parts of CASA's simutil helper class (casatasks.private.simutil, not a tool) that sm scripts and simobserve use: readantenna, the mosaic pointings (calc_pointings2, pointing files), the direction helpers, noisetemp, bandname, polsettings, the baseline helpers, and the sky-model helpers modifymodel and flatimage, and the analysis helpers ismstp, cellsize, statim and convimage, the geodesy helpers, and msg, the report helpers, dir_s2m, is4d, spectral and setcfg. Its plotting methods newfig, nextfig, endfig, plotants, ephemeris and the default statim(plot=True) use the plot extra. Rust prepares all scientific arrays; Matplotlib draws onto the current figure and panel, so scripts can annotate and save them as in CASA. Its other methods have CASA's signatures and raise NotImplementedError naming the issue that records them. from casars import simutil is its public import.
  • casars.parameters is the accepted common API for typed task profiles described by ADR-0006.

The generic casars.tasks.run() entry point accepts every catalog task. Every task is also exposed exactly once as casars.tasks.<task> through a generated CASA-named function that takes CASA's parameters. These functions share the Rust-owned parameter and result contracts. A call resolves its parameters in Rust, starts the task's executable as a child process with --json-run -, passes the task's log lines to sys.stderr as they arrive. A task whose surface names its CASA task (every task but the casa-rs tasks calibrate, msexplore and msconvert, and plotms) has CASA's exact signature and returns CASA's value; the others return a TaskCompletion. A task that refuses its parameters raises casars.tasks.TaskParameterError, a ValueError, and one that does not succeed casars.tasks.TaskExecutionError. The executable is the task's CASARS_<APP>_BIN override when it is set, else the one in a suite's bin/ (CASARS_SUITE_ROOT, or the suite the package was installed into), else, for a package built from a checkout, that checkout's build (Compatibility). The in-process casars.data, casars.tools and casars.simutil need no executables.

casars.data is stateful and file-backed. It is intended for interoperability with the Python ecosystem through NumPy-native reads and writes. For images, the current object surface includes pixel-slice writes on existing persistent images; image creation and coordinate-system authoring remain outside the v1 object contract.

docs.title: Parameter profiles
docs.text:
The accepted profile API is shared with the task executables' command lines:

from casars import parameters, tasks

p = parameters.load("profiles/target-imaging.toml", workspace="project")
p.update(niter=20000, threshold="1mJy")

result = tasks.run("tclean", p)   # runs in the draft's workspace, project/

A loaded profile also runs through a CASA-named wrapper, in the current directory: tasks.tclean(**parameters.load("profiles/target-imaging.toml")).

The call saves no Last profile. parameters.last(...) reads the Last that a command-line run saved.

parameters.defaults(surface, ...) and parameters.last(surface, ...) create the other common source types. The resulting TaskParameters supports mapping updates, reset, reload, sparse TOML save, and run. Rust remains the sole parser, normalizer, validator, and sparse renderer.

casars.tasks is generated from the catalog's task definitions and supplies one CASA-named wrapper and typing stub per task. A task that mimics CASA's has CASA 6.7.6.14's signature, defaults and return value; the casa-rs tasks (calibrate, msexplore, msconvert) and plotms take keywords with an unset sentinel instead of copying catalog defaults into Python.

Python binds Rust through PyO3 alone, in one native module, casars._core. It carries task parameters, task results, MeasurementSet plot documents, the classes in casars.tools, and casars.simutil. Use casars.tools.image for NumPy pixel access and native image editing.

docs.title: Plotting and image inspection
docs.text:
casa-rs does not rasterise plots. Numeric MeasurementSet plot documents are available as casars.data.measurement_set_plot(...) and are drawn with Matplotlib by casars.data.plot_matplotlib(...). casars.imexplore reads image planes as NumPy arrays (casars.imexplore.data(...)) and draws them with Matplotlib (casars.imexplore.imshow(...)).

Install casa-rs-python[plot] for simulation graphics. tasks.simobserve honours graphics='file', 'screen', 'both' and 'none': it saves the model/pointing and observation figures, displays them, does both, or skips graphics. Figures include the complete model and UV samples. The interferometric quick PSF is a CASA image beside the MeasurementSet. The generic tasks.run('simobserve', ...) completion lists PNG files after they have been rendered. Displaying figures uses the Python session's Matplotlib backend.

See Task Parameter Profiles for sparse TOML, managed Last paths, source precedence, and examples.

Tagged releases build Python artifacts for Linux x86_64 and macOS arm64, plus a source distribution for environments that need to build from source. For suite installation and shell PATH setup, see Install.

docs.title: Common parameter API
docs.text:
ADR-0006 defines the common API for current task profiles:

casars.parameters.defaults(surface, *, workspace=None)
casars.parameters.last(surface, *, workspace=None)
casars.parameters.last_successful(surface, *, workspace=None)
casars.parameters.load(path, *, workspace=None)

TaskParameters.update(**values)
TaskParameters.reset(name)
TaskParameters.reload()
TaskParameters.save(path)
TaskParameters.run(**values)

casars.tasks.run(task, parameters=None, /, *, workspace=None, **values)
casars.tasks.<casa_task>(casa_parameters..., *, casa_rs_controls...)
casars.tasks.<task>(**parameters)

A task call starts the task's own executable. tasks.run returns a TaskCompletion (task, command, workspace, returncode, stdout, the reply; stderr, the log; provider_invocation, status, message, parameter, value, CASA's return value; and result, the declared products). A wrapper whose surface names its CASA task (every task but the casa-rs tasks calibrate, msexplore and msconvert, and plotms) has CASA's signature, positional or by keyword with CASA's defaults, then casa-rs's own controls, keyword-only, and returns CASA's value, with NumPy arrays where CASA returns them. A parameter casa-rs does not implement yet is taken only at CASA's default; its docstring names the issue. The other wrappers take keyword arguments and return the TaskCompletion.

On a single MeasurementSet, split and mstransform accept named fields and spectral windows, antenna baselines, scan predicates, calendar times, observation IDs and intents, array IDs, UV distances, and feed pairs. Channel selectors can include disjoint ranges and strides. Use a spectral-window qualifier such as correlation="SPW0:XX,YY" to select correlation products within a window. The CASA comparison checks unaveraged visibilities, flags, weights, and remapped metadata. Remaining behaviors are tracked in #978.

For stored visibilities, datacolumn="model" and "corrected" copy the selected source into DATA. Combined layouts retain the named columns. "all" copies the available physical visibility columns, including FLOAT_DATA and LAG_DATA when present.

A value the contract refuses raises ValueError before anything starts, or TypeError for a value of the wrong type. A task that refuses its parameters raises TaskParameterError, a ValueError, and one that starts and does not succeed TaskExecutionError, a RuntimeError; the .completion of either says how it ended. TaskBinaryNotFoundError (a FileNotFoundError) names what the executable search lacked; TaskInvocationError means the process could not start; TaskResultError means a success's result was malformed.

A Python task call saves no Last or Last Successful profile; those record command-line runs. The CASA-named wrappers take the surface's parameters. A profile runs through one as tasks.gaincal(**parameters.load(path)), since a draft, as a mapping, holds the parameters that have a value.

TaskParameters (a SurfaceParameters constrained to a task definition) is mapping-like and retains value origins and validation diagnostics. Saving writes only required values and differences from current defaults. Surface definitions and defaults are read from the same Rust catalog that the task executables' command lines use.

The catalog-driven generic runner and generated CASA-named functions are the only public task path. Generated conveniences live directly in casars.tasks; their checked .pyi file is regenerated from crates/casa-provider-contracts/resources/parameter-surfaces.json.

def plot_matplotlib(
    plot_data: MeasurementSetPlotData,
    *,
    figure: Any = None,
) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    """Render MeasurementSet plot data into editable Matplotlib objects."""

    try:
        import matplotlib.pyplot  # noqa: F401
    except ImportError as error:  # pragma: no cover - environment dependent
        raise ImportError(
            "Matplotlib plotting requires `pip install casa-rs-python[plot]`"
        ) from error
    from ._plot_document import render_document

    document = {
        "title": plot_data.title, "show_legend": plot_data.show_legend,
        "panels": [{
            "title": panel.title,
            "axes": [{"label": axis.label, "lower": axis.lower, "upper": axis.upper} for axis in panel.axes],
            "layers": [{
                "kind": "scatter", "title": series.label,
                "x_values": series.x, "y_values": series.y,
                "symbol_size": 9, "opacity": 1,
            } for series in panel.series],
        } for panel in plot_data.panels],
    }
    if not document["panels"]:
        document["panels"] = [{"title": "", "axes": [], "layers": []}]
    return render_document(document, figure=figure, use_native_limits=False)

docs.title: TaskCompletion dataclass
docs.text:
One finished task process: how it ended and what it wrote.

status is the task's outcome: succeeded, refused (its parameters, before it changed anything), failed, interrupted, signalled, or malformed_reply. stdout is the task's reply and stderr its log, which was also written to sys.stderr as the task ran.

Source code in crates/casars-python/python/casars/tasks/_runner.py 
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class TaskCompletion:
    """One finished task process: how it ended and what it wrote.

    ``status`` is the task's outcome: ``succeeded``, ``refused`` (its
    parameters, before it changed anything), ``failed``, ``interrupted``,
    ``signalled``, or ``malformed_reply``. ``stdout`` is the task's reply and
    ``stderr`` its log, which was also written to ``sys.stderr`` as the task
    ran.
    """

    task: str
    command: tuple[str, ...]
    workspace: Path
    returncode: int
    stdout: str
    stderr: str
    provider_invocation: ProviderInvocation
    status: str
    message: str | None
    parameter: str | None
    value: Any
    result: object | None

    @property
    def successful(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the task succeeded."""

        return self.status == "succeeded"

    @property
    def products(self) -> tuple[object, ...]:
        """Typed contract-declared products from the Rust completion decoder."""

        if self.result is None:
            return ()
        return tuple(self.result.products)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

    def describe(self) -> str:
        """One line saying how the task ended."""

        at = f" (parameter {self.parameter!r})" if self.parameter else ""
        if self.status == "succeeded":
            return f"{self.task} succeeded"
        if self.status == "refused":
            return f"{self.task} refused its parameters{at}: {self.message}"
        if self.status == "failed":
            return f"{self.task} failed{at}: {self.message}"
        if self.status == "interrupted":
            return f"{self.task} was interrupted: {self.message}"
        detail = self.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-1:] or ["no log output"]
        if self.status == "signalled":
            return f"{self.task} was ended by signal {-self.returncode}: {detail[0]}"
        return f"{self.task} gave no valid reply ({self.message}): {detail[0]}"

docs.title: TaskParameterError
docs.text:
Bases: ValueError

Raised when a task refuses its parameters before it changes anything; completion says why (#931).

A value the parameter contract refuses raises ValueError, or TypeError for a value of the wrong type, before the task starts; this is the refusal of a value only the task itself can judge, such as an input that does not exist. CASA raises AssertionError from its generated parameter checker in both cases.

Source code in crates/casars-python/python/casars/tasks/_runner.py 
class TaskParameterError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a task refuses its parameters before it changes anything;
    ``completion`` says why (#931).

    A value the parameter contract refuses raises ``ValueError``, or
    ``TypeError`` for a value of the wrong type, before the task starts; this
    is the refusal of a value only the task itself can judge, such as an
    input that does not exist. CASA raises ``AssertionError`` from its
    generated parameter checker in both cases.
    """

    def __init__(self, completion: TaskCompletion) -> None:
        self.completion = completion
        message = completion.message or ""
        # The native front end marks the narrow CASA-compatible missing-path
        # case with its exact wording; retain it for scripts that match CASA.
        prefix = f"the {completion.parameter} parameter must be a path that exists ('"
        if completion.parameter and message.startswith(prefix) and message.endswith("' does not exist)"):
            super().__init__(message)
        else:
            super().__init__(completion.describe())

docs.text:
Run any catalog task, with CASA-named values.

parameters is a draft to start from, such as a loaded profile; the contract's defaults otherwise. The task runs in workspace: the draft's, or the current directory. Values are normalized and checked by Rust before the task starts, so a value the contract refuses raises ValueError and starts nothing.

The call loads and saves no Last profile: those record command-line runs. :meth:TaskParameters.last and :meth:TaskParameters.write_last stay explicit. CASA's own parameters, such as overwrite, are the consent to replace or change data. A task that refuses its parameters raises :class:TaskParameterError, a ValueError, and one that starts and does not succeed :class:TaskExecutionError, a RuntimeError; an interrupt (Ctrl-C) is passed to the task, which is given time to stop, and then raised here.

def run(
    task: str,
    parameters: SurfaceParameters | None = None,
    /,
    *,
    workspace: StrPath | None = None,
    **values: ParameterData,
) -> TaskCompletion:
    """Run any catalog task, with CASA-named ``values``.

    ``parameters`` is a draft to start from, such as a loaded profile; the
    contract's defaults otherwise. The task runs in ``workspace``: the
    draft's, or the current directory. Values are normalized and checked by
    Rust before the task starts, so a value the contract refuses raises
    ``ValueError`` and starts nothing.

    The call loads and saves no Last profile: those record command-line runs.
    :meth:`TaskParameters.last` and :meth:`TaskParameters.write_last` stay
    explicit. CASA's own parameters, such as ``overwrite``, are the consent
    to replace or change data. A task that refuses its parameters raises
    :class:`TaskParameterError`, a ``ValueError``, and one that starts and
    does not succeed :class:`TaskExecutionError`, a ``RuntimeError``; an
    interrupt (Ctrl-C) is passed to the task, which is given time to stop,
    and then raised here.
    """

    return _run_task(task, parameters, workspace, values)

docs.title: casars.tools
docs.text:
CASA tools for casa-rs, under CASA's class names (ADR-0017).

A CASA script changes only its imports::

from casars.tools import measures, quanta, simulator

me = measures()
sm = simulator()
sm.open("sim.ms")
sm.setconfig(referencelocation=me.observatory("VLA"), ...)

Each tool is a class in the casars._core extension, with CASA's method names, parameter order and defaults declared in Rust. This module adds only the module path.

docs.title: casars.simutil
docs.text:
CASA's simutil helper class for casa-rs.

A CASA script changes only its import::

from casars import simutil

u = simutil.simutil()
x, y, z, d, padnames, antnames, telescope, posobs = u.readantenna("vla.d.cfg")
pointings = u.calc_pointings2("10arcsec", ["60arcsec", "40arcsec"], maptype="ALMA",
                              direction="J2000 18h00m00 -23d00m00")

In CASA, simutil is a Python helper class in the private simutil module of CASA's task package, not a CASA tool, so it is not in casars.tools or in the object-surface bundle. casa-rs implements, in Rust (the class lives in the casars._core extension, ADR-0017), the parts sm scripts and simobserve use: - readantenna; - the pointings calc_pointings2, read_pointings and write_pointings; - the direction helpers direction_splitter, average_direction, median_direction, dir_m2s, wrapang, isquantity and isdirection; - noisetemp, bandname and polsettings; - itrf2loc, baselineLengths and approxBeam; - the sky-model helpers modifymodel and flatimage; - the analysis helpers ismstp, cellsize, statim and convimage; - newfig, nextfig, endfig, plotants and ephemeris, with native scientific preparation and Matplotlib presentation (install the plot extra); statim draws its complete plane by default; - the geodesy helpers, getdatum through itrf2locname; - msg, the report file (isreport, openreport, closereport), dir_s2m, is4d, spectral and setcfg.

CASA's other public methods exist with CASA's signatures and raise NotImplementedError naming issue #1053, which records which ones casa-rs will implement.

casars.simutil is the class's public import: CASA's private path would mislabel a supported entry point.

docs.title: Data API
docs.text:
Use casars.tools to work with image and table files in process. casars.data provides data helpers and publishes the native object protocol.

  • protocol_info() returns the stable object protocol descriptor.
  • schema_bundle() returns the canonical schema bundle for the casars.tools classes.

docs.title: Create and edit a native CASA image
docs.text:
Use casars.tools.image to create a native image and edit its pixels and coordinates through the CASA Python interface:

import numpy as np
from casars.tools import image

ia = image()
ia.fromshape("example.im", [4, 3])
ia.putchunk(np.array([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]]), blc=[1, 0])
cs = ia.coordsys()
cs.setreferencepixel([1.5, 1.0])
ia.setcoordsys(cs.torecord())
ia.setbrightnessunit("Jy/pixel")
ia.done()

Use ia.addnoise(seeds=[1, 2]) to add reproducible normal noise. Pass type and pars for another CASA noise distribution, or zero=True to replace the selected pixels with noise. The region selects the lattice section and the image's validity mask is retained.

A coordinate tool returned by ia.coordsys() has its own state. Inspect the direction axes with cs.findcoordinate("direction")["pixel"] or identify the coordinate for a particular axis with cs.findaxis(world=False, axis=0). cs.names() and cs.units() follow world-axis order. Use cs.copy() to edit a separate coordinate system, then pass its record to ia.setcoordsys() to persist the edits to the image.

Use cs.projection() to inspect the direction projection and cs.referencecode() to list stored frames in coordinate order. cs.getconversiontype("direction") reports the current conversion frame. Use cs.lineartransform(type) and cs.setlineartransform(type, matrix) to read or edit the linear coupling between axes of the selected coordinate. On a sampled tabular coordinate, saving its record folds the current transform into the lookup values used on reopen. Use cs.setnames(values) to replace the world-axis labels in order, or pass type to replace one coordinate's labels. cs.setstokes(values) sets the polarization labels in pixel order.

Use cs.referencevalue() and cs.increment() to read the world-axis reference values and spacing. Pass type to select a coordinate, or combine n, q, s, and m in format to request numbers, quantities, display strings, and CASA measures. Use cs.setreferencevalue(values) and cs.setincrement(values) to edit the coordinate record. Numeric values use the declared world-axis units. Quantity strings can specify their own units, and type selects one coordinate. Use cs.setreferencelocation(pixel, world, mask) to set pixel and world references together. A full-length boolean mask can limit the edit to specific axes. Stokes references stay fixed. Use cs.setunits(values) to change the declared units and rescale the coordinate values. On a selected linear or tabular coordinate, overwrite=True relabels units while keeping the numeric values. Use cs.setrestfrequency(values, which=0, append=False) to choose the active spectral rest frequency. Floating-point inputs use the coordinate's unit. Pass quantity strings or a quantity record to supply units explicitly. With append=True, which indexes the combined old and new list. Use cs.frequencytovelocity(values) and cs.velocitytofrequency(values) to convert relative to the active rest frequency. The default convention is radio Doppler and the default velocity unit is km/s. Pass doppler, velunit, or frequnit to choose other conventions or units. Use cs.frequencytofrequency(values, velocity="10km/s") to shift a vector by a velocity. A dimensionless velocity is a fraction of the speed of light.

To build a coordinate system without an image, call tools.coordsys().newcoordsys(direction=True, spectral=True, stokes=["I", "Q"]). Use addcoordinate to append axes and fromrecord to restore a coordinate record. Pass cs.torecord() as the csys argument to ia.fromshape or ia.fromarray. The coordinate record must describe each image axis.

Use cs.setepoch(epoch) to store an epoch measure record. cs.epoch() returns the epoch in days with its reference code and any reference offset.

Use cs.setobserver(name) and cs.settelescope(name) to update observation metadata. An unknown telescope name is stored and the setter returns False. The record retains the last known telescope position.

Use cs.toworld(pixel) and cs.topixel(world) for a single absolute coordinate. toworld supports the same numeric, quantity, string, and measure format letters as referencevalue. Use cs.toworldmany(pixels)["numeric"] and cs.topixelmany(world)["numeric"] to convert a floating-point matrix with one point per column. The rows follow the coordinate system's axis order. World values use the units reported by cs.units(). NumPy float32, float64, longdouble, longlong, and ulonglong matrices are converted to double precision, as in CASA.

Use cs.torel(value, isworld=1) for world offsets from the reference and cs.toabs to recover absolute positions. Use isworld=0 for pixels, or pass the tagged record from a coordinate conversion. The corresponding torelmany and toabsmany methods take matrices with one coordinate per column.

Use ia.toworld(pixels, format="nqsm") to convert one image position. Each format letter requests numeric values, quantities, strings, or measures. Pass dovelocity=False to omit spectral velocities from the measure record. Pass one of these representations to ia.topixel(world) to obtain the zero-based pixel coordinates in its numeric field. ia.coordmeasures(pixel) returns world measures and the pixel's intensity and validity. Pass dframe or sframe to request specific direction or spectral frames.

Use ia.open("example.im") to reopen the product. Use outfile="" with fromshape or fromarray for a temporary image. Use ia.setmiscinfo(record) to replace an image’s miscellaneous metadata, and ia.sethistory(origin, messages) to append provenance. For an image with stored restoring beams, ia.restoringbeam() reads the beam quantities and ia.restoringbeam(mbret="matrix") reads a per-plane beam grid. Use ia.beamforconvolvedsize(source, convolved) to calculate the Gaussian beam needed to reach a target resolution. Use ia.deconvolvefrombeam(source, beam) to recover a fitted source size and see whether the source is resolved. Pass the major axis, minor axis and position angle as angular quantity strings. Use ia.rotatebeam("15deg") to rotate all stored restoring beams. On a directly opened FITS image, the rotation applies only to the open tool. Each open tool keeps its own view of the restoring beams. Reopen a native image to read beam changes made through another tool. Use ia.summary(list=False) to read the shape, coordinate axes, mask names and restoring beams and return the two report messages. The default list=True sends the report to the logger. Use ia.makecomplex("output.im", "imaginary.im") to combine the attached real image with a conformant real image of matching precision. A supplied region selects the same section from both inputs. The output copies the real image's metadata and uses the intersection of the input masks. Use ia.isconform("other.im") to check whether a float image has the same shape and compatible coordinates as a native float or complex image. Use ia.convertflux(value, major, minor) to convert a Gaussian's integrated flux to peak brightness. Pass topeak=False for the reverse conversion and select the channel and polarization for an image with per-plane beams. Use ia.deconvolvecomponentlist(cl.torecord()) to remove the restoring beam from Gaussian components on an attached float or complex image. Point components are returned intact. For a per-plane beam grid, select the channel and polarization on each nondegenerate axis. Use ia.modify(cl.torecord(), subtract=False) to add a component model to a float image. The default subtracts the model. A region limits the pixel section. CASA validates an explicit mask and applies the edit to the stored pixels in that section. Use ia.imageconcat(infiles=["a.im", "b.im"], axis=0) for a temporary concatenation, or give outfile for a native image. The default concatenation axis is spectral. reorder=True sorts inputs along the selected coordinate. Virtual modes are tracked in #1749. Use ia.replacemaskedpixels(pixels=0) to replace invalid pixels in an attached float or complex image. Use update=True to validate the selected native pixel mask after replacement. Use ia.set(pixels=3.5) to fill the attached float image. pixels can also be a scalar lattice expression. Use region to restrict the edit and set pixelmask=0 to invalidate the selected pixels or pixelmask=1 to validate them in the default mask.

Use ia.calc(pixels=...) to evaluate a numeric expression into a writable float or complex image. An existing default mask limits writes to its valid pixels. The operation preserves the destination coordinates and metadata. Use ia.imagecalc(outfile=..., pixels=...) to create a native product with the expression's validity mask. An empty outfile returns a read-only image whose pixel reads evaluate the expression against its source images. Use prec="double" for double precision or imagemd to copy metadata from a separate image. Use ia.calcmask(...) to save a Boolean expression as a named native image mask. Expressions can combine real, complex, and FITS images and read named masks using mask("image.im:maskname") where CASA accepts that source type.

Use ia.fitsheader() to inspect the FITS header for a float image without exporting the pixels. Pass exclude="HISTORY" to omit the log from the returned dictionary. Use retstr=True to return the complete string of 80-byte cards. Use ia.tofits("example.fits") to write FITS from an attached float image. It accepts region and mask selection, scaled integer pixels with bitpix=16, spectral velocity or wavelength axes, and export axis ordering controls. Pass history=False to omit the image log from the output.

For a native image, ia.haslock() reports its read and write locks in that order. Use ia.lock(writelock=True, nattempts=1) to try for a write lock without waiting. ia.unlock() flushes pending changes and releases the lock. putchunk normally releases the lock after writing. Pass locking=False to keep it while making several updates.

Use ia.putregion(pixels, pixelmask, region) to edit pixels and validity in the same region. The default usemask=True skips masked pixels after applying the supplied mask. Pass replicate=True to fill omitted axes and use the region's stride.

Use ia.open("example.fits") to read pixels and their validity mask directly from a FITS file. Metadata edits apply for the life of the attachment. Use ia.subimage(...) on that attachment for a temporary or native section with its WCS and validity mask. With wantreturn=False and an output path, the tool publishes the section and returns a detached image tool. Use ia.rename("new-name.fits") to move an attached FITS file. The tool reopens the moved file and reads its stored metadata again.

Use ia.insert("source.im") to place a source image by aligning reference pixels, or supply locate to set the lower corner. A region record may select a strided section. CRTF text uses the attached destination's coordinates before applying the selection to the source. An existing writable destination mask receives the source validity over the inserted section.

Use ia.fromfits("example.im", "example.fits") to import a FITS image as a writable native CASA image for pixel edits. whichhdu selects the image HDU and whichrep selects the coordinate representation. zeroblanks=True writes zero at blank pixels while preserving their invalid mask values. ia.newimagefromfits(...) returns a separate image tool.

ia.torecord() captures the pixels, coordinates and image info, including restoring beams. ia.fromrecord(record) restores a temporary image. Pass an output path to write a native CASA image. As in CASA, restoring a record uses single-precision pixels and starts a new history.

Use ia.fromimage(outfile="copy.im", infile="example.im") to copy an image with its coordinates, active pixel mask, metadata and history. Use newimagefromimage to keep the current attachment and receive a separate tool. An absolute CASA LCSlicer region selects a pixel box and its stride. The copy retains the selected frequencies and restoring beams. Additional region forms are tracked in #1625.

Use ia.getregion(region=...) to read that same selection. Pass getmask=True to read validity, mask to apply a lattice expression, or axes to average the valid pixels along selected axes. Use ia.boundingbox(region=...) to inspect the inclusive pixel corners, stride, sampled shape and world coordinates of the corners. Use ia.crop(axes=...) to trim fully masked edge planes along the selected axes. The method applies the region and optional mask expression before finding the crop bounds. Pass region=[] when using box, chans, or stokes separately. Use ia.decimate(axis=..., factor=..., method="copy") to keep every nth plane. With method="mean", it averages valid samples in each complete group and drops the trailing partial group. Use ia.rebin(outfile="", bin=[...]) to average valid pixels over bins on several axes. Trailing partial bins are included unless crop=True. A bin with no valid pixels is masked. Binning supports real and complex single-precision images.

ia.statistics() returns statistics over a real native CASA image, an attached FITS image, or a temporary image. Pass axes for per-plane results, region or mask to select pixels, and robust=True for the median, quartiles, and median absolute deviation. The tool supports classical, biweight, Chauvenet, fit-to-half and hinges-and-fences statistics. Supply logfile for a report with labeled planes. append=False replaces that file. list=True adds a summary, and verbose=True sends the table to the logger. Flux density for a retained channel or polarization uses that plane's restoring beam. An all-axis reduction over a selected single polarization integrates the channel flux densities. Disk storage is tracked in #1627.

The remaining CASA image and coordinate operations are tracked in #1027.

Use ia.maketestimage() to load demo/Images/imagetestimage.fits as a temporary image. Pass outfile to write a native image. The tool searches the working directory, CASA_RS_MEASURESPATH, and the CASA installation's data directory when CASAPATH or AIPSPATH identifies it.

docs.title: Extract a subimage
docs.text:
Use ia.subimage(outfile="cutout.im", region=region) to copy a selection to a native CASA image. The method returns a separate image tool. Leave outfile empty for a temporary image, or set wantreturn=False to write the file and return None. The copy shifts its reference pixels, keeps the applicable restoring beams and input history, and combines the region with the input's validity mask and any supplied mask expression.

Use dropdeg=True to drop singleton axes. List the singleton axes you want to keep in keepaxes. Region inputs include CRTF text and files, saved region references, and unit-stride boxes and polygon records. An existing entry inside the input image cannot be replaced, protecting the source's history and mask tables.

Use ia.adddegaxes(stokes="I", spectral=True) to make a copy with new singleton axes. Pass outfile to save the copy as a native image. The copy preserves the source pixels, existing coordinates, named masks and history. Set silent=True to skip requested coordinate types that already exist. Sources with image attribute groups are tracked in #1625.

docs.title: Migrate an existing image reader or writer
docs.text:
The former casars.data.Image and casars.Image exports have been retired. Create an image() tool, call open(path), and call done() when finished.

Previous operation CASA image tool shape, pixel_type, units shape(), pixeltype(), brightnessunit() coordinate_system, misc_info coordsys().torecord(), miscinfo() image_info torecord()["imageinfo"], or restoringbeam() for beam quantities mask_names, default_mask_name maskhandler("get"), maskhandler("default") get_slice(start, shape, stride=...) getchunk(blc=start, trc=last, inc=stride) get_mask_slice(...) getchunk(..., getmask=True) put_slice(pixels, start) putchunk(pixels, blc=start)

blc and trc are inclusive zero-based pixel coordinates. For each axis, calculate last = start + (shape - 1) * stride. To read a plane, give that axis the same start and end, and squeeze that axis from the resulting array. Use casars.imexplore.data for a plane with its native NumPy dtype, mask and WCS.

Like CASA, getchunk returns real pixels as float64 and complex pixels as complex128. Use the storage type from pixeltype() if your caller needs the original width. An unmasked chunk returns an all-true mask. Use maskhandler("default") if your caller distinguishes a missing default mask. CASA returns [""] for a missing default mask and ["T"] when listing an unmasked image.

docs.title: Stitch independently CLEANed pointings
docs.text:
Run tclean for each field with the same spectral selection, reference frequency and restoring beam. Pass each restored .image and its .pb to linearmosaic. Use the uncorrected .image from each clean. A separate tclean(niter=0) can supply the output grid if none of the pointing images covers the region you want.

from casars.data import linearmosaic
from casars.tasks import tclean

common = dict(
    vis="two-pointings.ms", datacolumn="data", gridder="standard",
    specmode="mfs", reffreq="1.5GHz", cell="8arcsec", interactive=False,
    pblimit=0.01,
)
for field in (0, 1):
    tclean(**common, field=str(field), imagename=f"point{field}",
           imsize=288, niter=20, restoringbeam=["80arcsec", "80arcsec", "0deg"])

tclean(**common, field="0", imagename="mosaic-grid", imsize=96, niter=0,
       phasecenter="J2000 19h59m28.5 +40d50m01.5")

linearmosaic(
    [(f"point{field}.image", f"point{field}.pb") for field in (0, 1)],
    template="mosaic-grid.image",
    output="stitched.image",
    output_weight="stitched.weight",
)

Choose the reference frequency, angular cell size, restoring beam and output coordinates for your observation. Only the template's grid is used. stitched.weight gives the beam-squared coverage on that grid. The flux-correct image is zero where coverage is at most 1e-6 of peak coverage. Both outputs are CASA images, and both paths must be new. When a projected footprint edge falls exactly halfway between output pixels, coordinate rounding can move the edge by a pixel compared with CASA.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
Use the CASA-style casars.tools.table tool for in-process table access:

from casars.tools import table

tb = table()
tb.open("observation.ms")
print(tb.nrows(), tb.colnames())
first_baseline = tb.getcell("ANTENNA1", 0)
tb.close()

getcol returns fixed-shape arrays with rows on the last axis. Use getvarcol for variable-shape cells. To write, open with nomodify=False; the write methods are putcell, putcol, and putcolkeywords, among others.

docs.title: Calibrate Tasks
docs.text:
The calibration tasks are generated, CASA-named wrappers in casars.tasks:

  • calibrate(mode=..., ...), the workflow surface: apply (the default), solve_gain, solve_bandpass, fluxscale, gencal, summary, stats and export_corrected_data;
  • applycal, gaincal, bandpass, fluxscale and gencal, with CASA 6.7.6's signatures: CASA's parameters in CASA's order with CASA's defaults, then casa-rs's keyword-only output, overwrite and format (and array, gaincurve_table where they apply).

The CASA-named functions return what CASA's tasks return: gaincal and bandpass a dictionary of the tables applied (apply_tables) and solved (solve_tables), the data selected (selectvis) and how many solution intervals each window and antenna reached at each stage (solvestats); fluxscale its flux densities per field and spectral window; applycal and gencal None. calibrate(...) and tasks.run(name, ...) return a TaskCompletion. A CASA parameter casa-rs does not implement yet is taken only at its default, and a CASA value it does not implement yet is refused; both refusals name #979.

Each call starts the calibrate executable directly, with the surface as its first word (calibrate gaincal), and sends one TaskRunRequest on --json-run -: the values the call set, resolved inside the executable against the same contract as its own command line. Its log lines reach sys.stderr as they arrive. Python projects no flags and builds no Rust request. A refused value names its parameter: the task's refusal raises TaskParameterError, a ValueError, and a run that does not succeed raises TaskExecutionError; the .completion of either has its status, message and parameter.

On the CASA-named surfaces the chain is CASA's: gaintable is a list of tables, and gainfield, interp and spwmap are positional lists, so gaintable[i] takes gainfield[i], interp[i] and spwmap[i], and a table past the end of a list takes CASA's default for it (every field, 'linear', no window map). calwt holds one flag for every table or one per table. docallib=True applies the calibration library callib instead.

On calibrate, gaintables and summary_paths are lists of calibration-table paths: a list, or one comma-separated string. Its per-table controls (gainfield, interp, spwmap, calwt) are ;-separated strings aligned to gaintables, one value for every table or one per table.

The calibrate binary takes the same parameters on its own command line.

gaincal and bandpass replace their caltable by default; append=True adds compatible solutions. fluxscale requires append=True when its output already exists. gencal accumulates specified corrections. A solve with no successful solutions returns statistics and leaves the destination alone. The keyword-only overwrite controls the report on CASA-named tasks; on native calibrate it also permits scientific-product replacement.

docs.title: Parameter document compatibility
docs.text:
Sparse TOML documents carry two independent versions:

  • casars.format versions the document envelope and TOML conventions.
  • casars.contract versions the selected task definition.

Loading resolves sparse overrides against the current provider definition. Newly added optional parameters receive current defaults. Omitted parameters whose defaults changed also receive the new default and produce a compatibility warning. Renames and type/value changes require an explicit ordered migration; future or unmigratable versions fail before invocation.

This behavior preserves user intent rather than freezing an exact historical request. Use a separate resolved run manifest when exact replay is required. The Python implementation uses the shared Rust runtime and must not maintain an independent migration or default table.

Managed state normally lives at:

<workspace>/.casa-rs/parameters/<surface-id>/last.toml
<workspace>/.casa-rs/parameters/<surface-id>/last-successful.toml

CASA_RS_STATE_DIR redirects the managed root without changing workspace path resolution. An explicit source profile is never overwritten without an explicit save.

docs.title: Task-runner compatibility
docs.text:
Python has one task transport: every generated casars.tasks.<task> callable and casars.tasks.run start the task's own executable, named by the canonical application catalog, with its surface's fixed arguments and --json-run -. One Rust resolver (casa_provider_contracts::resolve_task_executable, through casars._core) finds that executable. The first step that applies decides:

  1. the task's catalog override variable, CASARS_<APP>_BIN (for example CASARS_IMAGER_BIN or CASARS_CALIBRATE_BIN), names the file;
  2. a suite root holds it at <root>/bin/<executable>: CASARS_SUITE_ROOT, or else the installed suite the Python package belongs to (the installer's environment is <suite>/python, beside <suite>/bin and bundle-manifest.json);
  3. a development checkout: the newest debug or release build of the executable under the workspace the package was built from, in $CARGO_TARGET_DIR or target/.

A step that applies but lacks the file raises TaskBinaryNotFoundError naming what it lacked; it never falls through to a later step, so an installed suite never runs a checkout's build. A missing development build is reported with the cargo build -p <package> --bin <executable> that makes it. Python does not search the current directory or PATH, and nothing runs through cargo. A wheel installed outside a suite, such as one from PyPI, runs tasks only with CASARS_SUITE_ROOT or the task's override set; its in-process casars.data, casars.tools and casars.simutil need no executables. The executable validates the provider contract and request before execution; Python does not maintain a second protocol descriptor, provider schema, or compatibility handshake.

Release tags also build and publish Python package artifacts separately from the Rust binaries:

  • GitHub release assets always receive the built wheels, source distribution, suite bundles, standalone binary bundles, and installer script.
  • PyPI publication is attempted from the same workflow when PYPI_API_TOKEN is configured.

That means Python package compatibility has two layers:

  1. package-version compatibility with the published wheel or sdist
  2. runtime contract compatibility with the resolved suite and its catalog-owned task executables

The direct object-surface contract published by casars.data.protocol_info() and casars.data.schema_bundle() is currently:

  • protocol name: casars_data_objects
  • protocol version: 1
  • surface kind: object

Persistent image and table access use casars.tools.image and casars.tools.table. The former casars.data.Image, casars.Image, casars.data.Table and casars.Table exports are retired. See the Data API for image migration.

The bundle describes the casars.tools classes (simulator, measures, quanta, componentlist, image, coordsys, table, msmetadata, ms). The bundle's Python projection names casars.data as its module; a tool's projection entry names its own module (casars.tools) and class, and records the parameter order of its constructor's keyword-only controls and of each method, which the JSON Schema properties do not keep. Its annotations.python entry records whether casa-rs implements each method. A consumer reads an object's module from its own projection entry and falls back to the bundle's. The provider contract (docs/provider-contracts.md, "Object Surfaces") describes a tool's entry.

casars.simutil is the public import of CASA's simutil helper class (from casars import simutil, for CASA's from casatasks.private import simutil). It is not a CASA tool and is not in the bundle.

The installed suite's layout, channels and command links are described in Install.

docs.title: casa-rs and CASA 6.7.6.14 tasks and tools
docs.text:
Truth class: generated reference Generated by: scripts/check-casa-inventory.py --write Sources: resources/casa-compat/casa-6.7.6.14/ (read from CASA by tools/casa-compat/dump_casa_task_inventory.py), crates/casa-provider-contracts/resources/parameter-surfaces.json, parameter-catalog.json, the CASA class signatures in crates/casars-python/python/tests/data/, and reviewed resources/casa-compat/semantics/

Do not edit this file by hand. Regenerate it after changing the inventory, a surface, a recorded class signature or a reviewed file.

Each casa-rs task that mimics a CASA task (#931) against that task as CASA 6.7.6.14 defines it: whether it presents CASA's signature, the CASA parameters casa-rs does not take yet, those it takes but accepts only at CASA's default, the parameters casa-rs takes that CASA does not (casa-rs names for CASA concepts, or casa-rs-only controls), whether the shared parameters keep CASA's order, and the defaults that differ. calibrate, msconvert and msexplore are casa-rs tasks with no CASA counterpart.

The CASA parameters casa-rs lacks or accepts only at their defaults are tracked by family: images in #977, MeasurementSet and flagging in #978, calibration in #979 and tclean in #980.

For direct cBool, cFloat, cInt, cPath and cStr schemas with the recorded coercions, a value both implementations reject for type reports CASA's wording, unless a narrower unimplemented-form diagnostic applies. Direct cBoolVec, cFloatVec, cIntVec, cPathVec and cStrVec schemas are also covered where the recorded vector coercions apply. Float-shaped cIntVec inputs keep the native diagnostic because a JSON integer outside the native range may lose its original spelling. For explicit scalar inputs checked by the task, a missing absolute or explicitly relative path gets CASA's wording when the schema has one direct required path. Other required-path cases, unions and variants retain casa-rs's diagnostics (#1099). CASA accepts booleans as integers and coerces them to floats; where casa-rs refuses one, it keeps its own message. Exception classes follow the casa-rs Python contract.

docs.title: Apply linearized and full-matrix leakage to four polarization products
docs.text:
Implemented — Linear and circular four-product data with D, Df, Dgen, Dfgen, DLLS and DfLLS tables. Includes variable time and channel solutions, G/D/P order, flags, missing antennas, subselected channels, and unequal scalar and spectral weights.

The permuted-correlation and malformed-table differences are documented below. Cross-hand phase families continue under #1522.

Evidence: leakage-application.

docs.title: honor-leakage-correlation-metadata: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Inputs: A consistent linear-feed CORR_TYPE order of XX, YY, XY, YX.
  • CASA: Applies the correction to fixed slots and modifies a parallel hand.
  • casa-rs: Applies the leakage correction and flags to the products named by the MeasurementSet.
  • Rationale: The four-product layout is valid in casacore. Applying a cross-hand formula to a parallel hand changes the observed data incorrectly.
  • User impact: The native output equals permuting the canonical-order result.
  • Owner decision: Correct CASA data corruption under the standing deviations rule. Owner decision
  • Evidence: leakage-application.

docs.title: reject-underspecified-leakage-shape: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Inputs: A D Jones calibration table with one complex receptor per solution.
  • CASA: Aborts with ArrayShapeError.
  • casa-rs: Raises a catchable invalid calibration shape error.
  • Rationale: Two coefficients are required for a four-product leakage correction.
  • User impact: The caller can handle the malformed caltable without losing the process.
  • Owner decision: Correct CASA crashes and aborts under the standing deviations rule. Owner decision
  • Evidence: leakage-application.

docs.title: deterministic-nan-statistics: Proposed
docs.text:
• Inputs: A table column with both numeric values and NaN samples.
  • CASA: The median, quartile range and bounds can change when the same NaN moves between rows.
  • casa-rs: Preserves deterministic bounds over non-NaN samples, counts every sample and reports undefined moments and quantiles.
  • Rationale: The moments and quantiles of the unmasked data are undefined when a sample is NaN.
  • User impact: The selected row order does not change the native NaN policy.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: paired.
