docs.title: safe-spectral-orders: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Fluxscale negative and underdetermined spectral-fit orders
  • Inputs: Negative order, too few valid windows for requested degree, or an exactly determined fit.
  • CASA: Can segfault, fit the wrong degree, return unstable coefficients/negative covariance, or invent roundoff uncertainty.
  • casa-rs: Use advertised negative-order fallback; cap degree at nvalid-1, pad requested vectors and retain zero residual uncertainty at zero residual degrees of freedom.
  • Rationale: Implement identifiable fits and CASA's advertised fallback while retaining existing strict linear-fit behavior.
  • User impact: Determined fits agree; invalid memory access and unstable underdetermined artifacts are corrected.
  • Owner decision: Standing owner rule in AGENTS.md: correct CASA crashes, out-of-bounds writes, corrupt data or behavior contradicting evident intent.
  • Evidence: oracle.

docs.title: initialized-history-and-empty-map: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Fluxscale history can contain uninitialized object identifiers
  • Inputs: Successful MS HISTORY writes or refspwmap=[].
  • CASA: Does not initialize OBJECT_ID; indexes an empty map and segfaults.
  • casa-rs: Initialize OBJECT_ID=0 and treat the empty map as identity.
  • Rationale: Avoid uninitialized scientific provenance and invalid memory access.
  • User impact: Stable provenance; empty mapping is safe.
  • Owner decision: Standing owner rule in AGENTS.md: correct CASA crashes, out-of-bounds writes, corrupt data or behavior contradicting evident intent.
  • Evidence: oracle.

docs.title: preserve-scientific-files: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Fluxscale listfile can overwrite scientific table files
  • Inputs: A listing path inside the input MS, input caltable or output product, or a failed listing stream.
  • CASA: Can truncate a scientific table file or report success despite an unchecked stream failure.
  • casa-rs: Refuse overlapping paths before mutation and report listing write failures.
  • Rationale: Preserve scientific data and fulfill the requested text output.
  • User impact: Potentially destructive paths are refused; ordinary listing paths work.
  • Owner decision: Standing owner rule in AGENTS.md: correct CASA crashes, out-of-bounds writes, corrupt data or behavior contradicting evident intent.
  • Evidence: oracle.

docs.title: safe-whole-axis-selection: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Explicit gencal wildcards can index outside the calibration array
  • Inputs: An explicit whole-axis wildcard, a negated antenna index, or an empty legacy VLA antenna selection.
  • CASA: Some of these selections abort the process when they index a nonexistent table element.
  • casa-rs: Whole-axis selections broadcast, and invalid negative antenna indices raise a task error.
  • Rationale: Prevent native crashes and preserve prior calibration products.
  • User impact: Explicit and equivalent all-antenna selections produce the same intended correction.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: specified, manual-positions.

docs.title: safe-scalar-opacity: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Opacity priors can index a nonexistent second receptor
  • Inputs: A scalar opacity table with a second-receptor or two-receptor selection.
  • CASA: Indexes a nonexistent second receptor and terminates the task process.
  • casa-rs: Raises a task error and preserves the existing product.
  • Rationale: The opacity coefficient is scalar and the requested selection cannot be applied.
  • User impact: Empty and first-receptor selectors remain usable.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: opacity.

docs.title: safe-switched-power-input: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: A one-receptor SYSPOWER shape aborts switched-power calibration
  • Inputs: One receptor per SYSPOWER measurement or a SYSPOWER timestamp between visibility scans.
  • CASA: A malformed receptor shape aborts. An empty scan match is dereferenced and returned 0 in the oracle.
  • casa-rs: Refuses malformed shapes before publication and assigns unknown scan -1 to timestamps without a matching scan.
  • Rationale: Avoid process termination and retain physical measurement timestamps.
  • User impact: Usable SYSPOWER samples retain their actual times. Samples with no matching visibility scan carry an unknown scan ID.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: switched-power.

docs.title: finite-jyperk-gains: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Invalid Jy/K factors can publish unflagged nonfinite gains
  • Inputs: Zero or negative factors, or repeated factors exceeding the representable gain range.
  • CASA: Can publish unflagged nonfinite or zero complex gains.
  • casa-rs: Refuses the correction before publishing either a fresh or updated product.
  • Rationale: An unusable gain can corrupt calibrated visibilities.
  • User impact: Usable gains retain CASA multiplication and selector semantics.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: jyperk.

docs.title: flag-incomplete-tec: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: A flagged F Jones coefficient can leave unflagged visibilities
  • Inputs: A circular-feed F Jones table with the last antenna flagged at every epoch.
  • CASA: Leaves that antenna with a unity gain and unflagged baseline outputs.
  • casa-rs: Flags baselines with an unavailable correction when the apply mode writes flags.
  • Rationale: Preserve the validity of calibrated visibilities when a term is missing.
  • User impact: Valid solutions continue to apply using CASA science and flags.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: tecim.

docs.title: preserve-empty-eop-destination: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: An empty EOP result can delete an existing calibration table
  • Inputs: An existing Fringe Jones table and a missing input file or input without matching Earth orientation updates.
  • CASA: Removes the destination during cleanup.
  • casa-rs: Keeps the existing table and only publishes a complete replacement.
  • Rationale: Preserve prior calibration products on input failures.
  • User impact: A missing input still raises FileNotFoundError. No matching Earth orientation leaves a diagnostic and preserves any prior product.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: eop.

docs.title: bracket-all-eop-samples: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: EOP interpolation can ignore later daily samples
  • Inputs: An observing epoch after the fourth day in a daily Earth orientation series.
  • CASA: Caps the upper sample index at three and extrapolates from earlier samples.
  • casa-rs: Brackets the observing epoch using the available samples.
  • Rationale: Prevent a stale polar-motion or UT1 correction despite available matching data.
  • User impact: The seven-epoch fixture agrees with an independent ERFA delay calculation.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: eop.

docs.title: finite-jyperk-gains: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Invalid Jy/K factors can publish unflagged nonfinite gains
  • Inputs: Zero or negative factors, or repeated factors exceeding the representable gain range.
  • CASA: Can publish unflagged nonfinite or zero complex gains.
  • casa-rs: Refuses the correction before publishing either a fresh or updated product.
  • Rationale: An unusable gain can corrupt calibrated visibilities.
  • User impact: Usable gains retain CASA multiplication and selector semantics.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: jyperk.

docs.title: reject-incomplete-antenna-integration: Proposed
docs.text:
• Inputs: A standard G Jones calibration solution table with the final antenna row removed.
  • CASA: Terminates after opening the output while reshaping the window into antenna blocks.

  • User impact: The caller can handle the error and the listing path remains available for a corrected retry.

docs.title: Channel derivatives and platforming
docs.text:

docs.title: integer-platforming-channel-bounds: Proposed
docs.text:
• Inputs: Channel derivatives with enough interior points to enter the platforming check.
  • CASA: Passes floating-point channel offsets to Python range and raises TypeError.
  • casa-rs: Uses integer channel indices and tests the interior derivative against the requested MAD or percentage threshold.
  • Rationale: Keep the documented platforming check functional for wide calibration spectral windows.
  • User impact: An interior amplitude step is reported at a threshold it exceeds and omitted at a larger threshold.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: paired.

docs.title: default-atmosphere-without-weather: Proposed
docs.text:
• Inputs: An atmospheric overlay on a bandpass whose associated MS has no WEATHER table.
  • CASA: Raises NameError while referencing needToClose_mymsmd.
  • casa-rs: Evaluates the ATM profile using the station defaults available in the absence of measured weather.
  • Rationale: Allow a transmission or sky-temperature overlay for supported data with missing weather measurements.
  • User impact: The plot includes a finite atmospheric curve and the original calibration spectra.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: paired.

docs.text:

CASA 6.7.6.14 plots and return values, including selected arrays, axes, titles, companion time grids, physical receptor labels, masking, overlay colors and legends, paging, PNG filenames, PDFs, measured water, wide atmospheric grids and split receivers.

docs.title: plotms interacting modes and task behavior
Read MeasurementSets and calibration tables
docs.text:
Partial — Open casacore MeasurementSets and current, BPOLY and GSPLINE calibration tables through vis or caltable, preserving the public None return and input-path checks.

Remaining MeasurementSet plotting paths are open under #1032 and #215.

Evidence: paired, legacy-calibration.

docs.title: Select solution samples
docs.text:
Partial — Select solution rows and channels by field, window, time, antenna, scan, observation, polarization, antenna-position component and TaQL. Refuse unsupported modern calibration selectors. Resolve GSPLINE selection directly against source table rows and CAL_DESC. Route ordinary MeasurementSet visibility plots through native row, baseline, channel, correlation and flag selection. Apply the same feed predicate to the selected visibility rows and the row selection used by atmospheric overlays.

Remaining MeasurementSet selection paths are open under #1032 and #215.

Evidence: paired, selectors, ms-ordinary-visibility, legacy-calibration, ms-feed-selection, ms-row-axes.

docs.title: Project axes and flags
docs.text:
Partial — Read complex and real parameter cells and select calibration axes. Keep flagged sample visibility consistent in text and image products. Validate active axis and range controls before writing. Use the reference axes for Tsys and antenna-position products. Evaluate stored BPOLY and GSPLINE coefficients and expose their solution flags and metadata. Plot independent stored MeasurementSet DATA, CORRECTED_DATA and MODEL_DATA axes and unaveraged vector and scalar residuals or model ratios with the shared sample mask. Use DATA for corrected axes, residuals and ratios when the stored corrected column is absent on a complex MeasurementSet. Use FLOAT_DATA for observed visibilities on unaveraged mixed inputs and signed amplitude or real axes on float-only inputs. Keep the requested order and column identity for independent unaveraged visibility ordinates and group them by figure side. Use the default visibility model for complex data without a stored model or an applicable virtual recipe. Predict selected virtual component and Fourier models through the native visibility model engine. Plot unaveraged visibility axes with integration interval and UVW in wavelengths using the selected visibility buffer and per-channel frequency. Unaveraged channel plots of three or more axes on Y use separate masks for visibility, U, V, W and observatory elevation ordinates. Plot raw row and buffer identifiers with selected visibility axes and use distinct STATE observing mode IDs for Intent. Use each metadata-only Time or Channel pair's dimensions to collapse selected visibility flags and report its compact point identifiers. Pair Time, antenna longitude and antenna latitude with selected cube masks, nearest or spline interpolation, and independently chosen scalar direction frames.

Averaged pointing, list-valued pointing controls, sample masks for other mixed visibility and metadata axes, additional averaging modes and additional MS column forms are open. Averaged interval and wavelength coordinates and reporting-frame transforms for these axes remain open.

Evidence: paired, selectors, ms-columns, ms-residual-columns, ms-scalar-residual-columns, ms-model-ratios, ms-ordinate-columns, ms-float-data, ms-corrected-fallback, callibrary, legacy-calibration, ms-default-model, ms-virtual-model, ms-channel-columns, ms-multiple-visibility-ordinates, ms-time-columns, ms-interval-wavelength, ms-channel-ordinate-masks, ms-row-axes, ms-metadata-pair-masks, ms-pointing-directions.

docs.title: Average selected plot samples
docs.text:
Partial — Average calibration solutions in weighted channel and time bins with scan, field, antenna, baseline and spectral-window controls. Keep flagged channel frequency coordinates consistent with the CASA cache. For MeasurementSets, independently channel-average stored visibility columns while applying each column's spectral weights and the selected channel flags. Ordinary vector time averaging uses the selected integrations, per-column weights and the MeasurementSet transform time groups. Channel averaging can follow ordinary vector time averaging. The primary channel weights determine which averaged bins render. Vector time bins can span the requested scan and field boundaries. Vector baseline averages use the visibility iterator order and preserve separate observations. Text exports use synthetic antenna IDs. For combined channel and baseline averages, each visibility column is averaged across channels before the baseline reducer applies the transformed scalar weight. Combined vector time and baseline averages follow the subchunks emitted by the time-averaging iterator and use their interval bounds. With all three vector controls, baseline weights come from the time-accumulated and channel-binned spectra. Ordinary scalar time averaging uses the raw visibility buffer windows and separate amplitude and phase means. Channel-averaged statistical coordinates use transformed spectra, the selected cube mask and the observed or calibrated column role. Baseline coordinates for ordinary vector time averaging use the transform row weights and the selected cube mask.

Scalar combinations with other averaging controls, antenna and spectral-window averaging, fully masked exports, effective FLOAT_DATA and derived visibility averages, and additional flagged and weight coordinates remain under #1032.

Evidence: paired, ms-channel-columns, ms-time-columns, ms-channel-time-columns, ms-scan-field-time-columns, ms-baseline-columns, ms-baseline-channel-columns, ms-baseline-time-columns, ms-baseline-time-channel-columns, ms-scalar-time-columns, ms-channel-statistics, ms-vector-time-uvw.

docs.title: Lay out and export plot pages
docs.text:
Partial — Partition selected series across a grid. Text uses the requested grid capacity. Image export provides current and all-page ranges and names the physical outputs in successful completions. A noniterated MeasurementSet visibility plot occupies the requested grid cell. Offset MeasurementSet scan pages account for the starting cell when exporting images.

Other offset iteration combinations, calibration-table placement, persistent pages and additional presentation modes remain open.

Evidence: paired, ms-static-grid-placement, ms-iterated-grid-start.

docs.title: Render the shared plot document
docs.text:
Partial — Transfer native arrays through the existing binary payload and draw them in the shared Matplotlib renderer. Apply plot titles, labels, marker size and shape, connectors, grids, legend, page headers and export sizing. Show or hide the clear and flagged symbols independently for unaveraged MeasurementSet visibility pairs.

Renderer-specific marker fill patterns and interactive editing remain open.

Evidence: paired, calibration-controls, ms-raw-flag-symbols.

docs.title: Save and publish selected plot products
docs.text:
Partial — Write current and legacy calibration coordinates and metadata as text and render figures through the shared Python presenter. Publish requested files and preserve existing files when overwrite is false. Export ordinary MeasurementSet visibility coordinates and independent stored visibility columns as text and figures. Export calibrated MeasurementSet text and paginated figures, including atmospheric curves. Write a successful empty text section and figure for fully hidden raw visibility pairs.

More export, multi-plot state and interactive display forms remain open.

Evidence: paired, ms-columns, ms-ordinary-visibility, callibrary, legacy-calibration, ms-raw-flag-symbols.

docs.title: Advanced calibration plotting controls
docs.text:
Partial — Apply calibration libraries to MeasurementSet plots in memory. Compute transmission, sky temperature and receiver sidebands for MeasurementSets and calibration tables, including selected channels and requested overlay color groups.

Remaining shared PlotMS forms are tracked in #1032 and #215.

Evidence: atmosphere, ms-atmosphere, selectors, remaining, callibrary.

docs.title: disable-selection: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: PlotMS disabling selection calls the selection setter with a missing argument
  • Inputs: A PlotMS request with selectdata=False and supplied selection text.
  • CASA: Raises Exception with message updateImmediately must be a boolean.
  • casa-rs: Displays and exports all available solution points without applying the selector text.
  • Rationale: Make the documented selection switch work when it is false.
  • User impact: The native request produces all 160 available points in the paired fixture. The same fallback preserves all 1,920 points in the unfiltered callibrary case.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: paired, callibrary.

docs.title: calibration-selection-diagnostics: Proposed
docs.text:
• Inputs: Modern calibration input with an unsupported selector, invalid antenna-position selector or empty TaQL selection.
  • CASA: Refuses the plot with an RPC failure whose details say plot parameters failed.
  • casa-rs: Refuses the plot with a task parameter error describing the selector or empty row set.
  • Rationale: Give the caller the cause using the native task error contract.
  • User impact: Both workflows preserve an absent export on selection failure.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: selectors.

docs.title: gspline-negative-antenna: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: PlotMS shows the excluded antenna on a GSPLINE plot
  • Inputs: A five-antenna GSPLINE table plotted with antenna="!A2".
  • CASA: Displays only antenna A2, despite negation.
  • casa-rs: Displays A0, A1, A3 and A4.
  • Rationale: Honor the documented antenna exclusion instead of passing the excluded ID to the plot cache.
  • User impact: The displayed antenna membership follows the source-row filter.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: legacy-calibration.

docs.title: singleton-mask-pairs: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: Single-dish baseline tables can contain malformed singleton mask ranges
  • Inputs: Select a spectrum whose fitted mask starts with a singleton channel and another disjoint range.
  • CASA: The saved mask has an odd endpoint count and CASA refuses to apply it.
  • casa-rs: The singleton channel has equal start and end endpoints and the native table applies in CASA.
  • Rationale: Every fitted range needs both endpoints to preserve its channels on interchange.
  • User impact: Coefficients can be reused after fitting non-contiguous masks.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: paired.

docs.title: remove-spectral-noise: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: Single-dish baseline weight updates can fail when removing two columns
  • Inputs: Set updateweight on an input containing both spectral noise columns.
  • CASA: The public task raises after producing the data and scalar weights.
  • casa-rs: The public task writes the recalculated weights with the two stale columns omitted.
  • Rationale: The table API must receive individual column names when dropping both columns.
  • User impact: A successful task leaves a usable product and only its current noise estimates.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: paired.

docs.title: per-spectrum-clipped-count: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: Single-dish baseline reports accumulate clipped-channel counts
  • Inputs: Reject one spectral channel in each of multiple consecutive integrations.
  • CASA: Reports a running clipped-channel count within a visibility buffer.
  • casa-rs: Reports the number clipped in that spectrum.
  • Rationale: Each row in the diagnostic describes an individual fit.
  • User impact: The number describes the channels rejected in the specified spectrum.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: paired.

docs.title: negative-iterations: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: Single-dish baseline fitting accepts negative iteration counts in CASA
  • Inputs: Set clipniter below zero or num_fitting_max to zero.
  • CASA: Converts the result to an unsigned fit count. Zero can return a model without a fit.
  • casa-rs: Reports a fitting-iteration validation error.
  • Rationale: Fitting a baseline requires at least the initial fit.
  • User impact: The wrapper cannot publish unused or uninitialized coefficients as a fitted model.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: iteration-source.

docs.title: dense-spline-accuracy: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: Dense single-dish cubic splines can lose numerical accuracy in CASA
  • Inputs: Fit 47 or 93 cubic pieces to a 96-channel seeded Gaussian spectrum.
  • CASA: Residuals differ from the independent B-spline least-squares solution.
  • casa-rs: An SVD of the design matrix reproduces that solution within 2.2e-8 RMS.
  • Rationale: The normal system squares the condition number of a dense spline design.
  • User impact: Highly segmented fits retain numerical accuracy.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: automatic-and-spline.

docs.title: line-finder-index-limits: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: Single-dish automatic line masks can access invalid channels in CASA
  • Inputs: Select a narrow fitted range or detect a line touching channel zero.
  • CASA: Can index before the median array or decrement an unsigned zero channel index.
  • casa-rs: Stop an averaging level with fewer than two eligible bins and bound wing extension.
  • Rationale: Those cases have no contributing bins or channels beyond the available data.
  • User impact: A narrow range can be fitted even if a coarser bin has no eligible channels.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: automatic-and-spline.

docs.title: protect-zero-sky-signal: Proposed
docs.text:
• Inputs: A sky calibration table with a clear flag and a zero OFF reference spectrum.
  • CASA: Divides by the zero spectrum and leaves the channel unflagged.
  • casa-rs: Retains the value entering the sky correction and flags the invalid sample in flag-writing modes.
  • Rationale: The OFF spectrum is the denominator of the correction and cannot define a finite calibrated value at zero.
  • User impact: Adjacent channels with valid references still calibrate and downstream consumers can mask the invalid correction.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: application.

docs.title: include-raster-final-strip: Proposed
docs.text:
• Inputs: A gapped raster map with multiple strips and valid reference integrations at both ends of each strip.
  • CASA: Depending on uninitialized gap-array contents, can omit the two solutions from the last strip.
  • casa-rs: Always close the final range at the integration count and select both ends of the last strip.
  • Rationale: The last observed strip has the same edge eligibility as preceding strips. Including both boundaries produces stable calibration across repeat runs.
  • User impact: All 44 reference spectra from the 22-strip fixture are present.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: edges.

docs.title: chronological-time-bins: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Single-dish line fitting can exceed its time bin on descending rows
  • Inputs: A one-second fit bin on four integrations provided in descending physical order.
  • CASA: The iterator fits one combined spectrum per hand.
  • casa-rs: Chronological ordering yields four fitted spectra per hand in either physical row order.
  • Rationale: The bin duration applies to integration times. Fit products agree with CASA on the chronological input.
  • User impact: A reordered MeasurementSet gives the same fitted time bins.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: paired.

docs.title: single-hand-average: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Single-dish polarization averaging can abort for one selected hand
  • Inputs: Select YY on an XX/YY setup and request geometric averaging.
  • CASA: The iterator can abort while indexing the original pair.
  • casa-rs: With no selected pair, fit the selected hand unchanged.
  • Rationale: The selected correlation is the only available eligible spectrum.
  • User impact: The call returns the equivalent fit of the selected hand.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: paired.

docs.title: negative-fit-count: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Single-dish line fitting aborts for negative component counts
  • Inputs: Use nfit=[-1] in list mode.
  • CASA: An unsigned component allocation can abort the process.
  • casa-rs: Raise a runtime error before allocating a fit.
  • Rationale: A component count cannot be negative.
  • User impact: The caller can correct the list without losing the session.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: paired.

docs.title: fit-report-overwrite: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: A failed line fit can delete the previous report
  • Inputs: Enable overwrite for an existing fit report and supply a mismatched component count.
  • CASA: The earlier report is removed before the error.
  • casa-rs: Keep the report until the replacement has been fitted and written.
  • Rationale: An incomplete fit cannot replace an existing product.
  • User impact: The caller keeps the earlier report after a failed fit.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: paired.

docs.title: simobserve interacting modes and task behavior
Sky model and component list
docs.text:
Partial — skymodel through modifymodel and flatimage with inbright, indirection, incell, incenter and inwidth; complist with compwidth and comp_nchan, alone or with a sky model.

Scoped CASA task evidence covers scalar indirection and incell overrides separately and together, four-channel component-only models, combined image/component inputs with brightness/cell/direction/frequency overrides, and a polarized four-Stokes, four-channel image with components. The receipts cover these representative workflows, not an exhaustive Cartesian product of inputs.

Evidence: task-tests, parity-20261103, model-overrides-20261111, main-integration-20261111, interferometric-projects-20261114.

docs.title: Antenna lists
docs.text:
Implemented — antennalist and sdantlist as files, ALMA resolution strings ('alma;0.5arcsec'), the search through the project directory and CASA's alma/simmos, and sdant.

Named configurations require external public alma/simmos files in a valid CASA_RS_MEASURESPATH or ~/.casa/data runtime. README describes obtaining them from NRAO's runtime-data archive; the compact measures snapshot does not bundle them. Project-local and explicit configuration files remain supported.

Evidence: task-tests, parity-20261103, uvw-long-baselines-20261112, array-configuration-controls.

docs.title: Pointings
docs.text:
Partial — setpointings with direction, mapsize, maptype and pointingspacing, or a ptgfile; written to .ptg.txt and checked against the model.

CASA task evidence includes square interferometric pointings, a three-entry user pointing file with 10/20/30-second dwell times over two full passes, and a 16 by 12 arcsecond hexagonal map with explicit 4 arcsecond spacing. Other file formats and pointing/model/mode combinations remain outside these receipts.

Evidence: task-tests, parity-20261103, scheduling-20261111, pointings-20261111, main-integration-20261111.

docs.title: Calibrator and observing schedule
docs.text:
Partial — caldirection and calflux, integration, totaltime, refdate and hourangle.

Paired task evidence now covers numeric and quantity non-transit hour angles, reference dates in 2015/2016/2017/2025 and discarded time suffixes. The historical calibrator cases still use CASA sm re-prediction because the CASA task leaves calibrator scans unpredicted (approved decision); these four new cases have no calibrator.

Evidence: task-tests, parity-20261103, scheduling-20261111, main-integration-20261111, uvw-long-baselines-20261112.

docs.title: Observation and prediction
docs.text:
Partial — obsmode 'int', 'sd' and '' (corrupting an existing MeasurementSet), outframe, and the prediction of the model and calibrator.

Image-model interferometry has scoped CASA comparisons for LSRK, TOPO, BARY, LSRD, GEO, GALACTO, LGROUP and CMB. REST image prediction succeeds; Undefined image/component predictions and REST component or joint predictions resolve to documented failures before native MS publication. Stateful controls also cover continuation of REST image and BARY MeasurementSets, an ignored Undefined output-frame request, single-dish continuation, manual/atmospheric noise and ignored leakage with prediction disabled; original MS spectral frames are preserved. These are scoped workflows rather than an exhaustive Cartesian product of inputs.

docs.title: Thermal noise and leakage
docs.text:
Partial — thermalnoise 'tsys-atm', 'tsys-manual' and '' with user_pwv, t_ground, t_sky, tau0, seed, leakage and correlator.

Noise is compared statistically (variances and KS tests), since draws differ; each environment parameter is exercised once; seed is casa-rs's own stream. CASA's own suite holds its noise tests to CASA's seed-11111 draws within 5%, which casa-rs's random stream cannot reproduce; over 20 seeds the two implementations' noise levels agree to 0.5%.

docs.title: compwidth-unset-spectral-increment: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: An unset compwidth gives the component-only model a meaningless spectral increment
  • Inputs: simobserve with a component list, no sky image and compwidth=''.
  • CASA: It observes 2 GHz when compwidth is not a quantity, but sets the .compskymodel spectral increment from compwidth anyway, yielding a meaningless value (the RA in radians read as hertz, 4.976 Hz for RA 19h, in CASA 6.7.6).
  • casa-rs: Uses the 2 GHz simobserve observes with.
  • Rationale: The increment is the model's only spectral information beyond its reference frequency.
  • User impact: The component-only model carries a consistent spectral increment.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: calibrator-last-pass-scans-lists: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simobserve's calibrator: the last pass, its scans and two component lists
  • Inputs: simobserve with a phase calibrator (caldirection and calflux), also with a complist or totaltime ending inside a pass.
  • CASA: CASA 6.7.6 never observes the pointings of an incomplete last pass (a 300 s total on 105 pointings has only the calibrator's scan), selects fields range(0,nfld) so the calibrator's scans keep zeros plus noise, and joins component lists into one nonexistent table so predict returns False.
  • casa-rs: Observes the pointings the time allows, predicts every scan including the calibrator's, and predicts both lists as one list of their components.
  • Rationale: The task means to observe and predict all of these.
  • User impact: CASA data can lack pointings, have unpredicted calibrator scans, or be all zero; casa-rs data are complete (parity cases agree at 5e-9 NRMS).
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: noisier-t-cal-left: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simobserve leaves <stem>.noisier.T.cal
  • Inputs: simobserve with tsys-atm noise set after leakage (the noisier measurement set).
  • CASA: The setnoise table is written beside the noisy MeasurementSet, and the clean-up deletes .noisy.T.cal and .noisy.sd.T.cal but not .noisier.T.cal.
  • casa-rs: Writes no Tsys table for any of the three.
  • Rationale: The table is a by-product the task means to remove.
  • User impact: CASA leaves a stray table in the project that casa-rs never creates.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: observing-loop-never-ends: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simobserve's observing loop never ends for pointings of no length
  • Inputs: simobserve with integration='0s' or a pointing file of zero times.
  • CASA: The while (sttime-scanstart) < totalsec loop advances by each pointing's scan length; when a pass's lengths sum to zero the time never advances and CASA loops forever, collecting pointings.
  • casa-rs: Refuses such a schedule with a message.
  • Rationale: A schedule with no length cannot be observed.
  • User impact: The task stops with an error instead of hanging.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: skymodel-deleted-when-output: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simobserve deletes a sky model that is the model it writes
  • Inputs: simobserve with skymodel given as the full path /.skymodel (e.g. a rerun on an earlier run's model) and overwrite=True.
  • CASA: The output is the input: CASA deletes the model and then fails to read it.
  • casa-rs: Refuses the input, and the model is left in place.
  • Rationale: The user's input must not be destroyed.
  • User impact: The model survives and the user gets a clear refusal.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: project-path-nests-in-itself: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simobserve nests a project path inside itself
  • Inputs: simobserve with project given as a path, e.g. 'a/b'.
  • CASA: The task names files fileroot + '/' + project + '.' + cfg, so 'a/b' gives a/b/a/b. in a directory that does not exist; only a plain name in the working directory works.
  • casa-rs: Names files by the directory's last component, a/b/b..
  • Rationale: For a plain name the two are the same.
  • User impact: Project paths work in casa-rs and fail in CASA.
  • Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: symlink-in-project-write-through: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simobserve writes through a symbolic link in the project
  • Inputs: simobserve overwrite=True in a project containing a symbolic link such as .ptg.txt.
  • CASA: CASA copies ptgfile through the link, replacing the file the link points to outside the project, and creates outside files for dangling links; links to tables stop the task via rmtree; existence checks follow links.
  • casa-rs: Replaces a link in the project with the new file or table, leaves the target alone, and counts a link as existing under overwrite=False.
  • Rationale: Owner's decision of 2026-10-26: only the project's own files are replaced.
  • User impact: Files outside the project are no longer overwritten or created through links.
  • Owner decision: Owner decision, 2026-10-26: the project's own files are the only ones overwrite replaces (recorded with the provider contracts' overwrite exception).
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: direction-list-of-one-mean: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simobserve rounds a direction list of one to its mean
  • Inputs: simobserve with direction=['J2000 18h00m00.123456789s ...'] (a list of one) versus the same direction as a string.
  • CASA: CASA passes the list to calc_pointings2, and direction_splitter centres it at its mean written at precision 5, so the map is laid out about 1e-5 s of RA (0.15 mas) from the string case.
  • casa-rs: casa-rs's simutil follows CASA, but simobserve treats a list of one like a string and lays the map out at the exact direction.
  • Rationale: The task contract resolves a string to a list of one, and the rounding carries no information.
  • User impact: A map is placed at the exact direction, differing from CASA by about 0.15 mas for a list of one.
  • Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: report-failed-frequency-predictions: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Inputs: Interferometric simobserve with Undefined output frames, or REST frames and component inputs/calibrators.
  • CASA: The simulator rejects frequency conversion with predict=False; simobserve ignores it, succeeds and publishes zero unpredicted DATA.
  • casa-rs: Report the simulator failure cause before close publishes an unpredicted MS; preserve prepared model/pointing products and support valid REST image prediction.
  • Rationale: A rejected prediction cannot produce a valid simulated science dataset. Do not hide the failure behind a successful zero-MS task result.
  • User impact: Scripts now receive the calculation error instead of silently continuing with invalid DATA. Valid other frame/model combinations are unchanged.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md CASA deviations: where CASA loses/corrupts data or contradicts its evident intent, casa-rs corrects it. This applies that existing policy to ignored predict=False outcomes.
  • Evidence: interferometric-projects-20261114.

docs.title: casa-suite-20261103
docs.text:
CASA's test_task_simobserve with casa-rs in place of CASA's task — measured. Of the 54 cases CASA 6.7.6.14 passes on this host, casa-rs passes 45. Of the other 9, 3 refuse as CASA does in casa-rs's own words: an empty project, and comp_nchan and sdant of the wrong type. The other 6 are noise levels just outside the suite's 5% band: tsys-manual interferometer noise 5.8% below CASA's recorded value, and tsys-atm single-dish noise 5.05% above it in all five variants. Those six are CASA's own seed-11111 draws, which casa-rs's random stream cannot reproduce; over 20 seeds the levels agree to 0.5% (noise-seeds-20261103). 23 cases fail with CASA's own task too and 16 are skipped by both. CASA's own simobserve suite (93 cases): sky models, component lists, both, noise, bad inputs and correlators, judged by the suite's checks against casatestdata's reference products.

The levels CASA's suite records are CASA's own seed-11111 draws, 1.8 and 2.9 of CASA's standard deviations from its mean, which a different random stream cannot reproduce: they explain the suite's six noise failures. testNZ_sdAtm and testNZ_intMan of CASA's test_task_simobserve, the suite's noise level (noisy minus original, real part, standard deviation) per run.

Implementation status is not behavioral verification. Implemented means the stated scope has a native code path; Partial has known missing forms or combinations; Default only is derived from the runtime refusal contract; Not implemented has no implementation; Unassessed has not been reviewed. Mappings, defaults, catalog domains, constraints and conditional default-only refusals are generated from the existing task contract. The catalog may admit values that the native reader then refuses: the reviewed scope and linked combinations describe those restrictions.

docs.title: preserve-fringe-delay-units: Proposed
docs.text:
• Inputs: Fringe Jones smoothing with smoothtype set to median.
  • CASA: Wraps delay and other non-phase values as radians and bypasses their median.
  • casa-rs: Preserves their units and applies the numerical median to each non-phase series.
  • Rationale: The source condition applies phase handling to every parameter. An 8 ns delay became about 1.717 ns.
  • User impact: The fringe phase comparisons pass and the non-phase outputs follow independently calculated medians.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: paired.

Implementation status is not behavioral verification. Implemented means the stated scope has a native code path; Partial has known missing forms or combinations; Default only is derived from the runtime refusal contract; Not implemented has no implementation; Unassessed has not been reviewed. Audit baseline: c64f13cb09054b080fe8b228a5f2c02c99bfd486. Status counts: Default only: 3, Implemented: 46, Not implemented: 0, Partial: 42, Unassessed: 1.

Mappings, defaults, catalog domains, constraints and conditional default-only refusals are generated from the existing task contract. The catalog may admit values that the native reader then refuses: the reviewed scope and linked combinations describe those restrictions.

CASA parameter CASA default casa-rs default; mapping Implementation Scope and runtime restrictions Evidence vis '' ''; vis → vis Partial Contract 38: a list of MeasurementSets images as one, as CASA's tclean images its vis list. Each is opened and surveyed with its own selectors. All inputs share one observation string. Other selectors take one per MeasurementSet or one for every input. MeasurementSets are ordered stably by its earliest MAIN TIME and visited as CASA visits its ms0, ms1, ... keys, as text (input_parameters.checkAndFixSelectionPars, mslisthelper.sort_mslist, imager_base.selectData); one selecting no sample is left out unless it is the first (SynthesisImagerVi2::selectData). The image's coordinates (obs date, telescope, phase centre, rest frequency, a cube's axis) come from CASA's msobj (buildCoordinateSystem): the first MeasurementSet, or for a cube or cubedata whose start is a frequency or velocity the last one whose selected band holds it (CAS-12877); a continuum band, and so the MFS and MT-MFS reference frequency, spans every one. A cube reads each other MeasurementSet's window where it reaches the cube, and one that does not reach it is read so its MODEL_DATA holds the zero prediction, as CASA writes it. Weighting density spans every MeasurementSet; datacolumn falls back to DATA per MeasurementSet; savemodel writes each one's MODEL_DATA (or virtual model). CASA's addwtspec, which adds WEIGHT_SPECTRUM to a listed MeasurementSet lacking it as a Vi/VB2 workaround, is not done: casa-rs reads each MeasurementSet's own weights, which that column copies, and never modifies its inputs. A row's spectral window and field are keyed among every MeasurementSet's, as if they were concatenated, so the mosaic keeps each one's beams (CASA's msId_spw, SimplePBConvFunc::convIndex) and a mosweight density each one's fields (VisImagingWeight's msId_field) apart; its dishes are every MeasurementSet's aperture classes (HetArrayConvFunc::findAntennaSizes). Refused with several MeasurementSets (#980): the awproject gridder (its catalog keys cells on the first MeasurementSet's frequencies), a moving phase centre, specmode cubesource, fitspw and a cube's per-channel density weighting. A cube with an unset start reads the band selected over every MeasurementSet, on the first one's channels (SynthesisParamsImage::buildCoordinateSystem). selectionCatalog domain: list[path (measurement_set)], length 0..many; scalar allowed signature, reader, vis-list-20261102, two-ms-band-20261104 selectdata True True; selectdata → selectdata Implemented Read then ignored; CASA task selection fields are applied regardless of this flag. selectionCatalog domain: bool signature, reader field '' ''; field → field Partial Comma lists and a surrounding pair of parentheses combine IDs, inclusive ranges, strict comparisons, names, shell patterns and slash-delimited regexes. Each input keeps the field text. Only exactly empty text selects all fields without matching metadata. A blank token can match an empty name or code. A bare token such as none or -1 can be a field name. Quotes allow bracket and brace patterns and commas inside a term. Quoted patterns and slash regexes discard backslashes and newlines as the CASA scanner does. Names match unflagged stored NAMEs before CODEs. Pattern CODE matching uses the stored text, and literal NAME and CODE comparisons trim only spaces. In-range numeric IDs include flagged rows. Out-of-range IDs within the signed 32-bit domain can match the first unflagged decimal NAME or CODE over the catalogue. Overflow is refused (#54). Slash regexes support positive and negative lookahead with whole-string byte matching. Unsupported ECMAScript groups are refused (#54). Bare escapes are refused so the scanner cannot silently drop input and select different rows (CASA bug, #54). Literal dollar signs at FIELD token boundaries and regex end anchors are accepted in tclean. Environment and shell expressions are refused. Supply one selector per MeasurementSet or one for every input. MSv2 imaging keeps selected rows distinct when two fields share an integration and antenna baseline. selectionCatalog domain: list[string], length 1..many; scalar allowed signature, reader, field-selection spw '' ''; spw → spw Partial The text reaches casa-ms's port of CASA 6.7.6.14's spectral-window grammar (casacore aaf72eb7 MSSpwGram/MSSpwParse/MSSpwIndex: IDs, ranges, steps, ; lists, exact names, patterns, quoted and /.../ patterns, frequency and stepped frequency ranges with units, ~f, >, < and <>, : channel lists with ranges, steps, -1 and frequency ranges, ( ) ), resolved on a MeasurementSet over SPECTRAL_WINDOW and DATA_DESCRIPTION: the MAIN rows of the data descriptions CASA keeps, and per window the union of its getChanList ranges, with CASA's clamps logged; 1,552 cases match CASA's ms.msselect and msselectedindices exactly (resources/casa-compat/evidence/msselection-spw-casa-20261102.json). Every refusal CASA makes is refused; velocity units are refused as CASA disables them. Refused although CASA accepts them, as their imaging is not established: a parenthesized expression (every MAIN row, some windows' channels), a window whose rows are kept but none of whose channel ranges found a channel, and overlapping channel ranges of one window. The parameter catalog's selector normalization (ms.selection.spw revisions 1 and 2) makes blank text and none unset and collapses whitespace, also inside quotes, so those CASA refusals and names are not exact (#980). Selected-channel derived cube extents are refused in limited nchan/start/width cases (#980). Contract 38: one selector per MeasurementSet of the vis list, or one (or a list of one) for every MeasurementSet; a list of another length is refused with CASA's message. A command-line text is one selector; a list is written as one or by repeating the flag. selection spectralCatalog domain: list[string], length 1..many; scalar allowed signature, reader timerange '' ''; timerange → timerange Implemented Contract 34 on a MeasurementSet: the exact text reaches casa-ms's port of CASA 6.7.6.14's time grammar (casacore aaf72eb7 MSTimeGram/MSTimeParse; 1,528 cases match CASA's ms.msselect), with CASA's defaults: the first MAIN row the other selections select for the first term (tclean always sets field and spw), row 0 for later terms. Each time is tested as TaQL tests TIME. An MSv4 processing set's timerange is refused (#980): CASA's defaults come from MAIN rows. CASA's row oracle (before and after a mid-observation time) reads CASA's rows exactly. Contract 38: one selector per MeasurementSet of the vis list, or one (or a list of one) for every MeasurementSet; a list of another length is refused with CASA's message. A command-line text is one selector; a list is written as one or by repeating the flag. selectionCatalog domain: list[string], length 1..many; scalar allowed signature, reader uvrange '' ''; uvrange → uvrange Implemented Copied as CASA selector text to request. Contract 38: one selector per MeasurementSet of the vis list, or one (or a list of one) for every MeasurementSet; a list of another length is refused with CASA's message. A command-line text is one selector; a list is written as one or by repeating the flag. selectionCatalog domain: list[string], length 1..many; scalar allowed signature, reader antenna '' ''; antenna → antenna Implemented Contract 34: the exact text reaches casa-ms's port of CASA 6.7.6.14's antenna grammar (casacore aaf72eb7 MSAntennaGram/MSAntennaParse: IDs, names, stations, patterns, regular expressions, &/&&/&&& baseline forms, ! negation, ; terms, @station and baseline-length forms), resolved over the catalogue's antennas into a baseline table that compile, survey and run test per sample. Blank text and none are refused. CASA's row oracle on mssel_test_small.ms (antenna 0, DA41, DA41&DA56, and with field and scan) reads CASA's MAIN rows exactly. Contract 38: one selector per MeasurementSet of the vis list, or one (or a list of one) for every MeasurementSet; a list of another length is refused with CASA's message. A command-line text is one selector; a list is written as one or by repeating the flag. selectionCatalog domain: list[string], length 1..many; scalar allowed signature, reader scan '' ''; scan → scan Partial Nonnegative IDs, comma unions, inclusive a~b ranges, and the six comparison forms (<, <=, >, >=, >a&=a&<=b) filter SCAN_NUMBER with either selectdata value. Each comparison becomes a compact interval. A nonnegative bound compares against the signed SCAN_NUMBER column, including stored negative values. Bare and comparison ranges require ascending bounds. Empty text is unset. Whitespace alone, signs, empty list terms and mixed strict/inclusive bounds are refused. Use one selector per MeasurementSet or the same selector for all. A valid predicate selecting no rows skips a later input. A first input with no rows is refused. A malformed predicate is refused on any input. selectionCatalog domain: list[string], length 1..many; scalar allowed signature, reader, field-selection, scan-observation-activation observation '' ''; observation → observation Partial The same grammar as scan filters OBSERVATION_ID with either selectdata value. A command-line text is one selector; a list is written as one or by repeating the flag. selectionCatalog domain: list[string], length 1..many; scalar allowed signature, reader datacolumn 'corrected' 'corrected'; datacolumn → DATA or automatic corrected/data Implemented data/observed maps to DATA; corrected maps to automatic CORRECTED_DATA else DATA; other strings refused. selectionCatalog domain: string signature, reader imagename '' ''; imagename → imagename Partial Fresh namespaces for supported imaging; restart=True continues on the products at imagename for every spectral mode, Taylor family and Stokes set casa-rs images (main image only), reusing the model, a CLEAN mask with no new mask, and with calcpsf/calcres=False the PSF, sums and residual. With restart=False the main image and its outliers share the next suffix, preserving relative and absolute directories and refusing an occupied destination. Same-prefix outlier continuation remains unfinished (#944). restartCatalog domain: path (image) signature, reader, lifecycle, restart-native-current, approved-comparisons-restart, numbering-activation, continuation-20261102 imsize [100] [100]; imsize → imsize Partial Positive even scalar/one/two dimensions; non-square standard/W/mosaic is implemented (#970). Unequal axes are implemented outside AW (#970). griddersCatalog domain: list[quantity], length 0..2; scalar allowed; Constraints: [{"kind": "positive"}] signature, reader, additions phasecenter '' ''; phasecenter → phasecenter or phasecenter_field Implemented Numeric text selects the phase center field. An explicit J2000, B1950 or ICRS literal supplies the main image's frame and two angles. Empty text uses the selected field direction. Catalog domain: string signature, reader stokes 'I' 'I'; stokes → stokes Partial Native Stokes/correlation coordinates; full-Stokes and basis-dependent combinations require their own acceptance, not an I-plane inference. With mtmfs every Stokes plane is a Taylor family of its own, cleaned and restored with its own beam (one beam under restoringbeam='common' or a given beam), and the spectral index is written only for Stokes I alone (issue 1065); Stokes planes other than I alone take the standard, mosaic, W-projection and awproject gridders (issue 1112); awp2 Taylor imaging remains Stokes I only (issue 1071), and Taylor imaging refuses a zero principal sum of weights and identifies a fully flagged first selected correlation when it removes the remaining channels (issue 1109). returnsCatalog domain: string signature, reader, mtmfs-nterms1-polarized-20261103, mtmfs-polarized-review-20261103 projection 'SIN' 'SIN'; projection → projection Unassessed SIN (default), NCP (written as SIN with [0, cot dec0], as CASA writes it), AZP with the zero parameters tclean writes, SZP with casacore padding to [0, 0, 90], AIR with the zero latitude parameter, TAN, ARC, STG, ZEA, CAR, SFL, PAR, MOL, PCO, TSC, CSC, QSC, MER and AIT: the image's direction coordinate records the projection and every placement on the image (mosaic and A-projection pointings, analytic primary beams, mask images, facet centres) converts through it; the gridded pixels do not depend on it, as in CASA. A name casacore does not know is refused as CASA refuses it. CASA also refuses COP, COE, COD, COO and BON when it constructs the projection before supplying parameters. A real Jy/pixel model, MFS or cube, in the image's direction and spectral frames; a cube start model of an MFS image or Taylor term is refused, as CASA refuses it (ImageRegrid::_checkAxes). It is regridded linearly over the direction and spectral axes (SIImageStore::regridToModelImage's ImageRegrid): a channel beyond the model takes the model's end channel, as casacore writes it into a model without a mask; a one-channel model onto a cube is refused (docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md). A plane no sample reaches restores its model with the image's largest beam, as CASA's restore does. Equal-count Stokes planes are copied positionally, warning when labels differ (owner decision 2026-10-31). Masked pixels become zero. Fresh restored standard one-facet Stokes I Högbom MFS with one outlier can use a separate Jy/pixel seed on each field. An omitted outlier startmodel key inherits the main seed, while an empty key clears it. The outlier owns its overlap for prediction and its model is copied back into the main field there (#1105). restartCatalog domain: list[path (image)], length 0..many; scalar allowed signature, reader, additions, default-products, numbering-activation, start-model-20261103 specmode 'mfs' 'mfs'; specmode → specmode Partial cont aliases mfs. Refused for continuation (#944, #980): existing outlier fields, another deconvolver family's products, a new user mask or auto-multithresh over an existing CLEAN mask when cleaning, embedded model/mask pixel masks and tabulated spectral axes. Preserving prior image histories remains the owner-agreed deviation. restartCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, lifecycle, restart-native-current, approved-comparisons-restart, numbering-preview, numbering-activation, continuation-20261102 savemodel 'none' 'none'; savemodel → savemodel Partial Copied. modelcolumn writes MODEL_DATA, at each time only the channels its bands select where CASA's final write is its last major cycle's; after nsigma, auto-multithresh, or niter=0 with calcres=False, CASA's final write is predictModel on the untuned parent selection, which casa-rs follows (issue 1134, PR 1197); a fresh run with niter=0, calcres=False and no start model writes zero to selected MODEL_DATA cells without creating a model image. virtual saves the final model as CASA's virtual model (casa_ms::virtual_model): the selection's fields'/windows' models are cleared first (VisModelData::clearModel), then the standard gridder's GridFT record (MultiTermFTNew over GridFT for mtmfs) and its FT_MODEL grid image are filed, incrementally, under SOURCE (rows and a known source) or MAIN keywords as CASA 6.7.6.14 files them; CASA predicts from them what it predicts from its own. A model of no flux saves nothing. Other gridders, polarizations than I, facets and outlier fields are refused (issue 823). returnsCatalog domain: modelcolumn, none, virtual signature, reader, virtual-model, model-column-bands-20261104 calcres True True; calcres → calcres Partial Contract 36: False runs no major cycle before the first minor cycle and cleans the residual an earlier run left at imagename, read with its sums of weights as the unnormalized normal state (task_tclean.py; not counted in nmajordone). With no residual and niter=0, calcpsf=True makes psf, sumwt and pb in a PSF-only pass. An explicit startmodel also publishes the output model, including with savemodel=none (#823). niter=0 with savemodel predicts the model (predictModel) and preserves any saved residual. Ordinary natural-weighted Stokes I Högbom mosaic cubes with a user mask may rebuild their PSF and then clean or restore the saved residual, or reuse both products with the saved sensitivity and PB (#944). Standard single-facet natural-weighted Stokes I Högbom MFS with outliers can rebuild the field PSFs while retaining each field's saved residual, or reuse both products (#944). Other mosaic and A-projection combinations, facets, and unsupported outlier combinations are tracked in #980. restartCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, continuation-20261102 calcpsf True True; calcpsf → calcpsf Partial Contract 36: False reads the PSF and sums of weights an earlier run left (each channel and Stokes plane, or a Taylor family's 2*nterms-1 moments) in place of gridding them; a complete saved PSF beam set is reused for the minor cycle and publication. Headerless PSFs fit at CASA's default cutoff before cleaning. MFS retains a complete saved PSF beam when recomputing, while cube gridding refits it. Refused: no earlier PSF or .sumwt, and mosaic, A-projection, facets or outliers (#980). restartCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, continuation-20261102, psfcutoff-restart-20261105 psfcutoff 0.35 0.35; psfcutoff → psfcutoff Implemented The requested cutoff fits a newly formed PSF and sets the beam used for minor-cycle sidelobes, Clark patches, automatic masking and publication. A complete existing PSF beam set is reused when calcpsf=False, and on MFS recomputation; cube gridding refits after discarding temporary PSF metadata. A headerless saved PSF is fitted at the default 0.35 before cleaning. Off-centre saved beams are subtracted at the image centre; an off-centre plane with no saved beam still uses its peak as its sidelobe pending #1140 item 6. The fit and sidelobe use both direction increments; rectangular-cell automatic masks retain the native support CASA 6.7.6.14 lacks. deconvolutionCatalog domain: float signature, reader, psf-off-centre-20261104, psf-off-centre-1130-20261104, psfcutoff-restart-20261105 parallel False False; parallel → parallel Partial Native local worker resource policy, not CASA MPI launch/partition semantics. Ordinary output equivalence and resource bounds require separate evidence; distributed behavior is unfinished. accuracyCatalog domain: bool signature, reader, adopted-defaults

docs.title: tclean interacting modes and task behavior
Selection and multi-MS inputs
docs.text:
Partial — vis, field, spw, timerange, uvrange, antenna, scan, observation, intent, datacolumn and selectdata (#54).

IDs/ranges, names/simple patterns, mixed field lists, SPW/channel text, intent and UV limits are routed natively. Sixteen field cases compare exact physical MAIN row order or refusal with CASA, including flagged and padded FIELD metadata. Since the main imaging cutover was integrated (3016f1b), FIELD selection resolves over the observation catalogue's FIELD rows on MSv2 and MSv4 alike; on the production traversal the field cases of the CASA row oracle (IDs, names, glob, mixed, range) and both refusals read exactly CASA's physical MAIN rows. Production T1 compares ID/name selections with selectdata=False on the single native route. Scan and observation selection is active from tclean contract 33 (owner decision 2026-11-02): on that path scan 1, scan 3 and observation 0 read exactly CASA's rows, and T1 images each numeric selection as its equivalent FIELD selection with either selectdata value and refuses CASA's refused forms without writing images. Through the public Python task, 13 science cases and 23 CASA grammar cases pass against CASA on CPU64, CPU32 and Metal32 (108/108). CODE/numeric-name fallback, advanced field forms, richer scan/observation grammar, remain unfinished; a vis list images as one observation from contract 38, as CASA's tclean does (awproject with several MeasurementSets is refused, #980); antenna and timerange are active from contract 34 (timerange on MeasurementSets only). Image-science comparisons for selected real datasets, flags, channel membership and data-column fallback remain separate required evidence.

Evidence: reader, representative, field-selection, cloud-continuation, scan-observation-activation, vis-list-20261102.

docs.title: Restart, product persistence and recalculation
docs.text:
Partial — imagename, restart, startmodel, calcres, calcpsf, restoration; main and outlier fields (#944).

Contract 36 continues every spectral mode, Taylor family and Stokes set of the main image and activates calcres/calcpsf (CASA test-case matrix at 4fe0e56: 11/48 restart/calcres/calcpsf cases pass, from 1/48 counting the 74a3b85 run's CASA refusals as environment failures; the rest are blocked by other gaps or an f32 scalar floor). Earlier: paired CASA 6.7.6.14 small standard Stokes-I MFS defaults pass (18 native 10->0->10 rows, 6 persisted nontrivial-mask cases, 6 CASA-to-native and 2 native-to-CASA continuations). Embedded model/mask pixel masks, tabulated spectral grids, new explicit/auto masks over occupied masks when cleaning, other outlier and direction-dependent restart variants and faceted restarts remain unfinished. An ordinary natural-weighted flat-noise Stokes-I Högbom mosaic can continue from its saved PSF and residual with a user mask or restore them without cleaning in MFS and cubes (#944). A natural-weighted Stokes-I Högbom MFS run with outliers and user masks can rebuild each field's residual from its saved model while keeping that field's PSF, positive sum of weights and PB (#944). With both PSF and residual saved, the same fields use their own saved residual for the first CLEAN boundary and keep it when no major cycle runs. A PSF without a stored restoring beam can be fitted. With a new residual pass, a field’s zero or negative saved sum of weights is refilled from the pass while a previously positive sum is kept. A run starting with saved residuals still requires positive sums for all fields. Concurrency at one prefix remains unassessed. CASA mutates prior logtables whereas native preserves them (owner-agreed). New-image history completeness remains unfinished. This is not general persistence or full metadata acceptance.

Evidence: reader, lifecycle, restart-native-current, approved-comparisons-restart, scalars-empty-mask, numbering-preview, numbering-activation, continuation-20261102.

docs.title: Cube axes, reference frequencies and moving sources
docs.text:
Partial — specmode, spw, start, width, nchan, reffreq, restfreq, outframe, veltype, interpolation and perchanweightdensity.

nchan=-1 takes CASA's count from the start or the first selected channel to the band's far edge in channel, frequency and radio-velocity grids, and interpolation='cubic' fits casacore's four-point cubic (#1066); standard LSRK optical-velocity cubes preserve CASA's stored frequency table, extrapolate extra planes by its last interval, and match channel gridding, prediction, and density weights (#1096). The other optical gridder and frame combinations and a constant table on multiple image planes remain scoped out; a cube over several selected windows lays its axis over their channels merged as CASA's MSTransformRegridder::combineSpwsCore merges them, grids every window's rows onto it, and with nchan=-1 counts a channel grid's planes over the merged band as regridChanBounds does (#980); MFS outframe (LSRK/BARY/TOPO, header only, gridding stays LSRK as in CASA) and restfreq lists (first active, the others listed in the header) are read; MFS REST outframe and blank restfreq entries remain restricted. Moving-source cubesource needs its own representative oracle (#714). Fresh standard MVC uses cube major cycles and Taylor minor cycles. The standard multi-SPW dirty and clean comparisons pass, with remaining cases on #1069. The moving-MFS spectral envelope now uses CASA FIELD-origin direction semantics; six fixed/moving CPU64/CPU32/GPU32 comparisons pass recorded WCS values, and the previous 3.5 Hz increment mismatch is repaired at its unchanged tolerance. This does not complete moving-PB or cubesource acceptance. The ordinary MFS default SOURCE rest-frequency label is now repaired; five fresh mosaic/AW weight families and small restart metadata checks match. DOPPLER-backed SOURCE lookup and multiple SOURCE key groups with stored wildcards are explicitly unfinished, not approved deviations. The MFS header's first visibility field is the least (ARRAY_ID, DATA_DESC_ID, FIELD_ID) of the selected samples, CASA's buffer order: the MSv2 adapter states each partition's array and the survey reads the rows' arrays for a partition holding several (3bdf6fa, after Astra's review found the merge had dropped ARRAY_ID); a T1 run with opposing arrays records CASA's choice. An MSv4 has no arrays. The moving-MFS increment oracle on the catalogue path gives CASA's 125020996.11132812 Hz exactly (8b0fe44).

Evidence: reader, representative, mvc-decision, taylor-pb-mfs, approved-comparisons-restart, cloud-continuation, cube-axes-20261103.

docs.title: Gridder, weighting and beam combinations
docs.text:
Partial — Standard, W projection, mosaic, AW projection and bounded AWP2; geometry, facets, normalization, beam terms and density weighting.

AWP2’s single-field dirty, two-field clean with model-column write, nonzero-W continuum, squinted Stokes IV continuum, and line cubes with single-channel windows or nearest interpolation agree with CASA (#1071). The named unsquinted Stokes continuum and cube cases also agree. The two-term MFS case also agrees across both selected fields and three single-channel windows. The one-field natural flat-noise AWP2 cube-major-cycle case agrees on both cube and Taylor products. The named two-field, uniform-weighted Stokes I AWP2 case with squint and four W planes agrees with CASA when its sensitivity FFT uses double precision. The release CASA Float FFT can change four pixels at the primary-beam cutoff. The raw and controlled comparisons are recorded in the CASA defect notes. Rectangular standard/W/mosaic and uvtaper were implemented in #970. AW remains square/equal-cell, and images MFS, MT-MFS and cubes whose selected windows hold one channel each; multi-channel cubes also run with nearest interpolation in the data, LSRK, tracked TOPO or tracked BARY frame, or from TOPO into the moving source REST frame with natural weighting (#1121), and linear interpolation between LSRK, tracked TOPO and tracked BARY with natural, Briggs or uniform weighting or from TOPO into moving source REST with natural weighting, and cubic interpolation between LSRK, tracked TOPO and tracked BARY with natural, Briggs or uniform weighting or from TOPO into moving source REST with natural weighting. The one-field cubic REST AW route also supports Briggs and uniform with per-channel density and no UV taper. The native TOPO data-frame route supports natural nearest, linear and cubic (each plane its own weight image, issue 719; remaining combinations wait for issue 1121); it reads tclean's aterm, psterm, wbawp, conjbeams and any positive wprojplanes (#980), and an imported CASA cache must already exist: where cfcache names a missing directory CASA fills it, casa-rs refuses (aw_cf_source=native-evla generates its own). The imported two-field test_mosaic_mtmfs caches agree with CASA for both beam choices, including pointing with uniformly odd cache buffers (#1214, #1070). Mixed-parity caches use each selected buffer's own pointing origin, avoiding CASA's reuse of a wider gradient array (#1070). On same-prefix continuation CASA can multiply the saved higher Taylor weight planes again. casa-rs recomputes the weights with the PSF and agrees with fresh CASA controls (#1315, #1070). Continuation with calcpsf=False,calcres=True reuses the saved AW PSF and weights (#1317); two-term PB correction is also supported in this case (#1318). Mosaic per-field density weighting (mosweight) is implemented, continuum and a cube's per-channel density (BriggsCubeWeightor multiField, #818); W/AW facets and additional gridders/weightings remain incomplete. Native CF generation is verified separately from CASA cache oracles. The native write_pb default is True. Homogeneous ALMA-labelled 7m arrays select ACA; legacy VLA PB now covers all named bands and NVSS frequency gaps. Fresh ordinary-default W/Hogbom20 CPU64/CPU32 runs pass all seven products, with PB NRMS zero. EVLA/VLA mosaics grid with CASA's common EVLA primary beam (HetArrayConvFunc COMMONPB, PBMath1DEVLA) at the first buffer's LSRK frequencies and MosaicFT's sector edges; conjbeams on one-plane mosaics grids with CASA's widened, resampled conjugate cell (#980). Moving/nonconstant FIELD directions, mixed dish classes, unsupported telescopes and remaining EVLA bands are unfinished. Explicit GPU W/AW remains refused. CASA Float channel-frequency narrowing is now matched in shared Taylor factors. All five fresh mosaic/native-AW MT-MFS rows pass the owner-approved scoped weak weight.tt1 rule and retained original recorded checks; 3 override only raw weight.tt1 relative-error failures. Exact guards and 1e-6 matrix-scale limits remain. Full metadata is separate. Existing #690 odd-sumwt scaling remains distinct. Legacy VLA cube PB takes CASA's channel-zero aperture scaled per channel: both T1.5 VLA cube rows give .pb NRMS 0.0 at 9768bb1, 3016f1b and 2628d8b (pre-candidate 0.0136); independent review pending. Cube Briggs density cells now use CASA's negated u and v (2628d8b): all 3,056,967 point-cube-briggs (row, channel) weights match CASA's to 1.35e-7, where 7 exact Float ties previously read a neighbouring cell.

Evidence: reader, additions, representative, default-products, compensated-current, taylor-pb-mfs, approved-comparisons-restart, cloud-continuation, awp2-dirty-mfs.

docs.title: Deconvolution, masks and stopping
docs.text:
Partial — Hogbom, Clark, Clark-Stokes, multiscale, MT-MFS, iteration controls, user masks and auto-multithresh.

Clark-Stokes uses Clark's solver on each polarization separately, while Clark jointly selects and updates a channel's polarization planes (#1126). Five paired CASA 6.7.6.14 I, IV, IQUV, IV-cube and masked-IV runs agree in every returned minor-cycle row and all seven image products; worst product NRMS 5.63e-6. The owner approved contract31's native CASA-inclusive Hogbom default, preserving explicit strict. Normal-build ordinary Hogbom10 point-source comparisons pass seven products on CPU64/CPU32/GPU32 with no explicit accounting option; prototype ALMA mosaic CLEAN also passes in that mode. Independent default-continuation and migration tests pass. ASP, MEM, MT-MFS nterms=1, PB masks/pbsquare, several auto-mask controls, explicit restoring beams are incomplete or refused. The shared nmajor=-1/0/positive domain is implemented;20 small paired CLI/Python rows verify initial-only products, threshold/zero-mask precedence, seed retention and exact counts. Compare convergence/flux/beam and exact mask support separately; nonlinear component identity is not required, but approved mode-specific gates stay binding. The owner accepted only the original identity-bound b6a87 clean8/cpu32 weak model result; raw model.tt1 NRMS 0.0012759712 remains recorded. No general weak-model waiver or automatic future-output acceptance exists. Explicit all-zero image masks now stop with CASA code 7 for the verified standard-MFS cases; existing nonzero models are preserved on empty-mask restart. Broader mode combinations still require evidence. Signed integer pixel-box clipping and explicit empty CRTF are repaired at086a67f1d4.36 CLI pairs pass recorded products/exact counts at two PB limits on three backends;2 public Python pairs additionally pass two selected scalars and old-file preservation under fresh numbering. General regions and other mask combinations remain unfinished. A plane whose published .sumwt is positive but at most CASA's 1e-07 bound is now empty as in CASA (zero PSF, residual, model and image; nothing cleaned), verified by a paired constructed-weight cube probe (8fcee92).

docs.title: Return values, exceptions and metadata
docs.text:
Partial — Python and CLI CASA return record, output topology, coordinates, beams, mask validity, model-column effects and reopen.

The recorded 22-key structure exists. Final maxpsfsidelobe and raw automatic cyclethreshold now report already-measured controller statistics with CASA Float rounding; 18 small pinned cases pass these two scalar checks, exact iteration/major/stop integers and recorded scientific products on CPU64/CPU32/Metal32. This does not verify every return key. summaryminor's rows are measured for each plane, and agree with CASA on 29 of 35 cases, the rest attributed (summary-rows-20261103). The fd7b8e7b2d full normal gate passes 4,698 workspace tests/45 skips and relevant checks. Each image holds tclean's history and CASA's object name, image type and miscinfo but memreq and memavail (image-history-20261103). Broader exceptions/mode combinations and representative persistence remain open. Earlier moving-MFS increment and ordinary SOURCE rest-frequency defects are repaired at their recorded revisions. Contract32 numbering adds20 small product rows, with19 raw selected-scalar passes and one identity-bound owner-accepted Metal cyclethreshold result (1.5132ppm difference). The original failed verdict remains; no future-output waiver. The owner agreed to native preservation of prior histories during fresh numbering; correct new-image history remains required. Nmajor-zero adds20 scoped product/count pairs; two public Python pairs also gate the two selected numeric scalars. Full return parity remains unfinished. The owner declined the native .summary.json sidecar (2026-11-02): a tclean run writes only its image products, as CASA's does, and the six-case replay now requires an exact product inventory; casars-imager writes the run summary only when CASA_RS_IMAGER_RUN_SUMMARY=1, for performance tooling. The handoff's point-cube-briggs maxpsfsidelobe raw failure (relative 8.2e-6 at 2851c6dc, 9768bb1 and 3016f1b) is attributed to those 7 boundary weights and passes at 2628d8b (relative 7.7e-8), with all six handoff cases passing both selected scalars.

docs.text:

The original compact PSF discrepancy is repaired. Current compact comparisons against CASA 6.7.6.14 pass within 7.1e-7 NRMS. Default Metal and CPU f32 pass the frozen 512-square four-window standard MT-MFS dirty and CLEAN rows with the existing primary-beam support rule. docs.title: interactive-headless: Agreed for now
docs.text:
• Inputs: interactive=True; graphical mask editing and pause/resume.
  • CASA: Uses casaviewer where available; 6.7.6.14 on macOS raises when the viewer is absent.
  • casa-rs: Refuses interactive=True explicitly; accepts False. Supply a mask or use supported auto-multithresh controls.

docs.title: mvc: Unfinished
docs.text:
• Inputs: specmode='mvc'.
  • CASA: Supports the MVC task path.
  • casa-rs: Supports the bounded fresh standard-gridder mode and same-prefix CLEAN with two supplied Taylor start models. Explicit Taylor start models use the saved cube and Taylor primary beams to project the first cube model. An ordinary restart reads the saved cube model for prediction and the saved Taylor terms for the solver. The three-SPW dirty, clean, PB-corrected and seeded clean references agree on all published images, masks, coordinates and controller counts. The original flat-noise mosaic case also agrees for dirty imaging and a ten-iteration clean, including the common-beam correction of both Taylor images. The original four-plane W-projection dirty and cleaned cases agree on both product families and controller counts. The original flat-noise AW-projection case also agrees with imported or natively generated cube caches, including both PB-corrected Taylor images.

docs.text:

  • CASA: Continues existing products by default, or chooses a numbered fresh prefix with restart=False.

Contract32 activates single-main fresh numbering; small public products/preservation pass. Other occupied namespaces, coordinated outlier/orphan numbering and calc flags remain unfinished.
