docs.title: simulator interacting modes and tool behavior
airy-blockage-ratio: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: The Airy beam's blockage term uses the inverse length ratio
  • Inputs: Any Airy primary beam with a central blockage, e.g. ALMA's default 10.7 m dish with 0.75 m blockage via setvp.
  • CASA: PBMath1DAiry::fillPBArray evaluates the blockage term at xD/b instead of xb/D, so main-lobe power is about 1% above the physical pattern (0.507 against 0.500 at the half-power radius).
  • casa-rs: Tabulates the same expression (AnnularApertureVoltageTable), matching CASA's predictions to 1.6e-7.
  • Rationale: ALMA's 10.7 m effective diameter was chosen against CASA's beam.
  • User impact: Beam-dependent predictions and images agree with CASA but are about 1% off the physical pattern.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: tai-stored-as-utc: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: The simulator stores TAI as UTC
  • Inputs: sm.observe with a reference epoch; the stored TIME column.
  • CASA: observe adds TAI seconds to the offsets and writes the result into TIME labelled UTC, so data start TAI-UTC (37 s since 2017) after the requested epoch; geometry reads the number as UT1.
  • casa-rs: Stores the requested UTC and also reads the stored TIME as UT1 for geometry, so uvw agree with CASA at equal TIME.
  • Rationale: The stored value should match its MEASINFO label; parity runs offset the start by TAI-UTC taken from the measures data.
  • User impact: Schedules and simulated calibration tables differ from CASA's by TAI-UTC (37 s today) unless the start is shifted.
  • Owner decision: Owner decision 5 of the simulation plan, accepted 2026-10-20 (docs/simulation/simulation-plan-20261020.md): TIME honours the requested UTC.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: shadowing-antenna-in-front: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: The simulator charges shadowing to the antenna in front
  • Inputs: sm.observe over antennas close enough to shadow each other.
  • CASA: NewMSSimulator::blockage leaves the blockage on the antenna in front (the one doing the blocking), whereas CASA's own flagger FlagAgentShadow flags the antenna behind.
  • casa-rs: Flags the antenna behind (ShadowedAntenna::Behind); the CASA convention remains available as CasaSimulatorFront.
  • Rationale: CASA's own flagger shows the intent: the antenna behind is the shadowed one.
  • User impact: Shadowed rows are flagged on the opposite antenna from CASA's simulator unless CasaSimulatorFront is selected.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: setspwindow-relabels-frame: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: setspwindow relabels every spectral window's frame
  • Inputs: setspwindow called twice with different frames, e.g. a TOPO window then an LSRK one.
  • CASA: Each call ends with measFreqRef().fillColumn(freqType), writing the new frame into MEAS_FREQ_REF for every row, so both windows end up labelled LSRK.
  • casa-rs: Writes each window's own frame.
  • Rationale: Frequencies were given in different frames, so each window must keep its own label.
  • User impact: Earlier windows get a wrong frame label in SPECTRAL_WINDOW.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: setconfig-unconvertible-coordsystem: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: setconfig accepts coordinate systems it cannot convert
  • Inputs: setconfig(coordsystem='longlat') or an unknown coordinate system name.
  • CASA: longlat2global logs SEVERE 'not yet implemented' (or initAnt 'Unknown coordinate system type'), the antennas are added at the Earth's centre, and setconfig returns True.
  • casa-rs: Raises RuntimeError for longlat; an unknown name logs CASA's message and returns False; neither adds antennas.
  • Rationale: An array with meaningless geometry should not be silently built.
  • User impact: A script continues with a meaningless array in CASA but stops or sees False in casa-rs.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: calls-before-setconfig-abort: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Simulator calls before setconfig abort the process
  • Inputs: setfeed or observe called before any setconfig.
  • CASA: The table slice over zero antennas throws std::runtime_error (an empty Slicer), which the tool binding does not catch, and the Python process aborts.
  • casa-rs: Raises RuntimeError from setfeed, and observe returns False with 'Antenna information not yet defined'.
  • Rationale: An unhandled C++ exception must not kill the interpreter.
  • User impact: A mis-ordered script gets a normal error instead of a process abort.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: zero-integration-time-unbounded-rows: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: A zero integration time adds rows without bound
  • Inputs: settimes() with no arguments (0 s) or integrationtime of zero, then observe over a nonzero span.
  • CASA: settimes only asserts the time is not negative; observe divides the span by zero and adds billions of rows before the disk fills.
  • casa-rs: Observe returns False for a non-positive integration time ('observe: the integration time must be positive').
  • Rationale: A zero integration time cannot define a schedule.
  • User impact: The script stops cleanly instead of exhausting the disk.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: predict-rewrites-model: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: sm.predict rewrites the model image
  • Inputs: sm.predict with model images.
  • CASA: createSkyEquation opens each model as PagedImage, forces LSRK spectral conversion and Hz units and stores it back, so predicting rewrites the model's table.dat.
  • casa-rs: Converts the spectral axis to Hz in memory and never writes the model.
  • Rationale: A prediction should not modify its input.
  • User impact: Models stay as the user wrote them; CASA's oracle copies models per call.
  • Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: predict-unreadable-models: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: sm.predict accepts models the simulator cannot read
  • Inputs: sm.predict with a FITS model or a complex-valued CASA image.
  • CASA: The binding checks with ImageFactory::fromFile, but the simulator reads PagedImage; predict logs 'Failed to create SkyEquation', returns False, and the script continues with DATA unpredicted (read from source, not probed).
  • casa-rs: Checks each model by opening it as the simulator reads it, so predict raises RuntimeError 'Unable to open image ...'.
  • Rationale: The check should match what is later read.
  • User impact: Unreadable models fail loudly at the call.
  • Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: negative-component-under-beam: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: A negative component turns positive under the primary beam
  • Inputs: sm.setvp(dovp=True) with a negative-flux component, e.g. -0.4 Jy point 20 arcsec off centre.
  • CASA: The fullspectral beam path multiplies by a spectrum sample over abs(flux), restoring the sign twice, so a negative flux comes out positive (+0.4 Jy times the beam).
  • casa-rs: Keeps the sign.
  • Rationale: A beam attenuates; it should not change the flux's sign.
  • User impact: Negative components predict with the right sign under a beam.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: beam-component-spectrum-lsrk-label: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: The primary beam's component spectrum labels topocentric samples LSRK
  • Inputs: Component prediction with the primary beam on (setvp) over channels with a topocentric-LSRK difference.
  • CASA: The full-spectral beam path stores products at the channels' LSRK frequencies, labels the table LSRK, and SkyCompRep::visibility reads it at topocentric frequencies, shifting each channel by up to about 1e-4 of the frequency.
  • casa-rs: Evaluates the beam and spectrum at each channel's own frequency.
  • Rationale: The table's frame label and lookup frequencies should agree.
  • User impact: With the beam on, scenarios agree with CASA to 7e-5 and 1e-4 normalized RMS instead of 1.3e-5.
  • Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: setmosaicfield-grid-offset: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: setmosaicfield sits its grid off the field centre
  • Inputs: setmosaicfield with a 3x3 or 2x2 grid at 1 arcmin spacing.
  • CASA: The odd-count test (nx/2)!=floor(nx/2) on integers is always false, so every grid takes the even-count offsets; a 3x3 grid has RA offsets -1.5,-0.5,+0.5 spacings and Dec -2.5,-1.5,-0.5 (CASA 6.7.6).
  • casa-rs: Centres every grid at (i-(n-1)/2) spacings, divides RA by cos(dec), and keeps CASA's field names {sourcename}_{k}.
  • Rationale: The grid should be centred on the field centre.
  • User impact: Mosaic pointings sit at different offsets from CASA's, which are off-centre.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: observemany-pads-one-name: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: observemany pads one name with empty ones
  • Inputs: observemany with one source name (or one direction) and several pointings.
  • CASA: casatools pads the list with Vector::resize, giving empty names; pointing 1's field is '', observe raises 'Field 1: not yet defined' and observemany returns False (CASA 6.7.6).
  • casa-rs: Pads the same way and returns the same False, moving only the first pointing, but adds no rows before refusing.
  • Rationale: Follows CASA's outcome of refusing the call.
  • User impact: The call fails with the same message as CASA.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: observemany-rows-before-field-lookup: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: observemany adds rows before it looks up later fields
  • Inputs: observemany where a later pointing's field is not defined.
  • CASA: observe adds every pointing's MAIN rows before looking up later fields, so an undefined field raises with the rows added and FIELD_ID, TIME and UVW unwritten, and returns False.
  • casa-rs: Looks up every field before planning, so the call returns False with the same message and leaves no rows.
  • Rationale: A refused call should leave the MeasurementSet unchanged.
  • User impact: CASA leaves junk rows in the MeasurementSet after the error; casa-rs does not.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: predict-wprojectft-no-planes-crash: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: sm.predict through WProjectFT without planes crashes the simulator
  • Inputs: setoptions(ftmachine='wproject', wprojplanes=0 or -1) then sm.predict.
  • CASA: The simulator builds WProjectFT with no w statistics so the automatic branch gets a negative largest w and zero or negative planes; predict kills the Python process with a segmentation fault (exit 139, CASA 6.7.6).
  • casa-rs: Records the planes at setoptions as CASA does, and predict raises RuntimeError ('W projection needs at least two planes'); it follows CASA's other quirks of the machine.
  • Rationale: A segfault should be an error.
  • User impact: A bad plane count raises instead of killing the process.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: sdgrid-total-power-nonpositive-uvw: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: SDGrid predicts total power into cross-correlations with no positive uvw
  • Inputs: sm.predict after setoptions(ftmachine='sd') with cross-correlation rows whose u, v and w are all zero or negative.
  • CASA: SDGrid::get leaves out rows with max(uvw)>0, meant to keep cross-correlations at zero. The eight-antenna CASA 6.7.6.14 oracle reproduces nonzero total power in 56 of 112 cross-correlation rows, alongside 32 autocorrelations; raw DATA is retained in the committed fixture.
  • casa-rs: Predicts total power into autocorrelations only.
  • Rationale: The test was meant to keep cross-correlations at zero.
  • User impact: Cross-correlations of a single-dish prediction stay zero regardless of uvw sign.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record, predict-multiple-models-20261111.

docs.title: evla-beam-no-11052-fit: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: The EVLA's beam table has no 11052 MHz fit
  • Inputs: Simulated EVLA beam near 10.05 or 11.05 GHz (X band).
  • CASA: PBMath1DEVLA::init inserts 10948, then 10052, then 11180 MHz; the second 10052 (meant 11052) overwrites the first, so the map has no 11052 entry and coefficients differ by about 1% in the linear term (few 1e-3 at half power).
  • casa-rs: casa-rs's table (EvlaPowerPattern, shared with imaging) is CASA's map as built.
  • Rationale: Kept for parity with CASA's beam.
  • User impact: EVLA X-band beams match CASA's, including its typo.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: close-aborts-after-mosaic-predict: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: sm.close() aborts the process after a mosaic predict
  • Inputs: setoptions(ftmachine='mosaic'), a successful predict, then sm.close() (simobserve's own sequence).
  • CASA: CASA 6.7.6 sm.close() kills the Python process with 'Pure virtual function called!' and SIGABRT (exit 134); DATA is already complete on disk. The 14-case multi-image oracle reproduces the cleanup abort after sm.done(); a duplicate-model run also produced SIGBUS after preserving complete DATA.
  • casa-rs: Close returns normally; the CASA oracle runs these scenarios in a child process and records close as aborted.
  • Rationale: An abort at close is a defect, not behaviour to copy.
  • User impact: Scripts do not die at close in casa-rs.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record, predict-multiple-models-20261111.

docs.title: simulator-mosaic-machine-not-tclean: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: The simulator's mosaic machine is not tclean's
  • Inputs: sm.predict with setoptions(ftmachine='mosaic') compared with tclean(gridder='mosaic').
  • CASA: The simulator degrids through the earlier HetArrayConvFunc/SimplePBConvFunc/MosaicFT, which differ from tclean's in support radius, screen size, frequency cells, support search and channel frequencies (4.5-5.6e-3 NRMS on the #875 probe).
  • casa-rs: casa-rs's mosaic set takes either machine's rules (MosaicRules): imaging follows tclean's, the simulator its own.
  • Rationale: Parity with each CASA machine.
  • User impact: Simulated and imaged mosaics each match CASA's own machine and differ from each other by up to about 5e-3 NRMS.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: predict-moved-pointing-phased-on-field: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: sm.predict phases a moved observemany pointing on its field
  • Inputs: sm.predict over an observemany pointing moved off its field.
  • CASA: NewMSSimulator writes UVW at the moved direction but leaves FIELD unchanged, so predict (VisBuffer phase centre from FIELD) phases the pointing on its field; a source at the moved direction gets phases spread over +-180 deg (rms 101 deg).
  • casa-rs: Follows: UVW, elevation limit and POINTING at the moved direction, DATA phased on the field.
  • Rationale: FIELD is the only phase centre recorded, which every imager and calibrator assumes.
  • User impact: Moved-pointing DATA match CASA to 8.4e-6 NRMS or better.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: beam-moved-pointing-first-row: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: The beam on a moved pointing stays where the field's first row points
  • Inputs: setvp beam over a model, component list, total power or mosaic machine on a pointing observemany moved off its field.
  • CASA: VPSkyJones updates only when BeamSkyJones::changed fires and the pointing-direction comparisons are commented out, so every row of a field is beamed where the field's first-visited row points (0.652 of peak kept in both pointings in the probe).
  • casa-rs: Fresh and resumed interferometric image/component beams and mosaics follow each integration's POINTING independently of FIELD phase, correcting the stale cache. Fresh displaced total-power beam consumption remains explicit on #1299.
  • Rationale: None of CASA's outcomes is the beam the moved pointing sees.
  • User impact: Changing pointings receive the requested beam response. Raw CASA rows remain in the oracle; distinct equal-phase FIELD identities provide independent cache-reset controls.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: predict-corrupt-scratch-columns: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: predict and corrupt add scratch columns to a MeasurementSet without them
  • Inputs: sm.predict or sm.corrupt on a MeasurementSet without CORRECTED_DATA.
  • CASA: The VisSet constructor adds MODEL_DATA (1) and CORRECTED_DATA (DATA); predict sets CORRECTED_DATA to the new DATA and MODEL_DATA to 1, and corrupt sets CORRECTED_DATA to the corrupted DATA.
  • casa-rs: Writes DATA only, creates neither column after openfromms, and keeps existing ones in step with DATA.
  • Rationale: Plan decision 6: no scratch columns added as a side effect.
  • User impact: Output MeasurementSets lack MODEL_DATA and CORRECTED_DATA that CASA would add.
  • Owner decision: Owner decision 6 of the simulation plan, accepted 2026-10-20 (docs/simulation/simulation-plan-20261020.md): DATA only, unless a later step needs MODEL_DATA.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: gain-screens-read-past-transform: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: CASA's gain screens read past their transform
  • Inputs: setgain(mode='fbm') (and settrop(mode='individual')), corrupt.
  • CASA: fBM::initialize copies n values from a transform of length n-2 or n-3, reading the last two or three past the end, and the RMS normalisation includes them; amplitude scale varied 0.969, 0.966, 1.005 between runs and some antennas had unit gain throughout.
  • casa-rs: Transforms every slot, so screens have the documented scale; it refuses individual mode on fewer than six slots.
  • Rationale: Avoid reading out of bounds.
  • User impact: CASA gain scales vary from run to run; casa-rs screens are reproducible and at the documented scale.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: gain-screens-share-seed: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Gain screens of neighbouring antennas share a seed
  • Inputs: setgain(mode='fbm') on neighbouring antennas.
  • CASA: GJonesCorruptor::initialize seeds antenna a's receptor r screen with seed+a+r, so antenna a's second receptor and antenna a+1's first draw identical screens (measured identical amplitudes).
  • casa-rs: Keys each antenna's and receptor's screens apart.
  • Rationale: Independent errors should be independent draws.
  • User impact: CASA's neighbouring antennas have correlated gains; casa-rs's do not.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: setgain-random-about-zero: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: setgain(mode='random') draws gains about zero
  • Inputs: setgain(mode='random', amplitude=[0.05]) on a 1 Jy point.
  • CASA: simPar returns camp.ren1 + icamp.im*n2 without adding one: mean gain modulus 0.065 and DATA mean modulus 0.0046 Jy, nearly erasing the data (CASA 6.7.6).
  • casa-rs: Draws 1 + camp.ren1 + icamp.im*n2.
  • Rationale: Gain errors are multiplicative and near unity; the owner said follow CASA only if there is a good reason, which there is not.
  • User impact: random gains perturb the data instead of destroying it.
  • Owner decision: Owner, 2026-10-24 (#841 Phase 3): follow CASA only if there is a good reason for its behaviour, which there is not.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: autocorrelation-resets-term: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: An autocorrelation row resets its antenna's simulated term
  • Inputs: setgain or setleakage with autocorrelations written (CASA's default).
  • CASA: setSimulate sets ANTENNA1's value at every row and 1 at an autocorrelation, so the last antenna (ANTENNA1 only of its autocorrelation) has unit gain and leakage 1 throughout (antenna 42 of 43 in corrupt-gain).
  • casa-rs: Simulates every antenna's term, including settrop's Tf term.
  • Rationale: Every antenna should be corrupted.
  • User impact: CASA leaves the last antenna uncorrupted; casa-rs does not.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: setleakage-first-two-spws: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: setleakage simulates only the first two spectral windows
  • Inputs: setleakage(table=...) with three, four or eight spectral windows, then corrupt.
  • CASA: The table has solutions for windows 0 and 1 only; corrupt logs 'no (simulated) calibration' for later windows and leaves their rows uncorrupted (CASA 6.7.6; cause not traced).
  • casa-rs: Simulates a leakage for every window.
  • Rationale: All windows should be corrupted; setgain already does so.
  • User impact: Windows beyond the second are unchanged in CASA but corrupted in casa-rs.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: setleakage-one-per-window: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: setleakage draws one leakage per window for the whole run
  • Inputs: setleakage followed by corrupt over several scans, or setgain with interval=.
  • CASA: setleakage simulates with an infinite solution interval (one solution per window and antenna spanning all scans) and corrupt applies it as the linearised JonesGenLin, which raises on two-correlation data; setgain's interval is not used.
  • casa-rs: Follows both, and does not read setgain's interval.
  • Rationale: Parity with CASA's documented and observed behaviour.
  • User impact: Leakage is constant across scans; two-correlation data are refused as in CASA.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: term-table-written-when-set: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: A simulated term's table is written when the term is set
  • Inputs: setgain(table=...) or setleakage(table=...).
  • CASA: CASA writes the calibration table as soon as it simulates the term, replacing a table of that name, with subtables copied from the MeasurementSet as it then is.
  • casa-rs: Writes the table at close from the written MeasurementSet; rows are the same but subtables include what was observed after the call, and it refuses to replace anything but a table.
  • Rationale: casa-rs writes the MeasurementSet only at close.
  • User impact: The table appears later (at close) and its subtables include later observations.
  • Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: tsys-manual-stale-or-borrowed: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: tsys-manual noise takes stale or borrowed system temperatures
  • Inputs: setnoise(mode='tsys-manual') then corrupt, especially at low elevation, with rows observed after setnoise, changed integration time or shadowed antennas.
  • CASA: The airmass cache is up to 100 s stale (variance sawtooth 1.01 to 1.56), later scans take the nearest earlier integration's solution, every row takes the first row's EXPOSURE, and an antenna without an unflagged row applies as 1.
  • casa-rs: Computes each row's sigma from its own integration: airmass at the row's TIME, own EXPOSURE, window and dishes, regardless of flags; non-finite T keeps CASA's scale of 1.
  • Rationale: Each row's noise should follow its own conditions.
  • User impact: CASA's noise is wrong by up to 1.5x at low elevation or after changing the integration time; scenarios above 40 degrees agree.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: tsys-manual-scales-every-noise-term: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: A tsys-manual term scales every noise term
  • Inputs: Two tsys-manual terms, or simplenoise plus tsys-manual, then corrupt.
  • CASA: collapseForSim adds every ANoise term then applies every NoiseScale T term to DATA, so each term's scale multiplies all noise: variance 4 sigma^4 for two terms, and a 0.5 Jy simplenoise comes out scaled by the system temperature.
  • casa-rs: Adds each term's noise with its own sigma, so simplenoise stays in Jy and terms of one seed still add coherently.
  • Rationale: Owner: follow CASA only if its product is the better simulation, which it is not; powers of uncorrelated noise add.
  • User impact: Combined noise terms add in quadrature rather than multiply.
  • Owner decision: Owner, 2026-10-24 (#841 Phase 3): follow CASA only if its product is the better simulation, which it is not.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: refused-tsys-manual-leaves-noise: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: A refused tsys-manual setnoise leaves a unit noise term
  • Inputs: setnoise(mode='tsys-manual', pwv='200mm') or a zenith Tsys that is not positive or above 1e6 K, then corrupt.
  • CASA: setnoise creates the unit ANoise term before checking parameters; the refused call returns False but the ANoise stays and the next corrupt adds 1 Jy of noise (tsys-atm takes the same path, read from source).
  • casa-rs: Refuses such a setnoise without adding a term.
  • Rationale: A refused call should have no effect.
  • User impact: A refused setnoise no longer adds unexpected 1 Jy noise.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: tsys-atm-half-band-below: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: tsys-atm noise takes its atmosphere half a band below each channel
  • Inputs: setnoise(mode='tsys-atm') on windows spanning an atmospheric line (183 GHz) or a one-channel window after the first.
  • CASA: initAtm builds the ATM grid so channel c reads the atmosphere half a band below it (variance off by mean factor 6.1, up to 103 across 183 GHz), and a one-channel later window reads the channel map past its end, so its T was bad and applied as 1.
  • casa-rs: Evaluates ATM at each channel's CHAN_FREQ for every window, one-channel windows included; it also refuses a term whose zenith Tsys is not a number.
  • Rationale: A channel's noise should follow the sky it observes.
  • User impact: Noise across line features and for one-channel windows differs strongly from CASA's.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: settrop-dispersive-wet-delay: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: settrop turns the phase by the dispersive wet delay alone
  • Inputs: sm.settrop with default pwv and deltapwv.
  • CASA: cphase takes the zenith wet phase delay from getDispersiveH2OPhaseDelay (the dispersive part alone), which is 940, 119, 36, 23 and 8.5 times smaller than the whole wet delay at 43, 100, 183, 230 and 345 GHz.
  • casa-rs: Takes the whole wet delay (dispersive plus non-dispersive), so deltapwv means the fluctuation of the water column it names.
  • Rationale: The path a water column adds is mostly non-dispersive (Thompson, Moran & Swenson eq. 13.19).
  • User impact: CASA phases are too small (3 deg rms at 100 GHz); casa-rs phases are fully scrambled with defaults at millimetre wavelengths.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: settrop-half-band-below: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: settrop takes its atmosphere half a band below each channel
  • Inputs: sm.settrop on windows spanning an atmospheric line, or a one-channel window after the first.
  • CASA: cphase reads channel c of the same ATM grid as tsys-atm, so each channel's phase uses the atmosphere half a band below it, and a later one-channel window reads the map past its end.
  • casa-rs: Evaluates ATM at each channel's CHAN_FREQ.
  • Rationale: Same grid error as the tsys-atm noise.
  • User impact: Phases across the 183 GHz line spread by 2.5 of themselves in CASA relative to the channel's own frequency.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: settrop-screen-anisotropic: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: settrop's screen has an anisotropic spectrum
  • Inputs: settrop(mode='screen') on a screen long along the wind (e.g. 1359 by 271 pixels).
  • CASA: fBM::initialize uses index rather than wavenumber (stretching the spectrum along the wind), does not wrap the full axis, uses exponent -(beta+1/2)/2 (comment: 'still something not quite right'), and sets values past the half axis's end, copying the last two pixels from past the output.
  • casa-rs: Draws |k|^-(beta+1)/2 on wrapped wavenumbers in cycles per pixel with proper conjugate pairs and transforms every pixel, giving equal structure along and across the wind.
  • Rationale: Isotropic turbulence's phase spectrum depends only on spatial frequency size.
  • User impact: CASA structure functions differ by a factor of five between the axes; casa-rs's are the same.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: settrop-simint-stamp: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: settrop with simint stamps a solution halfway to its interval's start
  • Inputs: settrop with simint longer than an integration (e.g. simint=6 on 2 s integrations).
  • CASA: setSimulate stamps each solution (t0+t)/2, so times are 0,1,2,6,7,8 s for integrations at 0,2,4,6,8,10 s, and corrupt gives later integrations a slot from earlier in the interval.
  • casa-rs: Stamps each solution with its integration's time, as CASA does when simint is unset.
  • Rationale: Each integration should use its own time.
  • User impact: Time-varying troposphere in later integrations of an interval lags in CASA.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: atm-hcn-106ghz-line: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: ATM's HCN catalogue misplaces a line at 106 GHz
  • Inputs: Any ATM calculation near 106.3 GHz.
  • CASA: mkSpecificRefractivity_hcn lists the J=12-11 line as 106.298069519 GHz (decimal point moved from 1062.98), so ATM sums an HCN line there and none at 1063 GHz; zenith opacity 0.029368 against 0.028919 corrected, 1.5% high.
  • casa-rs: Moves the decimal point back (1062.98069519 GHz), one of four corrections in atm-corrections.patch.
  • Rationale: The catalogue (JPL c027001.cat) puts the line at 1062.98 GHz; owner decision.
  • User impact: Opacity near 106 GHz is about 1.5% lower than CASA's; elsewhere changes are below 3.5e-5.
  • Owner decision: Owner decision, 2026-10-24 (#841 Phase 4): ATM's data errors are corrected.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: atm-air-density-sea-level: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: ATM's reference air densities drop a digit at sea level
  • Inputs: ATM with mid-latitude, subarctic or US Standard atmospheres at sea level to 1 km.
  • CASA: st76's sea-level reference air densities lost their leading digit (.496E+19 etc., about 2.5e19 meant), so minor gases (O3, N2O, CO, NO2, SO2, HCl, HCN) are up to about four times too scarce in the lowest layers.
  • casa-rs: Restores the digit (2.496e19, 2.711e19, 2.549e19, 2.855e19, 2.548e19 cm^-3).
  • Rationale: Air density falls with height; US Standard gives 2.547e19 by the ideal gas law (owner decision).
  • User impact: Sites below 1 km see O3, CO, N2O line opacities up to 1.8%, 7.7%, 8.5% higher; sites at 1 km and above are unchanged.
  • Owner decision: Owner decision, 2026-10-24 (#841 Phase 4): ATM's data errors are corrected.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: atm-h2-17o-abundance: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: ATM weights H2(17)O by the (18)O abundance
  • Inputs: Any ATM wet opacity calculation.
  • CASA: ratiohh17o uses the (18)O abundance (0.0020439) where the (17)O abundance (0.000375) belongs, so H2(17)O lines are 5.45 times too strong.
  • casa-rs: Uses abun_17o, as ATM does for oxygen and ozone.
  • Rationale: The siblings use abun_17o (owner decision).
  • User impact: Wet opacity falls by up to 0.61% (990 GHz); at Chajnantor 230 GHz opacity moves by 2e-4.
  • Owner decision: Owner decision, 2026-10-24 (#841 Phase 4): ATM's data errors are corrected.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: atm-hdo-weight: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: ATM's HDO weight divides by three
  • Inputs: Any ATM wet opacity calculation.
  • CASA: ratiohdo reads 2-0abun_d for 2.0abun_d, so the denominator is 3.0024 instead of 1.0030 and HDO lines are about three times too weak.
  • casa-rs: Uses 2.0*abun_d.
  • Rationale: It is a typo; every sibling ratio uses 2.0*abun_d (owner decision).
  • User impact: At Chajnantor zenith opacity rises 0.32% at 230 GHz and 0.15% at 90 GHz; wet opacity up to 1.8%.
  • Owner decision: Owner decision, 2026-10-24 (#841 Phase 4): ATM's data errors are corrected.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: atm-hcn-profile-100km: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: ATM's HCN profile stops at 100 km
  • Inputs: ATM profiles topped above about 90 km.
  • CASA: hcn[50] is initialised with 45 values, so the last five levels (100 to 120 km) are zero and interpolated HCN falls to zero over them.
  • casa-rs: Follows it: there are no values to restore, and air above 90 km is about 2e-6 of the column.
  • Rationale: No data exist to replace the zeros.
  • User impact: Negligible effect, only on profiles topped above about 90 km.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: atm-profile-copy-bottom-pressures: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Copying an AtmProfile copies its top pressures as bottom pressures
  • Inputs: Copying an AtmProfile (via RefractiveIndexProfile or SkyStatus) then getLayerBottomPressure or setAltitude.
  • CASA: The copy constructor fills v_layerPressure0_ from a.v_layerPressure1_, so bottom pressures return the top pressures; no opacity, path or brightness calculation reads them.
  • casa-rs: Keeps one profile and never copies it through such a path.
  • Rationale: The defect cannot arise in what casa-rs ports.
  • User impact: No effect on results.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: atm-ozone-isotopologue-padding: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: ATM leaves the ozone isotopologue layers unpadded
  • Inputs: An ATM user profile with a layer that has zero ozone.
  • CASA: mkRefractiveIndexProfile pushes a zero onto the total-ozone vector only, so the eight ozone state and isotopologue vectors become shorter than the layer count and later layers' values shift down one place.
  • casa-rs: The document records no casa-rs action; ATM's standard profiles have ozone in every layer so it does not arise.
  • Rationale: Latent ATM bug that does not arise with ATM's own profiles.
  • User impact: Only user profiles with zero-ozone layers would be affected.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: atm-omits-16o17o: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: ATM omits (16)O(17)O
  • Inputs: ATM opacity near (16)O(17)O lines.
  • CASA: mkSpecificRefractivity_16o17o returns zero before its line loop; the comment says the isotope was removed in 2024 while its catalogue is reviewed because it gave lines that do not exist.
  • casa-rs: The port returns zero too and keeps the catalogue in its tables for the record.
  • Rationale: The omission is deliberate in ATM.
  • User impact: Results match ATM, without (16)O(17)O lines.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA's behaviour is deliberate or users' results depend on it, casa-rs follows it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: atm-averaged-nondispersive-wet-phase: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: RefractiveIndexProfile's averaged non-dispersive wet phase reads a channel as a water column
  • Inputs: RefractiveIndexProfile::getAverageNonDispersiveH2OPhaseDelay on a window (e.g. 22 GHz, 1.3 mm water).
  • CASA: The call getNonDispersiveH2OPhaseDelay(v_transfertId_[spwid]+i) converts the index to a Length in metres, returning channel 0's phase for a water column of 0, 1, 2 ... m, giving 306,132 degrees; CASA's at tool (SkyStatus) is unaffected.
  • casa-rs: casa-atmosphere takes the mean of the channels' phases.
  • Rationale: The overload resolution is an error.
  • User impact: The window-averaged phase is a few degrees, not hundreds of thousands.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: mosaic-multiple-models-cache-geometry: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Mosaic multi-image prediction depends on image order
  • Inputs: sm.predict with two differently sized Stokes I images through the mosaic machine, in both orders, compared with independent single-image predictions.
  • CASA: CASA 6.7.6.14 joint predictions differ from the independent sum by 0.00353/0.0326 NRMS, and swapping the images changes DATA by 0.0307. The public convolution-cache key omits image geometry; repeated identical images accumulate correctly.
  • casa-rs: Prepares every image with its own geometry and sums the predictions, matching the independent CASA single-image sum to 2.11e-6 NRMS.
  • Rationale: SkyEquation intends to add every model image. Reusing an earlier image geometry corrupts DATA according to model order.
  • User impact: Multi-image mosaic prediction is linear across models; raw defective CASA joint outputs remain recorded and tested separately.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record, predict-multiple-models-20261111.

docs.title: flagged-component-duplication: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Mixed image/component prediction doubles components at flagged samples
  • Inputs: Existing MS with independent sample and row flags, predicted from an image and a 0.25 Jy component, replacing and incremental.
  • CASA: Retains the component in skipped flagged samples, then adds it again; joint flagged DATA contains two component contributions.
  • casa-rs: Adds the masked image prediction and each component once, using independent CASA image-only and component-only sums as the reference.
  • Rationale: The sky-model sum must not double components when an image is present; the upstream accumulator retains and adds the previous model at skipped samples.
  • User impact: Corrected flagged mixed-model DATA; the raw defective joint CASA DATA remains recorded and its excess is tested.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record, flagged-samples-20261112.

docs.title: invalid-leakage-solutions: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Invalid leakage solutions become unit leakage
  • Inputs: D calibration table with either receptor flagged or an antenna missing; nearest/linear time interpolation.
  • CASA: Substitutes both leakage coefficients with one, adding parallel hands to cross hands;3+4j becomes9+12j on an autocorrelation. Data flags remain unchanged.
  • casa-rs: Uses the neutral zero leakage pair for that invalid antenna, preserving valid antenna/time solutions. G retains CASA per-receptor unit substitution.
  • Rationale: One is neutral for diagonal gain but fabricates leakage in the linear D operator.
  • User impact: Invalid calibration cannot manufacture large unflagged cross-hand signals. Raw defective CASA results remain recorded and C++ table consumption reproduces them independently.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record, apply-flags-20261112.

docs.title: natural-spline-first-knot: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: Natural-spline interpolation skips the first interior back-substitution
  • Inputs: Frequency-dependent complex table, natural-spline interpolation of amplitudes/phases; four-point Tf closed-form discriminator.
  • CASA: Leaves the first interior second derivative partly eliminated, producing a derivative discontinuity; the discriminator differs by NRMS0.0780.
  • casa-rs: Completes back-substitution at every interior knot. The exact half-knot amplitudes are independently checked and supplied through a separately sampled CASA table.
  • Rationale: Natural cubic splines require continuous first derivatives at every interior knot; skipping one contradicts the stated mathematical method.
  • User impact: Corrected frequency-interpolated values; raw CASA outputs and its consumption of native tables remain separately verified. Numerical tolerances are unchanged.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record, apply-frequency-20261112.

docs.title: simutil interacting modes and tool behavior
readantenna-stale-loop-variable: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simutil.readantenna averages a stale loop variable
  • Inputs: readantenna on a configuration file with absolute coordinates, no known observatory and no COFA header.
  • CASA: readantenna averages the UTM branch's loop variables x, y, z instead of stnx, stny, stnz: UnboundLocalError for an XYZ file, the last antenna for a UTM file; it also swaps latitude and longitude from xyz2long.
  • casa-rs: Converts the mean antenna position, as the code's comment intends (casa_simulation::readantenna).
  • Rationale: The comment shows the observatory was meant to sit at the mean antenna position.
  • User impact: Such configuration files work in casa-rs instead of raising or placing the observatory wrongly.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: readantenna-blank-line-names: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simutil.readantenna names antennas after blank lines
  • Inputs: readantenna on a configuration file with blank lines, e.g. CASA's own WSRT.cfg (two blank lines).
  • CASA: A line with fewer than four values is skipped but still gets a default pad and antenna name, so readantenna returns 16 names for 14 WSRT antennas starting A00, A01, RT0.
  • casa-rs: Skips such lines entirely.
  • Rationale: Names must stay aligned with positions.
  • User impact: CASA misnames every dish in a WSRT simulation; casa-rs does not.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: calc-pointings2-undefined-pbcoeff: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: calc_pointings2's ALMA tiling reads an undefined pbcoeff
  • Inputs: calc_pointings2 with maptype='ALMA' (or alma, ALMA-OT) and no primary beam (beam <= 0), e.g. simobserve with an ALMA map and no antenna list.
  • CASA: The default spacing_asecpbcoeffsqrt(3) uses pbcoeff, a local of task_simobserve.py not defined in simutil.py, so the call raises NameError (CASA 6.7.6).
  • casa-rs: Uses simobserve's value 1.13 (PBCOEFF), so the beam is spacing x 1.13 x sqrt(3).
  • Rationale: The default clearly intends simobserve's value.
  • User impact: The call works instead of raising NameError.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: noisetemp-table-edges: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: noisetemp reads the wrong receiver temperature at the edges of its tables
  • Inputs: noisetemp at exactly the first band edge (e.g. ALMA at 35 GHz, VLA 0.8-1 GHz, SMA 180 GHz) or above 900 GHz for an unknown telescope such as WSRT.
  • CASA: The lookup leaves z=0 at the first edge so t0[-1] (the last entry) is used (230 K instead of 28 K for ALMA at 35 GHz), and for unknown telescopes the test reads f0[2] before checking z and raises IndexError (CASA 6.7.6, WSRT at 950 GHz).
  • casa-rs: Takes the first temperature at the first edge and keeps the last temperature (200 K) above the last edge.
  • Rationale: The lookup was meant to return the band's own receiver temperature.
  • User impact: Receiver temperatures at band edges are right instead of wrapping around, and no IndexError.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: direction-splitter-no-epoch: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: direction_splitter cannot split a direction without an epoch
  • Inputs: direction_splitter on a direction without an epoch, e.g. '18h00m00 -23d00m00'.
  • CASA: It reads the longitude from field 1 and the latitude from field 2 whatever the count, so a direction without an epoch raises IndexError and an unmatched latitude raises AttributeError (CASA 6.7.6).
  • casa-rs: Refuses both with "can't interpret ... as a direction" (the message isdirection gives); more than three fields split as CASA splits them.
  • Rationale: A clear error is better than a traceback.
  • User impact: simobserve stops with a clear message instead of a traceback.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: modifymodel-axis-swap: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: modifymodel swaps axes into place and refuses a cyclic order
  • Inputs: modifymodel with a model whose axes are a cyclic order, e.g. [spectral, RA, Dec, Stokes].
  • CASA: The swapaxes loop orders only transpositions (e.g. the FITS order), leaving a cyclic order out of place so the check raises "internal error: I'm confused about the shape if your model data cube" with the new image already created and empty (CASA 6.7.6).
  • casa-rs: Permutes the axes, so any order of the four is written as [RA, Dec, Stokes, spectral].
  • Rationale: A model's axis order should not matter.
  • User impact: Models in any axis order work; CASA refuses cyclic orders.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: modifymodel-stokes-labels: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: modifymodel labels the new image's Stokes planes by their count
  • Inputs: modifymodel on a model labelled I and V, or on three unlabelled planes.
  • CASA: The written image takes its Stokes axis from ia.fromshape's default, labelling planes by count (I, IQ, IQU, IQUV), so I and V comes out I and Q and the V data are read as Stokes Q; three unlabelled planes come out IQU though modifymodel returns 'IQV'.
  • casa-rs: Keeps the model's labels and labels unlabelled planes as modifymodel reports them; circular or linear bases keep their labels, so flatimage and adding components refuse them.
  • Rationale: modifymodel itself returns the model's Stokes labels.
  • User impact: CASA mislabels non-I Stokes planes; casa-rs preserves them but refuses polarisation bases CASA relabels.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: modifymodel-incell-map: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: modifymodel indexes the map it makes of two cells
  • Inputs: modifymodel with incell given as a list of two cells.
  • CASA: incell = map(qa.convert, incell, ['arcsec','arcsec']) is then indexed as incell[0]; under Python 3 map returns an iterator, so it raises TypeError: 'map' object is not subscriptable (CASA 6.7.6).
  • casa-rs: Takes the two cells, converted to arcsec and used as given (signs included), as under Python 2; a single cell is unaffected.
  • Rationale: The code was written for Python 2.
  • User impact: A two-cell incell works instead of raising TypeError.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: ia-modify-default-measures-frame: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: ia.modify converts a component spectrum through the image's default measures frame
  • Inputs: ia.modify adding a component list to an image from ia.fromshape (as modifymodel and simobserve make), with spectra in a different frame, e.g. TOPO spectrum on an LSRK image.
  • CASA: Each spectral model converts its reference frequency through the image's default measures frame (geocentre, epoch 0, J2000 pole), shifting frequencies by a velocity no observation has, about 1e-4 of the frequency in CASA 6.7.6.
  • casa-rs: Converts when the image's conversion layer carries a real frame (epoch and observatory position) and otherwise takes the frequencies as they are.
  • Rationale: A meaningful conversion needs the observation's epoch and position, which such a sky model does not carry.
  • User impact: Frequencies and spectral-index fluxes differ from CASA by about 1e-4 on frame-mismatched components; matched frames agree to 1e-6.
  • Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: ismstp-any-zero-uvw: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: simutil.ismstp takes any zero UVW value for total power
  • Inputs: simobserve corrupting an existing MeasurementSet (obsmode='') whose first antenna name lacks 'TP' and which has more than one antenna.
  • CASA: The test uvw.all() == 0. is true when any UVW value is zero, not all, so an interferometer MeasurementSet with one zero coordinate is corrupted as single dish with wrong file names and sensitivity constant.
  • casa-rs: Tests whether every value is zero.
  • Rationale: The test is meant to detect total power data.
  • User impact: Interferometric data with one zero UVW value are handled as interferometry.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: bugs-record.

docs.title: xyz2long-y-offset: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Inputs: xyz2long on a datum whose x and y offsets differ, such as NAD27.
  • CASA: Computes the longitude as atan2(y-dx, x-dx), subtracting the x offset from y; long2xyz then xyz2long on NAD27 at ALMA moves the longitude by 2.2 arcseconds.
  • casa-rs: Subtracts dy, so xyz2long inverts long2xyz.
  • Rationale: The rest of the function subtracts (dx, dy, dz); recorded in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md as "simutil.xyz2long subtracts the x offset from y".
  • User impact: Longitudes on datums other than WGS 84 and NAD83 are correct; WGS 84's agree with CASA's.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: geodesy-casa.

docs.title: xyz2long-old-z-offset: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Inputs: xyz2long_old on a datum whose x and z offsets differ.
  • CASA: Its second term is (z-dx)2/er2, subtracting the x offset from z.
  • casa-rs: Subtracts dz.
  • Rationale: The rest of the function subtracts (dx, dy, dz); recorded in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md as "simutil.xyz2long_old subtracts the x offset from z".
  • User impact: Latitudes on such datums are slightly different from CASA's; longitudes and WGS 84's results agree.
  • Owner decision: Standing rule, AGENTS.md "CASA deviations" (owner, #1054): where CASA crashes, aborts, reads out of bounds, loses or corrupts data, or contradicts its documentation or evident intent, casa-rs corrects it.
  • Evidence: geodesy-casa.

docs.title: msg-verbose-single-post: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Inputs: simutil(verbose=True).msg(s, origin=..., priority=...)
  • CASA: Posts the message twice to its log: once with ANSI colour codes around [origin], WARNING and ERROR, once with WARNING and ERROR coloured; both at INFO.
  • casa-rs: Logs it once at INFO on casars., without colour codes; the report file is written as CASA writes it.
  • Rationale: Colour codes in a log record are terminal noise, and Python logging shows the message once to every handler.
  • User impact: A script that counts or parses CASA's duplicated, coloured lines sees one plain line.
  • Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
  • Evidence: helpers-casa.

docs.title: is4d-leaves-image-open: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Inputs: simutil.is4d on an image that is not CASA's 4-D order.
  • CASA: Returns False before ia.done(), leaving the shared image tool open; the next ia.open warns 'Another image is already open, closing first'.
  • casa-rs: Opens nothing that outlives the call; no warning follows.
  • Rationale: The warning reports CASA's leaked state, not anything about the image.
  • User impact: None on results.
  • Owner decision: Owner approved on 2026-11-05; see docs/simulation/owner-decisions-20261105.md.
  • Evidence: helpers-casa.

docs.title: correct-numerical-diagnostic-runtime-failures: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Inputs: sfBeam1d under NumPy 2; sensitivity with telescope/diameter/count, missing manual opacity or doimnoise=True.
  • CASA: Raises scalar-array TypeError, undefined-padnames UnboundLocalError, negative-Tsys SystemError or broken legacy imclean/clean errors instead of a numerical diagnostic.
  • casa-rs: Compute the supported beam/radiometer/image diagnostics through native calculations; validate missing opacity and require an array configuration for image noise.
  • Rationale: Return the declared simulation calculation where CASA fails before producing it; do not invent array geometry or a manual opacity.
  • User impact: Scripts receive a numerical result or a clear invalid-input error; existing successful configured calculations retain their numerical acceptance and approved noise/UTC fixes.
  • Owner decision: Standing AGENTS.md CASA-deviation rule: correct CASA failures that contradict the documented/evident intent; preserve deliberate observable behavior.
  • Evidence: numerical-diagnostics-20261114.

docs.title: ephemeris-quantity-duration: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Inputs: Public simutil.ephemeris without an MS and the constructor default or a supplied quantity-record duration.
  • CASA: Compares its quantity record to an integer and raises TypeError after partially drawing the figure.
  • casa-rs: Convert the duration quantity before comparison; default zero draws no observation bar, while positive durations draw their actual hour range.
  • Rationale: The constructor itself supplies a quantity record, and the helper evidently intends a time interval rather than a Python type error.
  • User impact: Default and quantity-duration calls work while preserving the independent CASA elevation/transit curve.
  • Owner decision: Standing AGENTS.md CASA-deviation rule: correct behavior that contradicts documented or evident intent; the existing checkpoint already records this correction.
  • Evidence: simulation-figures-20261114.

Radiometer phase correction
docs.text:

Dataset-scale release profiling follows functionality under #979.

docs.title: sparse-window-phase-reversal: Previously agreed
docs.text:
• Record: WVR global phase reversal can miss sparse spectral-window selections
  • Inputs: A direct wvr.gcal invocation with global phase reversal and a sparse spectral-window selection.
  • CASA: CASA 6.7.6.14 can leave selected windows unchanged when the selected position differs from the actual ID.
  • casa-rs: Reverse the phase of every selected spectral-window ID.
  • Rationale: Match the documented phase operation and the algebraic conjugation of the ordinary gains.
  • User impact: A sparse output selection produces the same reversed phases as the corresponding subset of an all-window reversal.
  • Owner decision: Standing CASA bug policy in AGENTS.md.
  • Evidence: parameter-options.

docs.title: wvr-failed-segment-assignment: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: WVR can move successful atmospheric fits into earlier segments
  • Inputs: Run the default segmented WVR retrieval on the pinned recorded ALMA observation.
  • CASA: Two successful fits take the first two time bounds after two other fits fail.
  • casa-rs: Keep each successful fit attached to its original observation segment.
  • Rationale: The retrieved atmospheric coefficients describe conditions in those segments.
  • User impact: Each calibration gain is evaluated against the corresponding atmospheric fit.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: recorded-alma.

docs.title: wvr-empty-retrieval: Proposed
docs.text:
• Record: WVR can dereference a missing single retrieval
  • Inputs: Request one fixed-interval retrieval and a negative one-second offset on the pinned observation.
  • CASA: The pinned CASA process exits with SIGSEGV after a failed-reference retry.
  • casa-rs: Return a failed retrieval without publishing a calibration table.
  • Rationale: A flagged or rejected fit leaves no coefficients to apply.
  • User impact: The caller can choose other intervals or a suitable reference antenna and retry.
  • Owner decision: Pending; not an accepted deviation.
  • Evidence: recorded-alma.

Single-Dish Sky Calibrationsdcal task 1 calibration 15 Generate and apply single-dish sky and system-temperature calibration. Single-Dish Gain Calibrationsdgaincal task 1 calibration 14 Solve single-dish double-circle gain calibration. Single-dish spectral smoothingsdsmooth task 1 calibration 14 Convolve selected single-dish spectra and publish a MeasurementSet. Single-dish spectral baselinessdbaseline task 1 calibration 38 Fit, subtract and apply spectral baselines to selected single-dish observations. Single-Dish Line Fittingsdfit task 1 calibration 21 Fit Gaussian or Lorentzian lines to selected single-dish spectra. Single-Dish Atmospheric Correctionsdatmcor task 1 calibration 29 Correct calibrated single-dish spectra for differential atmospheric emission.

optional Stage Parameters Hogbom iteration accounting policy: casa-inclusive (default) reproduces CASA's inclusive terminal component and reported count; strict limits physical updates to the requested budget write_pb parameter.write_pb@r1 bool true; optional Stages Write the primary-beam image; without it or pbcor, the standard and W-projection gridders write no .pb and no PB pixel mask, unlike CASA fitspw parameter.fitspw@r1 string "none"; optional Continuum Subtraction Fit SPW selector. fitorder parameter.fitorder@r1 integer 0; optional Continuum Subtraction Polynomial fit order. save_continuum_residual parameter.save_continuum_residual@r1 bool false; optional Continuum Subtraction Overwrite output-role selected cells in an existing CORRECTED_DATA column in placeSurface: Requires continuum subtraction; Parameter Concept ID / revision Type / unit Default / required Group Summary vis data.input.vis@r1 array<path (measurement_set)> ""; required Input Input MeasurementSet path or paths. mode flagdata.mode@r2 choice (13 values) "manual"; optional Flagging Flagging mode. autocorr flagdata.autocorr@r1 bool false; optional Selection Flag only the autocorrelations of the selection. inpfile flagdata.inpfile@r1 variant ""; optional Input File, files or list of flag commands to apply in list mode. reason flagdata.reason@r1 variant "any"; optional Input Select list-mode flag commands by their reason. tbuff flagdata.tbuff@r1 variant 0.0; optional Input Time buffer in seconds that pads each flag command's time range. spw ms.selection.spw@r6 variant ""; optional Selection CASA flagdata spw selector. field ms.selection.field@r8 variant ""; optional Selection CASA flagdata field selector. antenna ms.selection.antenna@r7 variant ""; optional Selection CASA flagdata antenna selector. uvrange ms.selection.uvrange@r4 variant ""; optional Selection Accepts a CASA variant and converts it to selector text during MeasurementSet selection. timerange ms.selection.timerange@r6 variant ""; optional Selection CASA flagdata timerange selector. correlation ms.selection.correlation@r3 variant ""; optional Selection CASA flagging agent correlation selection.Surface: Selects stored correlation planes for manual, unflag, quack and summary. Clip and unaveraged TFCrop support ABS, REAL, IMAG, ARG and NORM on receptor labels, derived Stokes and WVR. Their defaults skip stored-I buffers. Summary counts stored flags for an operator expression. Automatic averaging and remaining mode combinations are tracked by #1616. scan ms.selection.scan@r6 variant ""; optional Selection CASA flagdata scan selector. intent ms.selection.intent@r4 variant ""; optional Selection CASA flagdata intent selector. array ms.selection.array@r2 variant ""; optional Selection CASA subarray selection by ARRAY_ID. observation ms.selection.observation@r4 variant ""; optional Selection Accepts selector text or an observation ID. Preserve the input type for HISTORY. feed ms.selection.feed@r2 variant ""; optional Selection CASA feed IDs and feed pair selection.Surface: Selects the requested feed IDs or pairs. CASA 6.7.6.14 flagdata silently ignores this selector. clipminmax flagdata.clipminmax@r1 array<float> []; optional Clip Two values define the closed clipping range. Other lengths leave the range unset. datacolumn parameter.datacolumn.flagdata@r1 variant "DATA"; optional Data Visibility data column selected by the clip, tfcrop and rflag agents.Surface: Unaveraged TFCrop reads DATA, CORRECTED, MODEL, RESIDUAL, RESIDUAL_DATA, FLOAT_DATA, WEIGHT or WEIGHT_SPECTRUM. DATA and RESIDUAL_DATA use complex DATA when both observed columns are present. A string vector is recorded in HISTORY when the active agent ignores this argument. clipoutside flagdata.clipoutside@r1 variant true; optional Clip Flag samples outside the closed clip range when true, or inside it when false. channelavg flagdata.channelavg@r2 variant false; optional Clip Average selected channels before clipping or TFCrop.Surface: MeasurementSet TFCrop uses channel averaging. Calibration automatic agents use stored channels. MeasurementSet RFlag channel averaging remains on #978. chanbin parameter.chanbin@r3 variant 1; optional Clip Channel averaging width for clipping or TFCrop.Surface: Calibration automatic agents use stored channel samples. timeavg flagdata.timeavg@r2 variant false; optional Clip Average baseline integrations before clipping or TFCrop.Surface: MeasurementSet TFCrop uses time averaging. Calibration automatic agents use stored integrations. MeasurementSet RFlag time averaging remains on #978. timebin parameter.timebin@r2 string "0s"; optional Clip Averaging time bin, a time quantity as CASA writes it.Surface: Calibration automatic agents parse this value when time averaging is requested. clipzeros parameter.clipzeros@r1 bool false; optional Flagging Flag exact zero amplitudes in clip mode. quackinterval parameter.quackinterval@r1 variant 1.0; optional Quack Quack interval in seconds. quackmode parameter.quackmode@r2 variant "beg"; optional Quack Which part of each scan quack flags, as CASA names it: 'beg' its first quackinterval, 'endb' its last, 'end' all but its last, 'tail' all but its first. quackincrement flagdata.quackincrement@r1 variant false; optional Quack Quack successive intervals, taking existing flags into account. tolerance flagdata.tolerance@r2 variant 0.0; optional Shadow Shadowing in metres that shadow mode tolerates. addantenna flagdata.addantenna@r2 variant ""; optional Shadow Antennas, from a file or dictionary, that shadow mode adds. lowerlimit flagdata.lowerlimit@r2 variant 0.0; optional Elevation Lowest elevation, in degrees, that elevation mode keeps. upperlimit flagdata.upperlimit@r2 variant 90.0; optional Elevation Highest elevation, in degrees, that elevation mode keeps. ntime flagdata.ntime@r2 variant "scan"; optional Automatic Visibility iterator time chunk: 'scan', a duration string, or seconds.Surface: Time-averaged clipping, TFCrop and flag extension process each iterator chunk independently. Calibration automatic agents follow stored scan boundaries. MeasurementSet RFlag chunk controls remain on #1616. combinescans flagdata.combinescans@r1 bool false; optional Automatic Let the automatic modes' time chunks span scans. timecutoff parameter.timecutoff@r1 float 4.0; optional Automatic TFCrop time cutoff in robust sigma units. freqcutoff parameter.freqcutoff@r1 float 3.0; optional Automatic TFCrop frequency cutoff in robust sigma units. timefit flagdata.timefit@r1 string "line"; optional Automatic Fit tfcrop makes along time: 'line' or 'poly'. freqfit flagdata.freqfit@r1 string "poly"; optional Automatic Fit tfcrop makes along frequency: 'line' or 'poly'. maxnpieces flagdata.maxnpieces@r2 variant 7; optional Automatic Number of pieces in tfcrop's piecewise polynomial fits. flagdimension flagdata.flagdimension@r1 string "freqtime"; optional Automatic Directions tfcrop flags along: 'freq', 'time', 'freqtime' or 'timefreq'. usewindowstats flagdata.usewindowstats@r1 string "none"; optional Automatic Sliding-window statistics tfcrop adds: 'none', 'sum', 'std' or 'both'. halfwin flagdata.halfwin@r2 variant 1; optional Automatic Half-width of tfcrop's sliding window. extendflags parameter.extendflags@r1 bool true; optional Extend Run post-extension after automatic flagging. winsize flagdata.winsize@r2 variant 3; optional Automatic Number of time steps in rflag's sliding window. timedev parameter.timedev@r3 optional<variant> (states: , none) ""; optional Automatic Explicit RFlag time threshold.Surface: Set a scalar, field/SPW/threshold rows or a CASA threshold file. Calculate mode can write the fitted values to a file. freqdev parameter.freqdev@r3 optional<variant> (states: , none) ""; optional Automatic Explicit RFlag spectral threshold.Surface: Set a scalar, field/SPW/threshold rows or a CASA threshold file. Calculate mode can write the fitted values to a file. timedevscale flagdata.timedevscale@r1 float 5.0; optional Automatic Factor that scales rflag's time-deviation threshold. freqdevscale flagdata.freqdevscale@r1 float 5.0; optional Automatic Factor that scales rflag's frequency-deviation threshold. spectralmax flagdata.spectralmax@r1 float 1000000.0; optional Automatic rflag flags a whole spectrum whose deviation exceeds this. spectralmin flagdata.spectralmin@r1 float 0.0; optional Antint Fraction of flagged channels at which antint flags an integration. verbose parameter.verbose@r1 bool false; optional Antint Verbose logging. extendpols parameter.extendpols@r2 variant true; optional Extend Extend flags across correlations. growtime flagdata.growtime@r2 variant 50.0; optional Extend Percentage of flagged time at which extend mode flags a whole channel. growfreq flagdata.growfreq@r2 variant 50.0; optional Extend Percentage of flagged channels at which extend mode flags a whole time step. growaround flagdata.growaround@r1 bool false; optional Extend Extend flags to points mostly surrounded by flags. flagneartime flagdata.flagneartime@r1 bool false; optional Extend Flag the time steps either side of each flagged one. flagnearfreq flagdata.flagnearfreq@r1 bool false; optional Extend Flag the channels either side of each flagged one. minrel flagdata.minrel@r1 float 0.0; optional Summary Smallest flagged fraction a summary entry reports. maxrel flagdata.maxrel@r1 float 1.0; optional Summary Largest flagged fraction a summary entry reports. minabs flagdata.minabs@r1 integer 0; optional Summary Report flags per spectral window and channel in the summary. spwcorr flagdata.spwcorr@r1 bool false; optional Summary Report flags per spectral window and correlation in the summary. basecnt flagdata.basecnt@r1 bool false; Can either be integer to be multiplied by the representative integration time, a quantity (string) in time units slidetimebin weightstats.slidetimebin@r1 bool false; optional Weights Use a sliding window for time binning, as opposed to time block processing? chanbin weightstats.chanbin@r1 variant "spw"; optional Weights Channel bin width for computing weights. A negative value means use the entire data set (ie default to the "classic" algorithm). Ignored if statalg is not "hinges-fences". center weightstats.center@r1 string "mean"; optional Weights Center to use for statalg="fit-half". Valid choices are "mean", "median", and "zero". Ignored if statalg is not "fit-half". lside weightstats.lside@r1 bool true; optional Weights For statalg="fit-half", real data are <=; center? If false, real data are >= center. Ignored if statalg is not "fit-half". zscore weightstats.zscore@r1 float -1.0; optional Weights For statalg="chauvenet", this is the target maximum number of standard deviations data may have to be included. If negative, use Chauvenet's criterion. Ignored if statalg is not "chauvenet". maxiter weightstats.maxiter@r1 integer -1; optional Weights For statalg="chauvenet", this is the maximum number of iterations to attempt. Iterating will stop when either this limit is reached, or the zscore criterion is met. If negative, iterate until the zscore criterion is met. Ignored if statalg is not "chauvenet". fitspw weightstats.fitspw@r1 string ""; optional Weights Channels to include in the computation of weights. Specified as an MS select channel selection string. excludechans weightstats.excludechans@r1 bool false; optional Weights If True: invert the channel selection in fitspw and exclude the fitspw selection from the computation of the weights. wtrange weightstats.wtrange@r1 array<float> []; optional Weights Range of acceptable weights. Data with weights outside this range will be flagged. Empty array (default) means all weights are good. flagbackup parameter.flagbackup@r1 bool true; optional Weights Create a flagmanager backup before mutating flags. preview weightstats.preview@r1 bool false; optional Weights Preview mode. If True, no data is changed, although the amount of data that would have been flagged is reported. datacolumn weightstats.datacolumn@r1 string "corrected"; optional Weights Data column to use to compute weights. Supported values are "data", "corrected", "residual", and "residual_data" (case insensitive, minimum match supported).
