docs.title: Simulation equivalence: owner decisions of 2026-11-05
docs.text: The owner approved the simulation equivalence proposals presented on 2026-11-05 for #1053. The approvals apply to the specific behavior and evidence recorded in the compatibility reference and the linked work below; they do not imply that unimplemented methods or unrelated deviations are complete.

docs.title: Audit proposals
docs.text:
The owner approved these existing behaviors, numbered as presented:

  1. Start the measures tool with an empty frame and require the missing frame elements for conversions.
  2. Keep sm.predict from rewriting its input model image.
  3. Raise for a model the simulator cannot read.
  4. Evaluate the component spectrum and primary beam at each channel's own frequency instead of reproducing the CASA spectral-frame shift.
  5. Write simulated gain and leakage tables at close, with the resulting table timing and subtable differences.
  6. Keep the supplied component flux precision.
  7. Withdraw the proposed difference in component shape record units and match CASA's in-memory units. This is unfinished: #1187 tracks torecord and #1185 tracks getshape.
  8. Convert a component spectrum through a real image measures frame when available; otherwise retain the input frequencies rather than convert through CASA's placeholder frame.
  9. Make simobserve project paths work using the directory's final name.
  10. Preserve the exact single direction supplied to simobserve.

docs.title: Later proposals
docs.text:
• Raise ValueError for scalar non-finite or cyclic component selections, leaving the selection unchanged, rather than aborting the process (#1176).
  • Preserve big-endian integer arrays' values in quantity records rather than reproduce CASA's byte-order corruption (#1183).
  • For componentlist.isphysical() on an empty list, use a catchable error rather than exiting the process; implementation and populated-list comparison remain open (#1158).
  • Follow casacore's observatory table interpretation even for the problematic rows; retain the EVLA fallback (#1111).
  • Retain whitespace trimming in the Rust MDirection::from_source_name and casacore's HI override (#1114).
  • Log a verbose simutil.msg once without terminal color codes, name its logger casars.<origin>, and leave no image open after is4d (#1116).

The comparison inputs, CASA and casa-rs behavior, rationale and impact are in the generated CASA compatibility reference and CASA bug records.

docs.title: Simulation programme: CASA's sm, simobserve, simanalyze and simalma in Rust
docs.text: Truth class: normative plan Date: 2026-10-20 Work issue: #841, which keeps the phase checklist and status Status: accepted by the owner on 2026-10-20.

docs.title: 1. Goal and requirements
docs.text:
Make CASA simulation scripts run on casa-rs with only their imports changed, and run them dramatically faster:

  • the simulator tool (sm), with every user-facing method under CASA's name, signature and effective default;
  • the simobserve, simanalyze and simalma tasks, with CASA's parameters and defaults.

Requirements:

  • ADR-0017 applies. All computation is in Rust, including the parts CASA writes in Python (task_simobserve.py, task_simanalyze.py, task_simalma.py, simutil.py); Python only presents CASA's interface.
  • Agreement with CASA follows AGENTS.md. The MS has CASA's columns, subtables and keywords, apart from decision 6; predicted visibilities agree to about 1e-3 normalized RMS; noise and corruptions are statistically equivalent, not bit-identical. casacore C++ reads the MS, proved by an interop test.
  • Performance is the point. Prediction uses Metal where it pays; geometry, prediction, corruption and writing use multiple workers; results do not depend on the worker count or the backend. Every benchmark reports wall time, single-worker (W1) user CPU and peak RSS, so parallelism cannot mask serial cost. The targets are in §5.
  • Memory is bounded. Peak resident memory stays under a declared budget whatever the number of rows, channels or fields, proved by a counting-law test. Work streams in time and channel chunks sized from the budget, and Metal device buffers count against it. The MS write session stays bounded (ADR-0008).
  • The MS write path may be optimized; what is on disk may not change. The same storage managers, tile formats and table metadata, guarded by the casacore C++ interop tests. The simulator writes every row in the layout casa-rs's other MS writers share, not NewMSSimulator's.

docs.title: 2. Status
docs.text: Phases 1 to 5 are merged, except 5e (simobserve graphics), which is now part of #1025. By the owner's priority of 2026-10-31 (#841), the new tasks of Phase 6 wait until the existing conversions reach behavioral equivalence with CASA; their design and dependencies stand (§6). Phase 7 follows.

docs.title: 3. Owner decisions (accepted 2026-10-20)
docs.text:
1. Namespace. CASA tool classes are in casars.tools under casatools' names, tasks in casars.tasks; there are no casatools or casatasks alias packages (ADR-0017).
  2. The simobserve surface is CASA's. The old family generator is the developer binary synthetic-ms, outside the catalog.
  3. casa-simulation is an application-layer crate in ADR-0016's dependency policy. simulation.rs, simulation_task.rs and casa-simulation-synthesis are deleted at the end (Phase 7).
  4. ATM is ported to Rust as casa-atmosphere.
  5. TIME honours the requested UTC. CASA computes its geometry at the requested time + (TAI − UTC); the divergence is recorded in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md. A parity run requests a start later by TAI − UTC at the reference epoch and compares rows at equal stored TIME.
  6. DATA only, unless a later step needs MODEL_DATA. MODEL_DATA is created only when something needs it, and CORRECTED_DATA is not written. casa-rs's imager falls back from datacolumn='corrected' to DATA, as CASA's tclean does.

docs.title: Deferred, single-pass execution
docs.text: The session records observe, predict and corrupt as a plan and, at close/done, materializes the MS in one streamed pass (geometry, prediction, corruption and the write for each chunk), published at close as ADR-0008 staging requires. The plan is a fold: each predict and corrupt applies to the scans observed before it, and a predict that is not incremental replaces every step before it. A call that needs data on disk forces the pending pass. Corrupting an existing MS (openfromms + corrupt) patches it in place through the bounded selected-row mutation path, in chunks aligned to the DATA tile.

docs.title: Prediction
docs.text: Prediction goes through the imaging operator, so simulation and imaging share one forward model, and through casa-imaging-runtime's worker teams, Metal backends and budget (HostResources, ResourcePolicy): the simulator builds no second budget or worker model. Total power is image-plane sampling of the model convolved with the primary beam, in casa-imaging-singledish.

docs.title: Random numbers
docs.text: A counter-based generator keys each draw by seed, row, channel, correlation and real/imaginary part, so noise is bitwise identical for any worker count, chunking or backend. It is not CASA's MLCG stream.

docs.title: CASA quirks
docs.text: CASA quirks that shape outputs users compare are matched (default limits, SIGMA and WEIGHT left at their geometric values after corrupt, noise scaling, fBM normalization, scan numbering, autocorrelation defaults). casa-rs diverges only for crashes, undefined behaviour or data corruption, such as setmosaicfield's integer division; every divergence is recorded in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md.

docs.title: 5. Performance and I/O targets
docs.text:
Each benchmark is timed for CASA, the old simulator, and casa-rs on CPU and on Metal. CASA's time is measured in-process, per call, excluding Python start-up.

Mode Target Analytic and component-list prediction No slower than July's record (#257) on the same case; the CASA multiple measured on a case where CASA runs ≥ 60 s. Image-model prediction, CPU ≥ 10× CASA on the same input, with W1 user CPU reported. Image-model prediction, Metal I/O-bound: meets the I/O target below; the CASA multiple reported. I/O-bound passes (geometry only, noise only, write only) Judged against the device's ceiling, not against CASA.

No-regression rule. On every case, the new simulator is no slower than the old one, within 5%; a trade-off needs owner approval.

I/O target. The sustained MAIN-table rate (bytes on disk over the wall time from the first row to publication, including the final sync), on a dataset at least twice the size of RAM with the page cache purged, is at least 70% of the same volume's raw sequential-write ceiling for the write-only case and at least 50% end to end with Metal prediction (tools/simulation/bench_sustained_io.py). Phase 1 met both on the external NVMe drive (owner decision, 2026-10-22, #855). The 1 GiB internal-disk case stays as a quick, cache-resident check.

Benchmark cases. ALMA (about 43 antennas, 1 h of 10 s integrations, 256 channels, a 1024² image model); VLA of similar size; one MFS model plane degridded at 256 frequencies; analytic and component-list models; write only.

docs.title: 6. Phases
docs.text: Phases 1 to 5 are on #841. What remains:

docs.title: Phase 6: simanalyze and simalma
docs.text:
Scope (planned 2026-10-27; the split is on #841). - Both tasks, ported to Rust (ADR-0017) from CASA 6.7.6's installed task_simanalyze.py and task_simalma.py, with the simutil and sdbeamutil parts they use: imtclean, convimage, statim, cellsize, ismstp, primaryBeamArcsec and TheoreticalBeam. - simanalyze: finds the project's MeasurementSets and sky model; grids total power with tsdimaging; concatenates several interferometric MeasurementSets and images them through the imager, with tclean's arguments as imtclean builds them; feathers; and analyses the convolved model, the difference, the fidelity and the statistics. - simalma: runs simobserve, simanalyze, concat and feather. Its own logic chooses the configurations and allocates the time; it lays out the total-power pointings, scales the total power, and makes the primary-beam-weighted feather. - The Python surfaces mimic CASA's exactly from the start (#931).

Owner decisions (2026-10-27). - The single-dish gridder is in its own library crate, casa-imaging-singledish (#938), which holds the kernels, the image-plane gridder and simobserve's total-power predictor (the gridder's adjoint). Single-dish image-plane gridding is its own operator family, outside ADR-0016's four interferometric kernel sets. - tsdimaging and concat read and write through casa-observation (#937, #938, #939), not through casa-ms's older access paths.

Decided in planning. Each part records these in docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md when it implements them. - Total-power intensity scaling: each task keeps its own formula, which differ by 8.7%. A part departs from one only if it measures that formula to be physically wrong. - simalma's TypeError for configuration names without "cycleN" (task_simalma.py:523) is fixed. - The user's modelimage is not changed in place; CASA's master branch has removed those lines. - No .tclean.last is written (#931: no Last profiles from Python). - Products do not depend on graphics. In CASA, simalma's combine figure deletes simanalyze's flat images. - Sky-model discovery takes candidates in sorted order, not in glob order. - Acceptance avoids simanalyze's feather of total power with interferometer data, which is not primary-beam weighted. CASA skips its own test of that path because feather fails. The simanalyze part decides it by the better-physics rule; simalma's weighted feather is the candidate.

Parts, one PR each. 6a (image analysis in casa-images), 6b (imager startmodel, uvtaper, non-square imsize, optimum size), 6c (the casa-imaging-singledish core) and 6f (simanalyze's analysis) are merged.

Part Content Waits for 6d tsdimaging on casa-observation (#938 part 2) #931 2a and 3 6e concat core on casa-observation (#939) #931 2a and 3 6g simanalyze: discovery, imaging, total power, concat, feather; its host and Python surface 6d, 6e, #931 3 6h simalma 6g 6i Graphics for both, on 5e's plot document 5e (#1025)

Acceptance. - regression/sim_multi_arrays_and_TP. It runs simobserve for 12 m, 7 m and total power, then simanalyze twice. - The oracle is CASA 6.7.6-14's products, regenerated by a committed recipe. The references in the test data are from an older CASA: 6.7.6-14 differs from them by 4–7% NRMS in DATA. - Compared by NRMS: the MeasurementSets (DATA within 1e-6, as in Phase 5), the total-power image, and the images and difference images. - regression/simalma_12m_ACA_combination. CASA's test checks only that 14 PNGs and 5 MeasurementSets exist. Acceptance instead compares every product with CASA 6.7.6-14's: the MeasurementSets, the concatenation included; the total-power image, each configuration's image and the concatenation's; the feathered image, the differences and the fidelities. The PNGs come after 6i. - Timing rows for both cases, against CASA. The multi-array case takes about 30 s in CASA 6.7.6-14 on the Mac mini.

docs.title: Phase 7: retire the old code
docs.text:
Scope. - Delete simulation.rs, simulation_task.rs and casa-simulation-synthesis, shrinking the file-length allowlist. - Move the imaging T1 fixtures and the perf benches to the new API. - Update the capability matrix and the docs.

Acceptance. No caller of the old API remains, and just quick is green.

docs.title: CASA Tutorial Parity
docs.text:
Truth class: current descriptive Last reality check: 2026-11-02 Verification: just docs-check

The CASA Guide "First Look" tutorials are checked section by section by the declarative runner in scripts/tutorial_parity. Its twelve version-1 section manifests (scripts/tutorial_parity/sections/) cover First Look at Image Analysis (imhead, imstat, immoments, exportfits) and First Look at Imaging (from listobs and the uv-coverage plots through cleaning and primary-beam correction). Each section runs on three surfaces, CASA, the command line and Python, and compares their products.

docs.title: Runtime contract
docs.text:
• CASA_RS_TUTORIAL_DATA_ROOT is the only tutorial-data root; it holds the pack paths the manifests declare.
  • CASA_RS_CASA_PYTHON selects the optional CASA oracle interpreter.
  • Native Python is found by scripts/resolve-python.sh and counts only when it can import the installed casars._core extension.
  • Task and parameter names are allowlisted by the schema. Workers accept only JSON requests produced from validated manifests, never Python or shell fragments.
  • A missing CASA, native Python, network or dataset is recorded as typed unavailable evidence, never as a success or a fallback to another surface.
  • Plot sections compare text point manifests; casa-rs does not render PNG plots.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Validate the manifests and list the sections, without external resources:

python3 scripts/tutorial_parity/runner.py validate --all
python3 scripts/tutorial_parity/runner.py run --dry-run --all

Run one section (omit --surface for all three):

python3 scripts/tutorial_parity/runner.py run \
  --section alma-first-look-image-analysis:01-imhead-continuum-header \
  --surface casa --surface cli --surface python

Evidence, review records and the section's Markdown and HTML documentation are written atomically under the pack paths the manifest declares. The runner's tests run with scripts/test-perf-tools.sh.

docs.title: VLA adaptive-scale examples
docs.text: The G55 standard-gridder and W-projection deconvolver='asp' commands are experimental CASA references. Native tclean rejects them before imaging with deconvolver="asp" is not implemented by casa-rs yet (#223). The refusal applies to the tutorial's fusedthreshold and largestscale combinations, including the requests that save model visibilities. VLA guide, revision 36701 · CASA 6.7.6 release notes

docs.text:

docs.title: ALMA protoplanetary disk tutorial
docs.text:
Truth class: current descriptive Last reality check: 2026-11-15 Verification: just docs-check

This is the simulation/ppdisk-alma-former outcome, work issue #180. It implements the single-interferometric-MS simanalyze route needed by the disk tutorial. Multi-array, total-power and simalma integration remain on #841.

docs.title: Source and sequence
docs.text:
The source is CASA Guide revision 41893, labelled CASA 6.6.6. Its four illustrations retain CASA 5.4 filenames. The current project oracle is CASA 6.7.6.14, superseding the old ticket's 6.7.5-9 baseline. Historical illustrations are shown for human comparison; the numerical reference comes from the installed current CASA.

The public input is ppdisk672_GHz_50pc.fits, the Wolf & D'Angelo (2005) disk model. Cite that paper for scientific use. The unmodified 270 KiB FITS is a small import regression fixture; full MS, images, renderer arrays and transient runs stay outside default gates. The antenna input is CASA's public alma/simmos/alma.out20.cfg, supplied explicitly to both engines from the same runtime-data installation.

The Guide sequence is imhead; ia.open/shape/toworld/close and qa.formxxx to inspect the centre; simobserve; simanalyze. The observation uses J2000 18h00m00.031s -22d59m59.6s, a 0.76 arcsec map, 1200 seconds, ALMA out20 and no thermal noise. Imaging uses 192×192 pixels, natural weighting, 10,000 Clark iterations, threshold 1e-7Jy, the input model as start model, and residual/convolved-model analysis panels.

docs.title: Explicit differences and classified steps
docs.text:
Step Classification and impact CASA's interactive default/inp/go shell External shell convenience. Both Python routes pass the same explicit task arguments and canonical defaults. Header inspection Both routes call their native imhead on the original FITS. Native FITS import now follows casacore's legacy FREQ-LSR, uppercase HZ, RESTFREQ and FITS brightness-unit aliases. ia.open/shape/toworld/close introspection The public native image-tool methods remain deferred on #1027: expose FITS/image shape and world-coordinate conversion through that tool. This does not gate simulation: its existing Rust coordinate library computes the same model centre during task preparation. The independent CASA centre is 18:00:00.03100 -022.59.59.602830; the Guide supplies the observing direction explicitly. FITS start model Literal Guide simanalyze(modelimage='...fits') fails in CASA 6.7.6.14 with “Model image … is not a readable Table”. Both controlled routes use their own lossless importfits first. Native execution never invokes CASA. Stored observation time Use the existing approved simobserve_parity.casars_params UTC/TAI comparison rule: native hourangle='35s' gives exactly the same stored TIME for the Guide's 2014 default date. Production defaults are unchanged. Screen display External interactive display. Both evidence runs use headless graphics='file', preserving every tutorial PNG and panel selection. The shared renderer also handles screen/both. Fidelity Preserve CASA's original result, plus an independent CASA control changing only its %f floor to full precision. Native fidelity follows the existing documented corrections: full-precision floor and dimensionless ratio. Seven selected analysis panels CASA warns about six axes, then draws fidelity over difference in the sixth panel. The native document retains both complete layers and their colour scales in that panel. .tclean.last Not produced: the programme's existing task-parameter policy does not save implicit last files. Numerical products are independent of graphics. Failed rerun / selected input overlap Native preparation preserves prior products and refuses input/output collisions, correcting CASA's deletion before preparation succeeds; recorded in the CASA bugs document.

All four workflow figures are reproduced. No Guide output table is present. The input's scientific interpretation, image/MS persistence and dependency set are unchanged. No new crate family or major algorithm is introduced. simanalyze adds a native application/catalog entry and its CASA parameters, reusing the simulation result and plot wire shapes. Its automatic zero/empty geometry has separate semantic concepts from explicit positive tclean geometry. Nondefault interactive cleaning, multi-MS, total power, feather integration and custom logging remain explicit refusals with owning issues.

docs.title: Numerical and figure evidence
docs.text:
The machine-readable comparison records all 15 image products, masks/units/coordinates/beams, the full 147,000-row MS, and the four figures' actual artists. Numerical acceptance is normalized RMS ≤0.001. The figure check compares every plotted sample/pixel, panel count, selection, axes, labels, units, display limits, markers, colours, statistics annotations and font sizes. Numerical limits use the same relative scientific tolerance; raster subtraction is not an acceptance gate. WCS references, increments and reference pixels are checked axis by axis, with frame identifiers and projection; negative controls reject angular errors even when a much larger spectral value is unchanged. Original CASA fidelity is reported separately from its corrected control.

Each row below places the original Guide illustration, current CASA and native output side by side. The Guide and current CASA can differ because of their versions; the current paired run is the scientific comparison.

Guide figure Guide / CASA 6.7.6.14 / casa-rs psim2-5.4.alma.out20.skymodel.png psim2-5.4.alma.out20.observe.png psim2-5.4.alma.out20.image.png psim2-5.4.alma.out20.analysis.png

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
Use separate output directories and the same model/configuration files. NATIVEPY imports the installed casa-rs Python extension and its plot extras; CASAPY is CASA 6.7.6.14's Python. Set the ordinary task binary overrides (or suite root) to the release build. A valid measures runtime is required.

python tools/simulation/ppdisk_tutorial.py --engine download --out target/ppdisk-inputs
cargo build --release -p casars-simulation --bins -p casa-images --bins -p casars-imexplore --bin imexplore
CASAPY tools/simulation/ppdisk_tutorial.py --engine casa \
  --out target/ppdisk/casa --model target/ppdisk-inputs/ppdisk672_GHz_50pc.fits \
  --config /path/to/alma/simmos/alma.out20.cfg --repeats 3
NATIVEPY tools/simulation/ppdisk_tutorial.py --engine native \
  --out target/ppdisk/native --model target/ppdisk-inputs/ppdisk672_GHz_50pc.fits \
  --config /path/to/alma/simmos/alma.out20.cfg --repeats 3
CASAPY tools/simulation/compare_ppdisk_tutorial.py \
  --casa target/ppdisk/casa --native target/ppdisk/native \
  --guides target/ppdisk-inputs/guide-figures --out target/ppdisk/review

The default end-to-end regression uses the same small eight-antenna inputs as the existing graphics oracle and compares 13 products from an actual CASA run, including the documented full-precision fidelity control:

cargo test -p casa-images --test legacy_simulation_fits
cargo test -p casa-simulation --test simanalyze_task_casa
python crates/casars-python/python/tests/test_ppdisk_tutorial.py

docs.title: Timing
docs.text:
The retained timing record accompanies the numerical comparison. It uses release native binaries, the same host and inputs, serial runs without concurrent compilation, and includes import, task-process startup, all scientific outputs and file rendering. These small end-to-end timings are not representative imaging benchmarks.

Timing samples, median of three runs:

Engine Import Simulate + figures Image/analyze + figures Total CASA 6.7.6.14 0.019 s 2.385 s 7.774 s 10.182 s casa-rs release 0.013 s 3.227 s 3.340 s 6.587 s

Native total time is 1.55× faster on this case. Both runs include evidence artist capture; source/runtime imports and initial header inspection precede the timed task sequence.
